payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Apple's FY2025 total net sales rose 6.4% to $416.2B with net income of $112.0B and diluted EPS of $7.46, as Services net sales grew 13.5% to $109.2B.

Revenue growth accelerated to 6.4% from 2.0% in the prior year, and net income rose 19.5% versus a 3.4% decline in FY2024, which had included a one-time $10.2B State Aid income tax charge.

- Total net sales increased 6.4% YoY to $416.2B, with Services up 13.5% to $109.2B and iPhone up 4.2% to $209.6B.
- Net income rose 19.5% to $112.0B and diluted EPS rose 22.7% to $7.46, aided by a lower effective tax rate of 15.6% versus 24.1% a year earlier.
- Greater China net sales declined 3.8% to $64.4B, the only reportable segment to decrease, which management attributes primarily to lower iPhone net sales.
- Operating cash flow was $111.5B, down from $118.3B, while capital expenditures rose to $12.7B from $9.4B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net sales | $416,161M | $391,035M | +6.4% | Management attributes the increase to higher net sales of iPhone and Services, partially offset by lower net sales of Wearables, Home and Accessories. |
| Products net sales | $307,003M | $294,866M | +4.1% | Products net sales increased, with iPhone up 4.2% to $209.6B and Mac up 12.4% to $33.7B, partially offset by a 3.6% decline in Wearables, Home and Accessories to $35.7B. |
| Services net sales | $109,158M | $96,169M | +13.5% | Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales from advertising, the App Store and cloud services. |
| Gross margin | $195,201M | $180,683M | +8.0% | Products gross margin percentage decreased to 36.8% on a different mix of products and tariff costs, while Services gross margin percentage increased to 75.4% on a different mix of services. |
| Operating income | $133,050M | $123,216M | +8.0% | Operating income rose as total operating expenses grew 8.1% to $62.2B, driven by increases in headcount-related expenses and infrastructure-related costs. |
| Net income | $112,010M | $93,736M | +19.5% | Net income rose as the provision for income taxes decreased to $20.7B from $29.7B, reflecting a $10.7B year-over-year decrease related to the State Aid Decision. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $7.46 | $6.08 | +22.7% | Diluted EPS grew faster than net income as weighted-average diluted shares declined to 15,004,697 thousand from 15,408,095 thousand. |
| Basic earnings per share | $7.49 | $6.11 | +22.6% | Basic EPS increased on higher net income and a lower weighted-average basic share count of 14,948,500 thousand. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

FY2025 results contain no comparable one-time tax charge; the prior-year provision for income taxes included a $10.2B net one-time charge related to the European Commission State Aid Decision, which raised the FY2024 effective tax rate to 24.1%. FY2025 also includes a $2.1B change in valuation allowance and a $486M favorable impact from the State Aid Decision in the tax reconciliation.

Operating cash flow was 1.0x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $98.8B.

**Red flag:** Accounts receivable, net increased 19.1% to $39.8B, outpacing the 6.4% increase in total net sales.

**Red flag:** Cash paid for income taxes, net rose to $43.4B from $26.1B, contributing to the decline in operating cash flow to $111.5B from $118.3B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $15.4B (prior $15.2B), share repurchases $90.7B (prior $94.9B); capital expenditures $12.7B (prior $9.4B).

Capital return remained funded by operating cash flow and supplemented by debt issuance; the company repurchased $89.3B of common stock and paid $15.4B of dividends and dividend equivalents during 2025, while also issuing $4.5B of new fixed-rate notes and repaying $10.9B of term debt. Management states it believes existing cash, marketable securities, ongoing operating cash generation and continued access to debt markets will satisfy cash requirements and the capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond.

Return on equity was 151.9% (prior 164.6%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 31.2% (prior 25.7%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In May 2025, the Company announced a new share repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26 per share beginning in May 2025.

## Forward Signals

No quantitative financial guidance is provided in the 10-K. Management states it believes its balances of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, which totaled $132.4 billion as of September 27, 2025, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond.

**Known trends**
- The Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure.
- Tariffs and other measures applied to the Company's products or components can have a material adverse impact on the Company's business, results of operations and financial condition, including impacting the Company's supply chain, the availability of rare earths and other raw materials and components, pricing and gross margin.
- The Company believes it is reasonably possible that its gross unrecognized tax benefits could decrease as much as $6 billion in the next 12 months.

**Subsequent events**
- Not disclosed—no material subsequent events are described in the provided filing text.

> "As a result, the Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure." — Apple Inc. (MD&A, Gross Margin)

> "The Company believes its balances of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, which totaled $132.4 billion as of September 27, 2025, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond." — Apple Inc. (MD&A, Liquidity and Capital Resources)

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | New U.S. tariffs announced beginning in the second quarter of 2025, including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the EU, with reciprocal measures threatened, could increase costs or limit availability of products and components. | Beginning in the second quarter of 2025, new tariffs were announced on imports to the U.S. ("U.S. Tariffs"), including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the European Union ("EU"), among others. |
| 2 | A significant majority of manufacturing is performed by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, and the Company relies on single-source partners for many components, reducing direct control over production and distribution. | A significant majority of the Company's manufacturing is performed in whole or in part by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, in addition to sourcing from partners and facilities located in the U.S. |
| 3 | The Company is subject to various claims, legal proceedings and government investigations, including a significant number of patent claims relating to standards-enabled products, where plaintiffs frequently seek broad injunctive relief and substantial damages. | The Company has faced and continues to face a significant number of patent claims relating to its standards-enabled products, and new claims may arise in the future, including as a result of new legal or regulatory frameworks. |
| 4 | The Company's products and services face substantial competition, including competitors that have aggressively cut prices and lowered product margins, and the Company holds a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets. | The Company has a minority market share in the global smartphone, personal computer, tablet and wearables markets, and some of the markets in which the Company competes have from time to time experienced little to no growth or contracted overall. |
| 5 | The Company is exposed to write-downs on inventory and other assets and purchase commitment cancellation risk, with manufacturing purchase obligations covering forecasted requirements typically for periods up to 150 days. | Manufacturing purchase obligations cover the Company's forecasted component and manufacturing requirements, typically for periods up to 150 days. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Americas | $178.4B | $72.5B | +6.8% | 41% operating margin — Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales of iPhone and Services, with weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar having an unfavorable year-over-year impact. |
| Europe | $111.0B | $47.7B | +9.6% | 43% operating margin — Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales of Services, iPhone and Mac. |
| Greater China | $64.4B | $26.9B | -3.8% | 42% operating margin — Management attributes the decrease primarily to lower net sales of iPhone, partially offset by higher net sales of Mac. |
| Rest of Asia Pacific | $33.7B | $14.6B | +9.9% | 43% operating margin — Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and Mac. |
| Japan | $28.7B | $14.0B | +14.6% | 49% operating margin — Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and iPad. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total term debt was $90.7B ($12.4B current, $78.3B non-current) plus $8.0B of commercial paper, against $35.9B of cash and cash equivalents and $96.5B of current and non-current marketable securities; total shareholders' equity was $73.7B, up from $57.0B.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $132.4B as of September 27, 2025; management states these balances, ongoing operating cash generation and continued access to debt markets will satisfy cash requirements and the capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $111.5B, investing $15.2B, financing $-120.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $148.0B vs. current liabilities $165.6B (current ratio 0.89x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-09-28: $153.0B vs. $176.4B (0.87x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Term debt principal of $91.3B with $12.4B payable within 12 months; future principal payments include $12.4B in 2026, $10.1B in 2027, $9.3B in 2028, $5.2B in 2029, $5.0B in 2030 and $49.3B thereafter.
- Future interest payments associated with the Notes total $37.0B, with $2.6B payable within 12 months.
- The deemed repatriation tax payable imposed by the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 was $8.8B, payable within 12 months.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| European Commission State Aid Decision | During the fourth quarter of 2024 the Company recorded a one-time income tax charge of $10.2B, net, representing $15.8B payable to Ireland via release of amounts held in escrow, partially offset by a U.S. foreign tax credit of $4.8B and an $823M decrease in unrecognized tax benefits; the FY2025 effective tax rate of 15.6% reflects a $10.7B year-over-year decrease in the provision related to this matter. |
| Uncertain tax positions | Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $23.2B as of September 27, 2025, of which $10.6B, if recognized, would impact the effective tax rate; the Company believes it is reasonably possible gross unrecognized tax benefits could decrease as much as $6B in the next 12 months. |
| Supply concentration | As of September 27, 2025, two vendors individually represented 10% or more of total vendor non-trade receivables, accounting for 46% and 23%, and one customer represented 12% of total trade receivables. |
| Segment reporting adoption | Beginning with the 2025 annual reporting period, the Company adopted ASU 2023-07 using a retrospective transition method, requiring disclosure of significant segment expenses provided to the CODM and the CODM's title and position. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Apple's FY2025 total net sales rose 6.4% to $416.2B and net income rose 19.5% to $112.0B, with diluted EPS of $7.46.

FY2025 revenue growth accelerated to 6.4% from 2.0% in FY2024, with Services and iPhone leading and Greater China declining for a second year.

- Total net sales $416.2B (+6.4% YoY) and net income $112.0B (+19.5% YoY); diluted EPS $7.46 vs $6.08.
- Services net sales $109.2B (+13.5% YoY) and iPhone net sales $209.6B (+4.2% YoY) drove the increase; Greater China net sales declined 3.8% YoY.
- Effective tax rate fell to 15.6% from 24.1%, which the filing attributes to a $10.7B year-over-year decrease in the provision related to the State Aid Decision and changes in unrecognized tax benefits.
- Cash generated by operating activities was $111.5B, down from $118.3B, while repurchases of common stock were $90.7B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net sales | $416,161M | $391,035M | +6.4% | Management attributes the increase to higher net sales of iPhone and Services across most segments, partially offset by lower Greater China iPhone net sales. |
| Products net sales | $307,003M | $294,866M | +4.1% | Products net sales rose on higher iPhone, Mac and iPad net sales, partially offset by lower Wearables, Home and Accessories net sales. |
| Services net sales | $109,158M | $96,169M | +13.5% | Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales from advertising, the App Store and cloud services. |
| Gross margin | $195,201M | $180,683M | +8.0% | Products gross margin increased on favorable costs and a different mix of products, partially offset by tariff costs; Services gross margin increased on higher Services net sales and a different mix of services. |
| Operating income | $133,050M | $123,216M | +8.0% | Operating income rose as gross margin growth outpaced an 8% increase in total operating expenses. |
| Provision for income taxes | $20,719M | $29,749M | −30.4% | Management attributes the decrease to a $10.7B year-over-year decrease in the provision related to the State Aid Decision and the impact of changes in unrecognized tax benefits, partially offset by a change in valuation allowance and a higher effective tax rate on foreign earnings. |
| Net income | $112,010M | $93,736M | +19.5% | Net income grew faster than operating income primarily because of the lower provision for income taxes. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $7.46 | $6.08 | +22.7% | Diluted EPS grew faster than net income as the weighted-average diluted share count declined to 15,004,697 thousand from 15,408,095 thousand. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

FY2024 net income included a one-time income tax charge of $10.2B, net, related to the European Commission State Aid Decision; FY2025's lower provision reflects the absence of that charge, with the FY2025 effective tax rate of 15.6% versus 24.1% in FY2024. FY2025 also included a $2,091M change in valuation allowance and a $486M favorable impact from the State Aid Decision line in the tax reconciliation.

Operating cash flow was 1.0x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $98.8B.

**Red flag:** Accounts receivable, net rose to $39,777M from $33,410M, a 19.1% increase, outpacing the 6.4% increase in total net sales.

**Red flag:** Cash paid for income taxes, net rose to $43,369M from $26,102M, reflecting the State Aid Decision settlement.

**Red flag:** Gross unrecognized tax benefits rose to $23,242M from $22,038M, of which $10.6B, if recognized, would impact the effective tax rate.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $15.4B (prior $15.2B), share repurchases $90.7B (prior $94.9B); capital expenditures $12.7B (prior $9.4B).

Capital return remained funded by operating cash flow, with repurchases and dividends exceeding operating cash flow and contributing to a $120.7B financing cash outflow; the company also issued $4.5B of new fixed-rate notes in 2025 and repaid $10.9B of term debt. The filing states the company believes its cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities balances, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond.

Return on equity was 151.9% (prior 164.6%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 31.2% (prior 25.7%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In May 2025, the Company announced a new share repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26 per share beginning in May 2025.
- During 2025, the Company repurchased 402 million shares of its common stock for $89.3 billion.

## Forward Signals

No forward financial guidance is provided in the 10-K; the filing states that future gross margins can be impacted by a variety of factors and that the Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure.

**Known trends**
- Tariffs and other measures: new U.S. Tariffs were announced beginning in the second quarter of 2025, including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the EU, and the ultimate impact remains uncertain.
- The Company's effective tax rate for 2025 was lower than the statutory federal income tax rate primarily due to a lower effective tax rate on foreign earnings, including the impact of changes in unrecognized tax benefits.
- The Company believes it is reasonably possible that its gross unrecognized tax benefits could decrease as much as $6 billion in the next 12 months.

**Subsequent events**
- Not disclosed—no material subsequent events are described in the provided excerpts.

> "The Company believes its balances of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, which totaled $132.4 billion as of September 27, 2025, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond." — Apple Inc. (Item 7. MD&A)

> "As a result, the Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure." — Apple Inc. (Item 7. MD&A)

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tariffs and other trade measures announced beginning in the second quarter of 2025, including additional U.S. Tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the EU, can increase costs or limit availability of products, components and rare earths and affect pricing and gross margin. | Tariffs and other measures that are applied to the Company's products or their components can have a material adverse impact on the Company's business, results of operations and financial condition, including impacting the Company's supply chain, the availability of rare earths and other raw materials and components, pricing and gross margin. |
| 2 | A significant majority of manufacturing is performed by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, and the Company relies on single-source partners for many components, reducing direct control over production and distribution. | The Company relies on single-source partners in the U.S., Asia and Europe to supply and manufacture many components, and on partners primarily located in Asia, for final assembly of substantially all of the Company's hardware products. |
| 3 | The Company is subject to various claims, legal proceedings and government investigations, including a significant number of patent claims relating to standards-enabled products, where plaintiffs frequently seek broad injunctive relief and substantial damages. | The Company has faced and continues to face a significant number of patent claims relating to its standards-enabled products, and new claims may arise in the future, including as a result of new legal or regulatory frameworks. |
| 4 | The Company's global operations are subject to complex and changing laws and regulations worldwide, including antitrust, privacy, data security and data localization, online safety, age verification and consumer protection. | The Company's global operations are subject to complex and changing laws and regulations worldwide on subjects including antitrust; privacy, data security and data localization; online safety; age verification; consumer protection; advertising, sales, billing and e-commerce; financial services and technology; product liability; intellectual propert |
| 5 | The Company is exposed to write-downs on inventory and other assets and purchase commitment cancellation risk given the rapid pace of product obsolescence, with manufacturing purchase obligations covering forecasted requirements typically for periods up to 150 days. | Manufacturing purchase obligations cover the Company's forecasted component and manufacturing requirements, typically for periods up to 150 days. |

| Americas | $178.4B | $72.5B | +6.8% | 41% operating margin — Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales of iPhone and Services, with weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar having an unfavorable year-over-year impact. |
| Europe | $111.0B | $47.7B | +9.6% | 43% operating margin — Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales of Services, iPhone and Mac. |
| Greater China | $64.4B | $26.9B | -3.8% | 42% operating margin — Management attributes the decrease primarily to lower net sales of iPhone, partially offset by higher net sales of Mac. |
| Rest of Asia Pacific | $33.7B | $14.6B | +9.9% | 43% operating margin — Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and Mac. |
| Japan | $28.7B | $14.0B | +14.6% | 49% operating margin — Management attributes the increase primarily to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and iPad. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total term debt was $90,678M ($12,350M current and $78,328M non-current) plus $7,979M of commercial paper, against $35,934M of cash and cash equivalents and $96,486M of current and non-current marketable securities; total shareholders' equity was $73,733M.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $132.4B as of September 27, 2025; the Company states these balances, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $111.5B, investing $15.2B, financing $-120.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $148.0B vs. current liabilities $165.6B (current ratio 0.89x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-09-28: $153.0B vs. $176.4B (0.87x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- As of September 27, 2025, the Company had outstanding fixed-rate notes with an aggregate principal amount of $91.3 billion, with $12.4 billion payable within 12 months.
- The Company had $8.0 billion of commercial paper outstanding, which was payable within 12 months, with a weighted-average interest rate of 4.19%.
- The balance of the deemed repatriation tax payable imposed by the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 was $8.8 billion, which was payable within 12 months.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Apple's FY2025 total net sales rose 6.4% to $416.2B with net income of $112.0B and diluted EPS of $7.46, as Services net sales grew 14% to $109.2B.

FY2025 revenue growth accelerated to 6% from 2% in FY2024, with Services and iPhone driving the increase and Greater China declining for a second consecutive year.

- Total net sales increased 6.4% YoY to $416.2B, with Services up 14% to $109.2B and iPhone up 4% to $209.6B.
- Net income rose 19.5% to $112.0B and diluted EPS rose 22.7% to $7.46, aided by a lower effective tax rate of 15.6% versus 24.1%.
- Greater China net sales declined 4% to $64.4B, the only reportable segment to decrease, on lower iPhone net sales.
- Cash generated by operating activities was $111.5B, down from $118.3B, while capital expenditures rose to $12.7B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net sales | $416.2B | $391.0B | +6.5% | Growth driven by higher net sales of iPhone and Services across most segments, partially offset by a decline in Greater China. |
| Products net sales | $307.0B | $294.9B | +4.1% | iPhone net sales increased due to higher net sales of Pro models; Mac increased on higher laptop and desktop sales. |
| Services net sales | $109.2B | $96.2B | +13.5% | Increase primarily due to higher net sales from advertising, the App Store and cloud services. |
| Gross margin | $195.2B | $180.7B | +8.0% | Products gross margin increased on favorable costs and a different mix of products, partially offset by tariff costs; Services gross margin increased on higher net sales and a different mix of services. |
| Operating income | $133.1B | $123.2B | +8.0% | Operating expenses grew 8% on higher R&D and SG&A, including headcount-related expenses and infrastructure-related costs. |
| Net income | $112.0B | $93.7B | +19.5% | Net income growth exceeded operating income growth due to a lower effective tax rate, which reflected a $10.7 billion year-over-year decrease in the provision related to the State Aid Decision. |
| Diluted EPS | $7.46 | $6.08 | +22.7% | Diluted EPS growth exceeded net income growth as weighted-average diluted shares declined to 15,004,697 thousand from 15,408,095 thousand. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

FY2024 net income included a one-time income tax charge of $10.2 billion, net, related to the European Commission State Aid Decision; FY2025 included a $486 million tax benefit from the State Aid Decision. Excluding these items, the year-over-year change in the provision for income taxes was a decrease of $10.7 billion. No other material one-time items were disclosed.

Operating cash flow was 1.0x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $98.8B.

**Red flag:** Accounts receivable, net increased 19.1% to $39.8B while total net sales increased 6.4%, and the cash flow statement shows accounts receivable use of $6.7B versus $3.8B in the prior year.

**Red flag:** Cash generated by operating activities declined 5.7% to $111.5B while net income rose 19.5%, with other current and non-current liabilities using $11.1B of cash versus $15.6B provided in the prior year.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $15.4B (prior $15.2B), share repurchases $90.7B (prior $94.9B); capital expenditures $12.7B (prior $9.4B).

Capital return remained the primary use of cash, with share repurchases and dividends exceeding operating cash flow and funded partly by a $4.5 billion term debt issuance and a reduction in marketable securities. In May 2025 the Company announced a new share repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26 per share.

Return on equity was 151.9% (prior 164.6%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 31.2% (prior 25.7%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In May 2025, the Company announced a new share repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26 per share beginning in May 2025.

## Forward Signals

No forward-looking financial guidance was provided in the filing. Management stated it believes its balances of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond.

**Known trends**
- Tariffs and other measures: Beginning in the second quarter of 2025, new U.S. Tariffs were announced, including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the EU, among others, and the ultimate impact remains uncertain.
- The Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure.
- The Company intends to increase its dividend on an annual basis, subject to declaration by the Board.

**Subsequent events**
- Not disclosed—no material subsequent events were identified in the provided excerpts.

> "The Company believes its balances of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, which totaled $132.4 billion as of September 27, 2025, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond." — Apple Inc. (MD&A)

> "As a result, the Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure." — Apple Inc. (MD&A)

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tariffs and other trade measures announced beginning in the second quarter of 2025, including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the EU, could materially adversely affect the Company's supply chain, component availability, pricing and gross margin. | Tariffs and other measures that are applied to the Company's products or their components can have a material adverse impact on the Company's business, results of operations and financial condition, including impacting the Company's supply chain, the availability of rare earths and other raw materials and components, pricing and gross margin. |
| 2 | The Company relies on single or limited sources for certain components, and substantially all hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam. | Substantially all of the Company's hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners that are located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam. |
| 3 | The Company is subject to various legal proceedings and government investigations, including a significant number of patent claims relating to standards-enabled products, with plaintiffs frequently seeking broad injunctive relief and substantial damages. | The Company has faced and continues to face a significant number of patent claims relating to its standards-enabled products, and new claims may arise in the future, including as a result of new legal or regulatory frameworks. |
| 4 | The Company's effective tax rate and financial condition could be materially impacted by resolution of uncertain tax positions; gross unrecognized tax benefits were $23.2 billion as of September 27, 2025, of which $10.6 billion, if recognized, would impact the effective tax rate. | As of September 27, 2025, the total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits was $23.2 billion, of which $10.6 billion, if recognized, would impact the Company's effective tax rate. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Americas | $178.4B | $72.5B | +6.8% | 41% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone and Services, with an unfavorable year-over-year impact from weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar. |
| Europe | $111.0B | $47.7B | +9.6% | 43% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of Services, iPhone and Mac. |
| Greater China | $64.4B | $26.9B | -3.8% | 42% operating margin — Net sales decreased primarily due to lower net sales of iPhone, partially offset by higher net sales of Mac. |
| Rest of Asia Pacific | $33.7B | $14.6B | +9.9% | 43% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and Mac. |
| Japan | $28.7B | $14.0B | +14.6% | 49% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and iPad. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total term debt was $90.7B ($12.4B current, $78.3B non-current) plus $8.0B of commercial paper, against $35.9B of cash and cash equivalents and $96.5B of current and non-current marketable securities. Total shareholders' equity was $73.7B, up from $57.0B.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $132.4B as of September 27, 2025. The Company stated this balance, along with cash generated by ongoing operations and continued access to debt markets, will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $111.5B, investing $15.2B, financing $-120.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $148.0B vs. current liabilities $165.6B (current ratio 0.89x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-09-28: $153.0B vs. $176.4B (0.87x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Term debt principal of $91.3B with $12.4B payable within 12 months; future principal payments include $12.4B in 2026, $10.1B in 2027, $9.3B in 2028, $5.2B in 2029, $5.0B in 2030 and $49.3B thereafter.
- Future interest payments associated with the Notes total $37.0B, with $2.6B payable within 12 months.
- The deemed repatriation tax payable imposed by the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 was $8.8B, payable within 12 months.

The FY2025 effective tax rate of 15.6% was lower than FY2024's 24.1% due to a $10.7 billion year-over-year decrease in the provision related to the State Aid Decision. |
| Uncertain Tax Positions | Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $23.2 billion as of September 27, 2025, up from $22.0 billion, of which $10.6 billion, if recognized, would impact the effective tax rate. The Company believes it is reasonably possible that gross unrecognized tax benefits could decrease as much as $6 billion in the next 12 months. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Microsoft's FY2025 revenue rose 15% to $281.7B with net income of $101.8B and diluted EPS of $13.64, as Intelligent Cloud revenue increased 21% driven by Azure and other cloud services revenue growth of 34%.

Segment composition was recast in August 2024 to bring the commercial components of Microsoft 365 together in Productivity and Business Processes, with prior-period segment information conformed; the recast had no impact on consolidated balance sheets, income statements, or cash flow statements.

- Revenue increased 15% to $281.7B with growth across each of the three reportable segments; net income rose 16% to $101.8B and diluted EPS rose 16% to $13.64.
- Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9B, while Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 69% driven by the impact of scaling AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure.
- Capital expenditures (additions to property and equipment) increased to $64.6B from $44.5B, and the company has committed $32.1B for construction of new buildings, building improvements, and leasehold improvements, primarily related to datacenters.
- The IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest related to intercompany transfer pricing for tax years 2004 to 2013; Microsoft states it disagrees and will vigorously contest the proposed adjustments.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenue | $281,724M | $245,122M | +14.9% | Growth across each of the three segments; Intelligent Cloud increased driven by Azure, Productivity and Business Processes increased driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, and More Personal Computing increased driven by Gaming and Search and news advertising. |
| Gross margin | $193,893M | $171,008M | +13.4% | Gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by Intelligent Cloud, offset in part by More Personal Computing; Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 69% driven by the impact of scaling AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure. |
| Operating income | $128,528M | $109,433M | +17.4% | Operating income increased with growth across each of our segments. |
| Net income | $101,832M | $88,136M | +15.5% | Not disclosed—the filing does not provide a single-line driver for net income beyond the operating income and other income (expense), net components. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $13.64 | $11.80 | +15.6% | Not disclosed—the filing does not provide a single-line driver for diluted EPS beyond net income and the weighted average diluted share count. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Other income (expense), net was $(4,901)M in FY2025 versus $(1,646)M in FY2024, with the change primarily reflecting net recognized losses on equity method investments, including OpenAI, within 'Other, net' of $(4,725)M versus $(1,319)M. Net recognized losses on investments increased primarily due to higher impairments, offset in part by higher gains on equity investments in the current period. Impairments of equity investments were $(951)M in FY2025 versus $(229)M in FY2024.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $71.6B.

**Red flag:** Accounts receivable, net increased to $69,905M from $56,924M (up 22.8%), outpacing the 15.0% increase in total revenue.

**Red flag:** Impairments of equity investments increased to $(951)M in FY2025 from $(229)M in FY2024.

**Red flag:** The IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest in Notices of Proposed Adjustment related to intercompany transfer pricing for tax years 2004 to 2013.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $24.1B (prior $21.8B), share repurchases $18.4B (prior $17.3B); capital expenditures $64.6B (prior $44.5B).

Capital allocation is weighted toward infrastructure investment: additions to property and equipment increased to $64.6B from $44.5B, and the company has committed $32.1B for construction of new buildings, building improvements, and leasehold improvements, primarily related to datacenters. Shareholder returns continued through dividends and share repurchases, and the company states it expects existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to continue to be sufficient to fund operating activities and cash commitments.

Return on equity was 29.6% (prior 32.8%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 16.5% (prior 17.2%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- As of June 30, 2025, $57.3 billion remained of the $60 billion share repurchase program.
- During fiscal years 2025 and 2024, the company repurchased 31 million shares and 32 million shares of common stock for $13.0 billion and $12.0 billion, respectively, through the share repurchase program.
- The Board of Directors declared dividends totaling $24.7 billion and $22.3 billion during fiscal years 2025 and 2024, respectively.

## Forward Signals

Not disclosed—the filing does not provide quantitative financial guidance; it states that investments in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase operating costs and may decrease operating margins.

**Known trends**
- The investments being made in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase operating costs and may decrease operating margins.
- The company continues to identify and evaluate opportunities to expand datacenter locations and increase server capacity to meet evolving customer needs, particularly given growing demand for AI services.
- If customers choose to license cloud-based versions of products and services rather than licensing transaction-based products and services, the associated revenue will shift from being recognized at the time of the transaction to being recognized over the subscription period or upon consumption.

**Subsequent events**
- The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) was enacted on July 4, 2025; the company is currently assessing it. The OBBBA provides a U.S. global intangible low-taxed income effective tax rate of 14% effective fiscal year 2027 for Microsoft, bonus depreciation for certain assets placed into service after January 19, 2025, and an election to expense U.S. incurred research or experimental expenditures.

> "The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins." — Microsoft Corporation

> "We disagree with the proposed adjustments and will vigorously contest the NOPAs through the IRS’s administrative appeals office and, if necessary, judicial proceedings." — Microsoft Corporation

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The company remains under IRS audit and received Notices of Proposed Adjustment seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest related to intercompany transfer pricing for tax years 2004 to 2013. | In the NOPAs, the IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest. |
| 2 | A nation-state associated threat actor compromised a legacy test account beginning in late November 2023 and gained access to Microsoft email accounts and some source code repositories and internal systems. | beginning in late November 2023, a nation-state associated threat actor used a password spray attack to compromise a legacy test account and, in turn, gain access to Microsoft email accounts. |
| 3 | The company bears significant development and operational costs to build and support AI models, services, platforms, and infrastructure, and AI technology and services are a highly competitive and rapidly evolving market with new competitors continuing to enter. | We will bear significant development and operational costs to build and support the AI models, services, platforms, and infrastructure necessary to meet the needs of our customers. |
| 4 | Datacenters depend on the availability of permitted and buildable land, predictable energy, networking supplies, and servers, including GPUs and other components, and there are limited suppliers for certain device and datacenter components. | Our datacenters depend on the availability of permitted and buildable land, predictable energy, networking supplies, and servers, including graphics processing units (“GPUs”) and other components. |
| 5 | The EU's AI Act may increase costs or impact the provision or operation of AI models and services in the European market, and legislative and regulatory action is emerging in AI. | the EU’s AI Act may increase costs or impact the provision or operation of our AI models and services in the European market. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Productivity and Business Processes | $120.8B | $69.8B | +13.1% | 58% operating margin — Revenue growth was driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, with Microsoft 365 Commercial seat growth of 6% driven by small and medium businesses and frontline worker offerings, as well as growth in revenue per user; Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue grew 11% driven by subscriber growth of 8% to 89.0 million and a price increase announced in January 2025. |
| Intelligent Cloud | $106.3B | $44.6B | +21.5% | 42% operating margin — Revenue growth was driven by Azure and other cloud services, which grew 34% driven by demand for the portfolio of services; Server products revenue decreased 3% driven by a decrease in transactional purchasing with continued customer shift to cloud offerings. |
| More Personal Computing | $54.6B | $14.2B | +7.5% | 26% operating margin — Revenue growth was driven by Gaming and Search and news advertising; Xbox content and services revenue increased 16% driven by the impact of the Activision Blizzard acquisition and Xbox Game Pass, while Xbox hardware revenue decreased 25% driven by lower volume of consoles sold, and Search and news advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 20% driven by higher search volume and higher revenue per search. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (short-term debt of $0 plus current portion of long-term debt of $2,999M plus long-term debt of $40,152M) was $43,151M as of June 30, 2025, versus $51,630M as of June 30, 2024; cash and cash equivalents of $30,242M plus short-term investments of $64,323M totaled $94,565M, and total stockholders' equity was $343,479M.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $94.6 billion as of June 30, 2025, versus $75.5 billion as of June 30, 2024; the company states it expects existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to continue to be sufficient to fund operating activities and cash commitments for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $136.2B, investing $-72.6B, financing $-51.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $191.1B vs. current liabilities $141.2B (current ratio 1.35x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-06-30: $159.7B vs. $125.3B (1.27x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt principal payments of $3,000M are due in fiscal year 2026, with $46,206M due thereafter; interest payments of $1,509M are due in fiscal year 2026, with $25,527M due thereafter.
- Construction commitments of $26,859M are due in fiscal year 2026, with $5,290M due thereafter.
- Purchase commitments of $103,940M are due in fiscal year 2026, with $6,013M due thereafter, primarily related to datacenters and including open purchase orders and take-or-pay contracts.
- Certain counterparty agreements for derivative instruments require the company to maintain an investment grade credit rating and minimum liquidity of $1.0 billion; as of June 30, 2025, long-term unsecured debt rating was AAA and cash investments were in excess of $1.0 billion, so no collateral was required to be posted.

| OpenAI investment | The investment in OpenAI Global, LLC is accounted for under the equity method of accounting, with total funding commitments of $13 billion; 'Other, net' in other income (expense), net primarily reflects net recognized losses on equity method investments, including OpenAI. |
| Segment reporting standard adoption | Adopted beginning with annual reporting for fiscal year 2025, resulting in incremental segment reporting disclosures, most notably disclosure of cost of revenue and operating expenses for each reportable segment. |
| Property and equipment commitments | As of June 30, 2025, the company has committed $32.1 billion for the construction of new buildings, building improvements, and leasehold improvements, primarily related to datacenters; depreciation expense was $22.0 billion, $15.2 billion, and $11.0 billion in fiscal years 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Microsoft FY2025 revenue rose 15% to $281.7B with net income of $101.8B and diluted EPS of $13.64, as Intelligent Cloud revenue increased 21% driven by Azure and other cloud services revenue growth of 34%.

Segment composition was recast in August 2024 to bring the commercial components of Microsoft 365 together in Productivity and Business Processes, with prior-period segment information conformed to the new presentation.

- Revenue increased 15% to $281.7B and net income increased 16% to $101.8B, with diluted EPS up 16% to $13.64.
- Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9B, while Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 69% driven by the impact of scaling AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure.
- Capital expenditures (additions to property and equipment) rose to $64.6B from $44.5B, and total assets increased to $619.0B from $512.2B.
- The IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest related to intercompany transfer pricing for tax years 2004 to 2013, which the company states it will vigorously contest.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $281,724M | $245,122M | +14.9% | Growth across each of our segments; Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure, Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, and More Personal Computing revenue increased driven by Gaming and Search and news advertising. |
| Gross margin | $193,893M | $171,008M | +13.4% | Gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by Intelligent Cloud, offset in part by More Personal Computing. |
| Operating income | $128,528M | $109,433M | +17.4% | Operating income increased with growth across each of our segments. |
| Net income | $101,832M | $88,136M | +15.5% | Not disclosed |
| Diluted earnings per share | $13.64 | $11.80 | +15.6% | Not disclosed |
| Basic earnings per share | $13.70 | $11.86 | +15.5% | Not disclosed |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income increased 17% to $128.5B, while other income (expense), net was a net expense of $4.9B compared with $1.6B in the prior year. The increase in net expense was driven by higher impairments on investments and higher losses on equity derivatives, as well as net recognized losses on equity method investments, including OpenAI, reflected in Other, net of $4.7B.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $71.6B.

**Red flag:** Accounts receivable increased to $69.9B from $56.9B, a 22.8% increase, outpacing the 15.0% revenue increase.

**Red flag:** Net recognized losses on investments increased to $349M from $118M, primarily due to higher impairments, offset in part by higher gains on equity investments in the current period.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $24.1B (prior $21.8B), share repurchases $18.4B (prior $17.3B); capital expenditures $64.6B (prior $44.5B).

Capital allocation was directed toward AI and cloud infrastructure, with additions to property and equipment increasing to $64.6B from $44.5B, alongside continued shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases. The company states it expects existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to continue to be sufficient to fund operating activities and cash commitments.

Return on equity was 29.6% (prior 32.8%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 16.5% (prior 17.2%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- As of June 30, 2025, $57.3 billion remained of the $60 billion share repurchase program.
- The Board of Directors declared dividends totaling $24.7 billion during fiscal year 2025, up from $22.3 billion in fiscal year 2024.

## Forward Signals

No financial guidance was provided in the filing. The company states it expects existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to continue to be sufficient to fund operating activities and cash commitments for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future.

**Known trends**
- The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins.
- If our customers choose to license cloud-based versions of our products and services rather than licensing transaction-based products and services, the associated revenue will shift from being recognized at the time of the transaction to being recognized over the subscription period or upon consumption, as applicable.

**Subsequent events**
- We are currently assessing the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) which was enacted on July 4, 2025, which provides a U.S. global intangible low-taxed income effective tax rate of 14% effective fiscal year 2027 for Microsoft.

> "The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins." — Management

> "We expect existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to continue to be sufficient to fund our operating activities and cash commitments for investing and financing activities, such as dividends, share repurchases, debt maturities, material capital expenditures, and the transition tax related to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA), for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest related to intercompany transfer pricing for tax years 2004 to 2013; the company disagrees and will vigorously contest the proposed adjustments. | In the NOPAs, the IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest. |
| 2 | A nation-state associated threat actor compromised a legacy test account and gained access to Microsoft email accounts, and used information obtained to gain unauthorized access to some source code repositories and internal systems. | beginning in late November 2023, a nation-state associated threat actor used a password spray attack to compromise a legacy test account and, in turn, gain access to Microsoft email accounts. |
| 3 | The company holds rights to OpenAI's intellectual property and has made total funding commitments of $13 billion to OpenAI Global, LLC, accounted for under the equity method, with net recognized losses on equity method investments including OpenAI reflected in Other, net. | We have an investment in OpenAI Global, LLC (OpenAI) and have made total funding commitments of $13 billion. |
| 4 | The company has committed $32.1 billion for the construction of new buildings, building improvements, and leasehold improvements, primarily related to datacenters, and total contractual obligations of $397.0 billion as of June 30, 2025. | As of June 30, 2025, we have committed $32.1 billion for the construction of new buildings, building improvements, and leasehold improvements, primarily related to datacenters. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Productivity and Business Processes | $120.8B | $69.8B | +13.1% | 58% operating margin — Revenue increased driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, with Microsoft 365 Commercial seat growth of 6% driven by small and medium businesses and frontline worker offerings, as well as growth in revenue per user; Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue grew 11% driven by subscriber growth of 8% to 89.0 million and a price increase announced in January 2025. |
| Intelligent Cloud | $106.3B | $44.6B | +21.5% | 42% operating margin — Revenue increased driven by Azure and other cloud services, which grew 34% driven by demand for our portfolio of services; Server products revenue decreased 3% driven by a decrease in transactional purchasing with continued customer shift to cloud offerings. |
| More Personal Computing | $54.6B | $14.2B | +7.5% | 26% operating margin — Revenue increased driven by Gaming and Search and news advertising; Xbox content and services revenue increased 16% driven by the impact of the Activision Blizzard acquisition and Xbox Game Pass, while Xbox hardware revenue decreased 25% driven by lower volume of consoles sold. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt was $43.2B (short-term debt of $0, current portion of long-term debt of $3.0B, and long-term debt of $40.2B) against cash and cash equivalents of $30.2B and total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of $94.6B; total stockholders' equity was $343.5B.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $94.6B as of June 30, 2025, up from $75.5B as of June 30, 2024; the company states it expects existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to continue to be sufficient to fund operating activities and cash commitments for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $136.2B, investing $-72.6B, financing $-51.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $191.1B vs. current liabilities $141.2B (current ratio 1.35x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-06-30: $159.7B vs. $125.3B (1.27x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt principal payments of $3.0B due in fiscal year 2026 and $46.2B thereafter, with total principal payments of $49.2B and interest payments of $27.0B.
- Certain counterparty agreements for derivative instruments contain provisions that require our issued and outstanding long-term unsecured debt to maintain an investment grade credit rating and require us to maintain minimum liquidity of $1.0 billion.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Activision Blizzard acquisition completed on October 13, 2023 for a total purchase price of $75.4 billion, with goodwill of $51.0 billion assigned to the More Personal Computing segment and intangible assets of $22.0 billion. | The financial results of Activision Blizzard have been included in our consolidated financial statements since the date of the acquisition and are reported as part of the More Personal Computing segment. |
| Segment composition was recast in August 2024 to bring the commercial components of Microsoft 365 together in the Productivity and Business Processes segment, with prior period segment information conformed to the new presentation. | The recast of prior period information had no impact on our consolidated balance sheets, consolidated income statements, or consolidated cash flows statements. |
| The company adopted a new segment reporting standard beginning with annual reporting for fiscal year 2025, which expanded disclosures about significant segment expenses, most notably disclosure of cost of revenue and operating expenses for each reportable segment. | The adoption resulted in incremental segment reporting disclosures, most notably disclosure of cost of revenue and operating expenses for each reportable segment. |

Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9B, while Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 69% driven by the impact of scaling AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure.
Capital expenditures (additions to property and equipment) rose to $64.6B from $44.5B, and total assets increased to $619.0B from $512.2B.

The IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest related to intercompany transfer pricing for tax years 2004 to 2013, which the company states it will vigorously contest.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Microsoft FY2025 revenue rose 15% to $281.7B with net income of $101.8B and diluted EPS of $13.64, as Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9B.

Segment composition was recast in August 2024 to bring the commercial components of Microsoft 365 together in Productivity and Business Processes, with prior-period segment information conformed to the new presentation.

- Revenue increased 15% to $281.7B, with growth across each of the three reportable segments.
- Net income rose 16% to $101.8B and diluted EPS rose 16% to $13.64.
- Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9B, led by Azure and other cloud services revenue growth of 34%.
- Capital expenditures (additions to property and equipment) increased to $64.6B from $44.5B, with $32.1B committed for construction of new buildings and improvements, primarily datacenters.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $281,724M | $245,122M | +14.9% | Growth across each of the three segments, led by Intelligent Cloud on Azure. |
| Gross margin | $193,893M | $171,008M | +13.4% | Growth across each segment; gross margin percentage decreased slightly driven by Intelligent Cloud, offset in part by More Personal Computing. |
| Operating income | $128,528M | $109,433M | +17.4% | Growth across each of the segments. |
| Net income | $101,832M | $88,136M | +15.5% | Effective tax rate of 18% in both fiscal years. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $13.64 | $11.80 | +15.6% | Diluted share count of 7,465 million versus 7,469 million. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of $128.5B was reduced by other income (expense), net of -$4.9B, which included net recognized losses on investments of -$349M, net losses on derivatives of -$260M, and 'Other, net' of -$4,725M that 'primarily reflects net recognized losses on equity method investments, including OpenAI.' Impairments of equity investments were $951M in FY2025 versus $229M in FY2024.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $71.6B.

**Red flag:** Accounts receivable increased to $69.9B from $56.9B, a 22.8% increase, outpacing the 15.0% revenue increase.

**Red flag:** Equity investment impairments rose to $951M from $229M, and 'Other, net' within other income (expense) widened to -$4,725M from -$1,319M, primarily on equity method losses including OpenAI.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $24.1B (prior $21.8B), share repurchases $18.4B (prior $17.3B); capital expenditures $64.6B (prior $44.5B).

Capital allocation was weighted toward infrastructure investment, with additions to property and equipment rising to $64.6B from $44.5B and $32.1B committed for construction of new buildings, building improvements, and leasehold improvements, primarily datacenters. Shareholder returns continued through dividends and repurchases, and the company stated it expects existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to be sufficient to fund operating activities and cash commitments.

Return on equity was 29.6% (prior 32.8%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 16.5% (prior 17.2%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- As of June 30, 2025, $57.3 billion remained of the $60 billion share repurchase program.
- During fiscal years 2025 and 2024, the Board of Directors declared dividends totaling $24.7 billion and $22.3 billion, respectively.
- On October 13, 2023, the company completed its acquisition of Activision Blizzard, Inc. for a total purchase price of $75.4 billion, consisting primarily of cash.

## Forward Signals

No forward financial guidance is provided in the filing. Management states that investments in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase operating costs and may decrease operating margins.

**Known trends**
- The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins.
- If our customers choose to license cloud-based versions of our products and services rather than licensing transaction-based products and services, the associated revenue will shift from being recognized at the time of the transaction to being recognized over the subscription period or upon consumption, as applicable.
- The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development published model rules establishing a global minimum corporate tax rate of 15% for certain multinational enterprises, which applies to Microsoft beginning in fiscal year 2025.

**Subsequent events**
- The One Big Beautiful Bill Act was enacted on July 4, 2025, providing a U.S. global intangible low-taxed income effective tax rate of 14% effective fiscal year 2027 for Microsoft, bonus depreciation for certain assets placed into service after January 19, 2025, and an election to expense U.S. incurred research or experimental expenditures.

> "The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins." — Microsoft Corporation (Item 7. MD&A)

> "We expect existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to continue to be sufficient to fund our operating activities and cash commitments for investing and financing activities, such as dividends, share repurchases, debt maturities, material capital expenditures, and the transition tax related to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act ("TCJA"), for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future." — Microsoft Corporation (Item 7. MD&A)

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The IRS issued Notices of Proposed Adjustment for tax years 2004 to 2013 seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest, primarily related to intercompany transfer pricing. | In the NOPAs, the IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of $28.9 billion plus penalties and interest. |
| 2 | A nation-state associated threat actor compromised a legacy test account beginning in late November 2023 and gained access to Microsoft email accounts and some source code repositories and internal systems. | beginning in late November 2023, a nation-state associated threat actor used a password spray attack to compromise a legacy test account and, in turn, gain access to Microsoft email accounts. |
| 3 | Datacenter expansion depends on availability of permitted and buildable land, predictable energy, networking supplies, and servers including GPUs, with limited suppliers for certain device and datacenter components. | Our datacenters depend on the availability of permitted and buildable land, predictable energy, networking supplies, and servers, including graphics processing units and other components. |
| 4 | The company holds an investment in OpenAI Global, LLC accounted for under the equity method, with total funding commitments of $13 billion, and recorded net recognized losses on equity method investments including OpenAI. | We have an investment in OpenAI Global, LLC ("OpenAI") and have made total funding commitments of $13 billion. The investment is accounted for under the equity method of accounting. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Productivity and Business Processes | $120.8B | $69.8B | +13.1% | 58% operating margin — Revenue growth was driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, with Microsoft 365 Commercial seat growth of 6% and growth in revenue per user; Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue grew 11% on subscriber growth of 8% to 89.0 million and a January 2025 price increase, and Dynamics 365 revenue grew 19%. |
| Intelligent Cloud | $106.3B | $44.6B | +21.5% | 42% operating margin — Revenue growth was driven by Azure and other cloud services, which grew 34% on demand for the portfolio of services, while Server products revenue decreased 3% on a continued customer shift to cloud offerings. |
| More Personal Computing | $54.6B | $14.2B | +7.5% | 26% operating margin — Revenue growth was driven by Gaming, where Xbox content and services revenue increased 16% on the Activision Blizzard acquisition and Xbox Game Pass, offset by a 25% decline in Xbox hardware revenue on lower console volume, and by Search and news advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs, which increased 20%. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt was approximately $43.2B ($3.0B current portion of long-term debt plus $40.2B long-term debt) against cash and cash equivalents of $30.2B and total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of $94.6B; total stockholders' equity was $343.5B.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $94.6B, up from $75.5B; the company stated it expects existing cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, cash flows from operations, and access to capital markets to be sufficient to fund operating activities and cash commitments for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $136.2B, investing $-72.6B, financing $-51.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $191.1B vs. current liabilities $141.2B (current ratio 1.35x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-06-30: $159.7B vs. $125.3B (1.27x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt principal payments of $3.0B are due in fiscal year 2026, with $46.2B thereafter, and interest payments of $1.5B in fiscal year 2026 and $25.5B thereafter.
- Certain counterparty agreements for derivative instruments require the company to maintain an investment grade credit rating and minimum liquidity of $1.0 billion; as of June 30, 2025, its long-term unsecured debt rating was AAA and no collateral was required to be posted.
- As of June 30, 2025, the eighth transition tax installment of $4.4 billion is short-term and payable in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Activision Blizzard acquisition completed October 13, 2023 for a total purchase price of $75.4 billion, allocated $51.0 billion to goodwill and $21.97 billion to intangible assets with a weighted average life of 15 years. | The acquisition added $51.0B of goodwill to the More Personal Computing segment and $21.97B of intangibles, contributing to the increase in amortization and to Xbox content and services revenue growth. |
| Segment composition was recast in August 2024, bringing the commercial components of Microsoft 365 together in Productivity and Business Processes, with prior-period segment information conformed. | The recast had no impact on the consolidated balance sheets, income statements, or cash flow statements, but changed segment-level presentation and disclosures. |
| The company adopted a new segment reporting standard beginning with annual reporting for fiscal year 2025, expanding disclosures about significant segment expenses. | The adoption resulted in incremental segment reporting disclosures, most notably disclosure of cost of revenue and operating expenses for each reportable segment. |
| Unearned revenue of $67.3B as of June 30, 2025, with $25.2B expected to be recognized in the three months ending September 30, 2025. | The balance reflects advance payments for volume licensing, cloud services, and other offerings recognized ratably over the coverage period. |
