payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

NVIDIA reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B (up 85% YoY) and net income of $58.3B ($2.39 diluted EPS), with Data Center revenue of $75.2B up 92% YoY.

Revenue and net income both increased sharply YoY, with gross margin expanding on the non-recurrence of the prior-year H20 inventory charge and net income further lifted by unrealized investment gains.

- Revenue of $81.6B rose 85% YoY and 20% sequentially; net income of $58.3B rose 211% YoY.
- Data Center revenue of $75.2B increased 92% YoY, driven by the ramp of Blackwell 300 products and demand for InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and NVLink solutions.
- Gross margin of 74.9% expanded 14.4 pts YoY, primarily due to the prior year's $4.5B charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.
- Other income (expense), net of $15.9B included unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities of $13.4B and non-marketable equity securities of $2.6B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $81,615M | $44,062M | +85.2% | Management attributes growth to data center products for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with Blackwell accounting for the majority of system shipments. |
| Gross profit | $61,157M | $26,668M | +129.3% | Gross margin increased primarily due to the prior year's $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations. |
| Operating income | $53,536M | $21,638M | +147.4% | Operating expenses rose 52% YoY, primarily driven by higher compensation and benefits, compute and infrastructure costs, and engineering development materials. |
| Net income | $58,321M | $18,775M | +210.6% | Net income exceeded operating income, reflecting total other income, net of $16,367M, primarily unrealized gains on equity investments. |
| Net income per share - diluted | $2.39 | $0.76 | +214.5% | Diluted EPS growth exceeded net income growth as the diluted weighted average share count declined to 24,391 million from 24,611 million. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income of $58,321M included total other income, net of $16,367M, of which Other income (expense), net of $15,929M primarily comprised unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities of $13.4B and non-marketable equity securities of $2.6B. Operating income was $53,536M. Gross margin benefited from the non-recurrence of the prior-year $4.5B H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations charge; current-period inventory and excess inventory purchase obligation provisions totaled $1.1B, with a provision release of $103M, for a net unfavorable gross margin impact of 1.2%.

Operating cash flow was 0.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $48.6B.

**Red flag:** Inventories increased to $25,797M from $21,403M at Jan 25, 2026, while revenue rose 20% sequentially.

**Red flag:** Three direct customers represented 21%, 17%, and 16% of total revenue, and three direct customers accounted for 30%, 18%, and 16% of accounts receivable as of April 26, 2026.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $243.0M (prior $244.0M), share repurchases $19.3B (prior $14.1B); capital expenditures $1.8B (prior $1.2B).

Capital allocation in the quarter combined large share repurchases and a nominal dividend with substantial purchases of non-marketable securities and equity investments, funded by operating cash flow. The Board subsequently approved an additional $80.0B share repurchase authorization and increased the quarterly cash dividend from $0.01 to $0.25 per share.

Return on equity was 29.8% (prior 22.4%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 22.5% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On May 18, 2026, our Board of Directors approved an additional $80.0 billion in share repurchase authorization, without expiration.
- On May 18, 2026, we increased our quarterly cash dividend from $0.01 per share to $0.25 per share to all shareholders of record on June 4, 2026.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide quantitative revenue or earnings guidance. It states that the Rubin platform is expected to start shipping in the second half of fiscal year 2027.

**Known trends**
- The availability of data centers, energy, and capital to support the buildout of NVIDIA AI infrastructure by customers and partners is crucial, and any shortage of these or other necessary resources could impact future revenue and financial performance.
- The complexity of bringing up our product architecture and sophisticated system configurations has caused and may in the future cause delays in production and create challenges in managing supply and demand.
- Beginning in February 2026, the U.S. government granted licenses that allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers; to date, we have not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program.

**Subsequent events**
- On May 18, 2026, our Board of Directors approved an additional $80.0 billion in share repurchase authorization, without expiration.
- On May 18, 2026, we increased our quarterly cash dividend from $0.01 per share to $0.25 per share to all shareholders of record on June 4, 2026.

> "We expect our Rubin platform to start shipping in the second half of fiscal year 2027." — NVIDIA Corporation

> "To date, we have not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program, and do not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China." — NVIDIA Corporation

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Revenue concentration among a limited number of direct customers, with three direct customers representing 21%, 17%, and 16% of total revenue in Q1 FY2027. | For the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, three direct customers represented 21%, 17%, and 16% of total revenue, all of which was primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment. |
| 2 | Supply and demand mismatches from long manufacturing lead times and capacity commitments, with manufacturing, supply, and capacity commitments of $119B as of April 26, 2026. | As of April 26, 2026, these commitments were $119 billion for which $95 billion will be paid in the remainder of fiscal year 2027 and the remaining balance will be paid in fiscal years 2028 through 2031. |
| 3 | Export control and regulatory restrictions on AI-related products, including the H200 licensing program requiring U.S. inspection and a 25% tariff upon importation. | The license requires that the H200s go through an inspection process in the United States prior to any shipment to the customer. As a result, any H200 shipped under the new licensing program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States. |
| 4 | Pending securities class action and derivative litigation related to channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining disclosures; the district court granted class certification on March 25, 2026. | On March 25, 2026, the district court granted plaintiffs' motion for class certification and certified a class of investors consisting of all persons or entities who purchased or otherwise acquired NVIDIA common stock between August 10, 2017, and November 15, 2018, inclusive |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compute & Networking | $74.5B | $53.3B | +88.3% | 72% operating margin — Management attributes the year-over-year increase to growth in Data Center products, driven by the ramp of Blackwell systems and demand for InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and NVLink solutions. |
| Graphics | $7.1B | $2.9B | +57.9% | 42% operating margin — Management attributes the year-over-year increase to sales of the Blackwell architecture. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt of $8,470M (net carrying amount) against cash and cash equivalents of $13,237M and shareholders' equity of $195,474M; long-term debt was $7,470M and short-term debt $1,000M.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable debt securities of $50.3B plus $30.2B of marketable equity securities; the commercial paper program had a capacity of $25.0B with no amounts outstanding.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $50.3B, investing $-26.4B, financing $-21.3B.

Working capital: Current assets $151.0B vs. current liabilities $43.9B (current ratio 3.44x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2026-01-25: $125.6B vs. $32.2B (3.91x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Debt maturities: $1,000M due in one year, $2,750M due in one to five years, $1,250M due in five to ten years, and $3,500M due in greater than ten years.
- As of April 26, 2026, we complied with the required covenants, which are non-financial in nature, under the outstanding notes.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Investment commitments of $27 billion as of April 26, 2026, expected to be made through the remainder of fiscal year 2027. | Represents a future cash outflow commitment beyond the balance sheet date. |
| Operating lease obligations of $5,604M, with expected future lease commencements of $32.4 billion between Q2 FY2027 and FY2033, primarily for data center leases. | Represents significant future lease commitments not yet reflected as liabilities on the balance sheet. |
| Facility lease guarantees with maximum gross exposure of $3.5 billion, reduced as partners make payments, with $712 million placed in escrow by partners. | Contingent obligation that could require payment in the event of partner default. |
| Unrecognized tax benefits of $4.5 billion, including related interest and penalties of $439 million, recorded in non-current income tax payable. | Potential future tax liability whose timing cannot be estimated; the company is under IRS examination for fiscal years 2023 and 2024. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

NVIDIA reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B (up 85% YoY) and net income of $58.3B ($2.39 diluted EPS), with Data Center revenue of $75.2B driven by the Blackwell 300 ramp.

Revenue, operating income, and net income all increased sharply YoY, with the prior-year period burdened by a $4.5B H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations charge that did not recur.

- Revenue of $81.6B rose 85% YoY and 20% sequentially, with Data Center at $75.2B (up 92% YoY) on the Blackwell 300 ramp and demand for InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and NVLink solutions.
- Net income of $58.3B included $16.0B of total other income, net, primarily from $13.4B of unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities and $2.6B on non-marketable equity securities.
- Gross margin expanded to 74.9% from 60.5% YoY, which management attributes primarily to the prior year's $4.5B charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.
- Three direct customers represented 21%, 17%, and 16% of total revenue, all primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $81,615M | $44,062M | +85.2% | Management attributes growth to data center products for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with Blackwell accounting for the majority of system shipments. |
| Gross profit | $61,157M | $26,668M | +129.3% | Gross margin increased primarily due to the prior year's $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations. |
| Operating income | $53,536M | $21,638M | +147.4% | Operating expenses rose 52% YoY, primarily driven by higher compensation and benefits, compute and infrastructure costs, and engineering development materials. |
| Net income | $58,321M | $18,775M | +210.6% | The change in Other income (expense), net compared to the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 was primarily driven by unrealized gains on investments in publicly-held equity securities of $13.4 billion and non-marketable equity securities of $2.6 billion. |
| Net income per share - diluted | $2.39 | $0.76 | +214.5% | Diluted weighted average shares declined to 24,391 million from 24,611 million, reflecting share repurchases. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income of $58.3B included $16.0B of total other income, net, of which $15.9B was Other income (expense), net, primarily from $13.4B of unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities and $2.6B on non-marketable equity securities. Operating income of $53.5B excludes these investment gains. The prior-year period included a $4.5B charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, and inventory and excess inventory purchase obligations provisions totaled $1.1B in the current quarter versus $5.3B a year ago.

Operating cash flow was 0.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $48.6B.

**Red flag:** Inventories increased to $25,797M from $21,403M at Jan 25, 2026, while revenue rose 20% sequentially; raw materials rose to $6,647M from $3,807M.

**Red flag:** Accounts receivable, net increased to $40,710M from $38,466M at Jan 25, 2026, with three direct customers accounting for 30%, 18%, and 16% of the accounts receivable balance.

**Red flag:** Net income of $58,321M exceeded net cash provided by operating activities of $50,344M, with the gap driven by $15,936M of non-cash gains from equity securities.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $243.0M (prior $244.0M), share repurchases $19.3B (prior $14.1B); capital expenditures $1.8B (prior $1.2B).

Capital allocation in the quarter combined shareholder returns with a large increase in investment purchases. Financing activities were directed to share repurchases and employee stock plan tax payments, while investing activities reflected $18.6B of purchases of non-marketable securities and $8.0B of purchases of marketable debt and equity securities. The company also increased its quarterly cash dividend and authorized a substantial additional repurchase program after period end.

Return on equity was 29.8% (prior 22.4%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 22.5% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On May 18, 2026, the Board of Directors approved an additional $80.0 billion in share repurchase authorization, without expiration.
- On May 18, 2026, the company increased its quarterly cash dividend from $0.01 per share to $0.25 per share to all shareholders of record on June 4, 2026, payable June 26, 2026.
- In the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, the company made $18.6 billion in investments in private companies and infrastructure funds.

## Forward Signals

No financial guidance was provided in the filing. Management stated it expects the Rubin platform to start shipping in the second half of fiscal year 2027.

**Known trends**
- The availability of data centers, energy, and capital to support the buildout of NVIDIA AI infrastructure by customers and partners is crucial, and any shortage of these or other necessary resources could impact future revenue and financial performance.
- The complexity of bringing up the product architecture and sophisticated system configurations has caused and may in the future cause delays in production and create challenges in managing supply and demand.
- Beginning in February 2026, the U.S. government granted licenses that allow shipment of small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers; to date, no revenue has been generated under the H200 licensing program.
- The recent rise in high-quality, open-source foundation models is making advanced AI capabilities broadly accessible, and if deployed on competitors' platforms, it could reduce demand for NVIDIA products and services.

**Subsequent events**
- On May 18, 2026, the Board of Directors approved an additional $80.0 billion in share repurchase authorization, without expiration.
- On May 18, 2026, the company increased its quarterly cash dividend from $0.01 per share to $0.25 per share, payable June 26, 2026 to shareholders of record on June 4, 2026.

> "We expect our Rubin platform to start shipping in the second half of fiscal year 2027." — NVIDIA Management

> "To date, we have not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program, and do not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China." — NVIDIA Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Revenue is concentrated among a limited number of direct customers; three direct customers represented 21%, 17%, and 16% of total revenue in Q1 FY2027. | For the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, three direct customers represented 21%, 17%, and 16% of total revenue, all of which was primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment. |
| 2 | Manufacturing, supply, and capacity commitments were $119 billion as of April 26, 2026, with $95 billion payable in the remainder of fiscal year 2027. | As of April 26, 2026, these commitments were $119 billion for which $95 billion will be paid in the remainder of fiscal year 2027 and the remaining balance will be paid in fiscal years 2028 through 2031. |
| 3 | The company is subject to export controls and licensing requirements affecting shipments to China, including the H200 licensing program and a 25% tariff on H200 imports into the United States. | As a result, any H200 shipped under the new licensing program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States. |
| 4 | The company is under examination by the Internal Revenue Service for fiscal years 2023 and 2024, and unrecognized tax benefits were $4.5 billion. | We are currently under examination by the Internal Revenue Service for our fiscal years 2023 and 2024. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compute & Networking | $74.5B | $53.3B | +88.3% | 72% operating margin — Management attributes the year-over-year increase to growth in Data Center products, driven by the ramp of Blackwell systems and demand for InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and NVLink solutions, plus the non-recurrence of a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the prior-year quarter. |
| Graphics | $7.1B | $2.9B | +57.9% | 42% operating margin — Management attributes the year-over-year increase to sales of the Blackwell architecture. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt was $8,470M ($1,000M short-term and $7,470M long-term) against total shareholders' equity of $195,474M and cash and cash equivalents of $13,237M; the company also held $37,098M of marketable debt securities and $30,237M of marketable equity securities.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable debt securities totaled $50.3 billion as of April 26, 2026, plus $30.2 billion of marketable equity securities; the commercial paper program had a capacity of $25.0 billion with no amounts outstanding.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $50.3B, investing $-26.4B, financing $-21.3B.

Working capital: Current assets $151.0B vs. current liabilities $43.9B (current ratio 3.44x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2026-01-25: $125.6B vs. $32.2B (3.91x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Debt maturities: $1,000M due in one year, $2,750M due in one to five years, $1,250M due in five to ten years, and $3,500M due in greater than ten years.
- As of April 26, 2026, the company complied with the required covenants, which are non-financial in nature, under the outstanding notes.
- Multi-year cloud service agreement commitments were $30 billion as of April 26, 2026, and total investment commitments were $27 billion, expected to be made through the remainder of fiscal year 2027.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Non-marketable securities and investment gains | Non-marketable equity securities increased to $42,336M from $22,251M at the beginning of the period, with $17,899M of net additions and $2,603M of unrealized gains; total investment commitments were $27 billion as of April 26, 2026. |
| Marketable equity securities and unrealized gains | Publicly-held equity securities of $30,237M included $27.4 billion subject to short-term lock-up restrictions; net unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities held at period end were $13.4 billion for the quarter. |
| Operating lease obligations and future data center leases | Between the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2033, the company expects to commence leases with future obligations of $32.4 billion, primarily for data center leases, with lease terms of 3 to 20 years. |
| Securities class action and derivative litigation | On March 25, 2026, the district court granted plaintiffs' motion for class certification in the In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation, and on April 8, 2026, NVIDIA filed a petition with the Ninth Circuit for permission to appeal; no accrued contingent liabilities were recorded. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

NVIDIA reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B (up 85% YoY) and net income of $58.3B ($2.39 diluted EPS), with Data Center revenue of $75.2B driven by the Blackwell 300 ramp.

Revenue, operating income, and net income all increased sharply YoY, with the prior-year period burdened by a $4.5B H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations charge and the current period aided by $16.0B of investment gains.

- Revenue of $81.6B rose 85% YoY and 20% sequentially, with Data Center at $75.2B (up 92% YoY) on the Blackwell 300 ramp and demand for InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and NVLink solutions.
- Net income of $58.3B included $16.0B of total other income, net, primarily from unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities of $13.4B and non-marketable equity securities of $2.6B.
- Gross margin of 74.9% expanded 14.4 points YoY, which management attributes to the prior year's $4.5B charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.
- Operating cash flow of $50.3B funded $19.3B of share repurchases and $1.8B of capital expenditures; the Board approved an additional $80.0B repurchase authorization and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.25 per share.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $81,615M | $44,062M | +85.2% | Management attributes the increase to data center products for accelerated computing and AI solutions, with Blackwell accounting for the majority of system shipments. |
| Gross profit | $61,157M | $26,668M | +129.3% | Gross margin increased primarily due to the prior year's $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations. |
| Operating income | $53,536M | $21,638M | +147.4% | Operating expenses rose 52% YoY, primarily driven by higher compensation and benefits expense, compute and infrastructure costs, and engineering development materials. |
| Net income | $58,321M | $18,775M | +210.6% | The change in Other income (expense), net compared to the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 was primarily driven by unrealized gains on investments in publicly-held equity securities of $13.4 billion and non-marketable equity securities of $2.6 billion. |
| Net income per share - diluted | $2.39 | $0.76 | +214.5% | Diluted weighted average shares declined to 24,391 million from 24,611 million, reflecting share repurchases. |
| Net income per share - basic | $2.40 | $0.77 | +211.7% | Basic weighted average shares declined to 24,286 million from 24,441 million, reflecting share repurchases. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income of $58.3B included $16.0B of total other income, net, primarily from unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities of $13.4B and non-marketable equity securities of $2.6B, which are non-operating. Operating income of $53.5B excludes these gains. The prior-year period included a $4.5B charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations within cost of revenue.

Operating cash flow was 0.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $48.6B.

**Red flag:** Net income of $58.3B exceeded operating income of $53.5B, with $16.0B of total other income, net, primarily from unrealized gains on equity securities that are subject to market price volatility.

**Red flag:** Accounts receivable, net increased to $40.7B from $38.5B at Jan 25, 2026, and three direct customers represented 30%, 18%, and 16% of the accounts receivable balance as of Apr 26, 2026.

**Red flag:** Inventories increased to $25.8B from $21.4B at Jan 25, 2026, with raw materials rising to $6.6B from $3.8B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $243.0M (prior $244.0M), share repurchases $19.3B (prior $14.1B); capital expenditures $1.8B (prior $1.2B).

Capital allocation in the quarter was weighted toward shareholder returns and ecosystem investment, funded by operating cash flow rather than debt. Share repurchases and dividends were funded from operations, and the company also deployed capital into non-marketable securities and infrastructure funds. The Board subsequently approved an additional $80.0B repurchase authorization and increased the quarterly dividend to $0.25 per share.

Return on equity was 29.8% (prior 22.4%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 22.5% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On May 18, 2026, the Board of Directors approved an additional $80.0 billion in share repurchase authorization, without expiration.
- On May 18, 2026, the company increased its quarterly cash dividend from $0.01 per share to $0.25 per share to all shareholders of record on June 4, 2026.
- In the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, the company made $18.6 billion in investments in private companies and infrastructure funds.

## Forward Signals

No financial guidance (revenue, margin, or EPS) is provided in this 10-Q. Management states that it expects the Rubin platform to start shipping in the second half of fiscal year 2027.

**Known trends**
- The availability of data centers, energy, and capital to support the buildout of NVIDIA AI infrastructure by customers and partners is crucial, and any shortage of these or other necessary resources could impact future revenue and financial performance.
- The complexity of bringing up the product architecture and sophisticated system configurations has caused and may in the future cause delays in production and create challenges in managing supply and demand.
- Beginning in February 2026, the U.S. government granted licenses that allow shipment of small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers; to date, no revenue has been generated under the H200 licensing program.
- The recent rise in high-quality, open-source foundation models is making advanced AI capabilities broadly accessible, and if deployed on competitors' platforms, it could reduce demand for products and services.

**Subsequent events**
- On May 18, 2026, the Board of Directors approved an additional $80.0 billion in share repurchase authorization, without expiration.
- On May 18, 2026, the company increased its quarterly cash dividend from $0.01 per share to $0.25 per share, payable on June 26, 2026 to shareholders of record on June 4, 2026.

> "We expect our Rubin platform to start shipping in the second half of fiscal year 2027." — NVIDIA Management

> "To date, we have not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program, and do not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China." — NVIDIA Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Revenue is concentrated among a limited number of direct customers; for Q1 FY2027, three direct customers represented 21%, 17%, and 16% of total revenue, all primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment. | For the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, three direct customers represented 21%, 17%, and 16% of total revenue, all of which was primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment. |
| 2 | Long manufacturing lead times and uncertain supply and capacity availability, combined with demand estimation errors, have led and could lead to supply-demand mismatches and inventory provisions. | Long manufacturing lead times and uncertain supply and capacity availability, combined with a failure to estimate customer demand accurately, has led and could in the future lead to mismatches between supply and demand. |
| 3 | Export controls and government actions, including restrictions on GPUs and AI-related semiconductors, could limit the ability to ship products and serve demand. | Export controls and other restrictions targeting GPUs and semiconductors associated with AI, which have been imposed and are likely to be more restrictive, would further limit our ability to export our technology, products, or services, creating a competitive disadvantage for us and negatively impacting our business and financial results. |
| 4 | The company is subject to regulatory inquiries and litigation, including a securities class action for which the district court granted class certification on March 25, 2026, and derivative lawsuits stayed pending resolution. | On March 25, 2026, the district court granted plaintiffs’ motion for class certification and certified a class of investors consisting of all persons or entities who purchased or otherwise acquired NVIDIA common stock between August 10, 2017, and November 15, 2018, inclusive |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compute & Networking | $74.5B | $53.3B | +88.3% | 72% operating margin — Management attributes the year-over-year increase to growth in Data Center products, driven by the ramp of Blackwell systems and demand for InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and NVLink solutions, and to the non-recurrence of a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026. |
| Graphics | $7.1B | $2.9B | +57.9% | 42% operating margin — Management attributes the year-over-year increase to sales of the Blackwell architecture. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt of $8.5B ($1.0B short-term and $7.5B long-term) against cash and cash equivalents of $13.2B and shareholders' equity of $195.5B; the notes are unsecured senior obligations and the company complied with required covenants, which are non-financial in nature.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable debt securities totaled $50.3B as of Apr 26, 2026, plus $30.2B of marketable equity securities; the commercial paper program had a capacity of $25.0B with no amounts outstanding.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $50.3B, investing $-26.4B, financing $-21.3B.

Working capital: Current assets $151.0B vs. current liabilities $43.9B (current ratio 3.44x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2026-01-25: $125.6B vs. $32.2B (3.91x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Aggregate debt maturities: $1.0B due in one year, $2.75B due in one to five years, $1.25B due in five to ten years, and $3.5B due in greater than ten years.
- As of April 26, 2026, the company complied with the required covenants, which are non-financial in nature, under the outstanding notes.
- Manufacturing, supply, and capacity commitments were $119 billion as of April 26, 2026, of which $95 billion will be paid in the remainder of fiscal year 2027.
- Multi-year cloud service agreement commitments were $30 billion as of April 26, 2026.

## Notable Footnotes

| --- | --- |
| Non-marketable securities and investment commitments | Non-marketable equity securities increased to $42.3B from $22.3B at Jan 25, 2026, with net additions of $17.9B and unrealized gains of $2.6B; total investment commitments were $27B as of Apr 26, 2026. |
| Marketable equity securities and unrealized gains | Marketable equity securities increased to $30.2B from $12.9B at Jan 25, 2026; net unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities held at period end were $13.4B for Q1 FY2027, recognized in Other income (expense), net. |
| Operating lease obligations and future lease commencements | Between the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2033, the company expects to commence leases with future obligations of $32.4B, primarily for data center leases, with lease terms of 3 to 20 years. |
| Income taxes and IRS examination | Income tax expense was $11.6B with an effective tax rate of 16.6%, up from 14.3%, primarily due to a lower percentage of tax benefits from stock-based compensation relative to the increase in income before income tax; the company is under IRS examination for fiscal years 2023 and 2024. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

JPMorgan Chase reported total net revenue of $182.4B (+2.8% YoY) and net income of $57.0B (-2.4% YoY), with diluted EPS of $20.02, as a $14.2B provision for credit losses (+33%) and a $7.9B Visa gain in the prior year shaped the comparison.

Revenue growth of 3% was outpaced by a 33% increase in the provision for credit losses and a 4% rise in noninterest expense, and the prior-year period included a $7.9B Visa share gain that did not recur, producing a 2% decline in net income.

- Net interest income rose 3% to $95.4B and noninterest revenue rose 2% to $87.0B, but net income declined 2% to $57.0B as the provision for credit losses increased 33% to $14.2B.
- Diluted EPS of $20.02 rose 1% despite lower net income, reflecting a lower diluted share count (2,781.5M vs. 2,879.0M) from net share repurchases.
- The provision included a $2.2B allowance addition related to the Apple Card transaction, and the total allowance for credit losses reached $31.2B with an allowance-to-retained-loans ratio of 1.83%.
- CET1 capital ratio (Standardized) declined to 14.6% from 15.7%, including an approximately 25 basis point decrease related to the Apple Card transaction.

## Results That Matter

| Provision for credit losses | $14,212M | $10,678M | +33.1% | Net charge-offs were $9.8 billion, up $1.2 billion, predominantly driven by Wholesale and Card Services; the net addition to the allowance was $4.4 billion, including $2.2 billion related to the Apple Card transaction. |
| Total noninterest expense | $95,640M | $91,797M | +4.2% | Driven by higher compensation expense, including higher revenue-related compensation and growth in the number of employees, higher brokerage expense and distribution fees, higher auto lease depreciation, continued investments in technology and marketing, and higher occupancy expense, partially offset by FDIC special assessment accrual releases of $763 million and the absence of a $1.0 billion contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

The prior-year period included a $7.9 billion net gain related to Visa shares and a $1.0 billion contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation, both recorded in the second quarter of 2024; the current period included a $588 million First Republic-related gain recorded in the first quarter of 2025 and a $774 million income tax benefit in Corporate recorded in the second quarter of 2025. The provision for credit losses included a $2.2 billion allowance addition related to the Apple Card transaction.

**Red flag:** Net income declined 2% to $57.0B while diluted EPS rose 1% to $20.02, with the divergence attributable to a lower diluted share count (2,781.5M vs. 2,879.0M) from net share repurchases.

**Red flag:** The provision for credit losses increased 33% to $14.2B, with net charge-offs up $1.2B to $9.8B and a net addition to the allowance of $4.4B, including $2.2B related to the Apple Card transaction.

**Red flag:** Net charge-off rate rose to 0.74% from 0.68%, and nonperforming assets increased 11% to $10.4B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $16.6B (prior $14.8B), share repurchases $31.6B (prior $18.8B).

Capital was returned to common shareholders through dividends and net share repurchases, with the common stock dividend declared per share rising to $5.80 from $4.80 and treasury stock repurchases increasing to $31,924 million from $19,007 million; retained earnings grew to $416,055 million. The filing states stockholders' equity increased reflecting net income and net unrealized gains in AOCI, largely offset by the impact of capital actions, including net repurchases of common shares and dividend payments on common and preferred stock.

Return on equity was 15.7% (prior 17.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 1.3% (prior 1.5%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On January 7, 2026, JPMorganChase announced that Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card, entering into a forward purchase commitment on December 30, 2025 to acquire the Apple credit card portfolio, with an expected closing in approximately 24 months.
- On December 8, 2025, JPMorganChase announced that Todd A. Combs had resigned from the Firm's Board of Directors and would join the Firm as the head of the Strategic Investment Group within the Firm's Security and Resiliency Initiative.

## Forward Signals

Management provided full-year 2026 outlook on January 13, 2026: net interest income of approximately $103 billion and net interest income excluding Markets of approximately $95 billion, market dependent; adjusted expense of approximately $105 billion, market dependent; and a net charge-off rate in Card Services of approximately 3.4%.

**Known trends**
- Management expects net interest income to be approximately $103 billion and net interest income excluding Markets to be approximately $95 billion, market dependent.
- Management expects adjusted expense to be approximately $105 billion, market dependent.
- Management expects the net charge-off rate in Card Services to be approximately 3.4%.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 7, 2026, JPMorganChase announced that Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card, with a forward purchase commitment entered into on December 30, 2025 to acquire the Apple credit card portfolio and an expected closing in approximately 24 months.
- On December 8, 2025, JPMorganChase announced that Todd A. Combs had resigned from the Firm's Board of Directors and would join the Firm as the head of the Strategic Investment Group within the Firm's Security and Resiliency Initiative.

| 5 | Political and geopolitical risk: Political developments in the U.S. and other countries could cause uncertainty in the economic environment and market conditions, including through monetary policy, fiscal policy, tariffs and trade policies. | Political developments in the U.S. and other countries could cause uncertainty in the economic environment and market conditions in which JPMorganChase operates. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total assets increased 11% to $4,424.9B, funded by deposits of $2,559.3B (+6%), long-term debt of $435.2B (+8%), federal funds purchased and securities loaned or sold under repurchase agreements of $442.4B (+49%), and short-term borrowings of $64.8B (+22%); total stockholders' equity rose 5% to $362.4B.

Liquidity: As of December 31, 2025, the Firm had eligible end-of-period High Quality Liquid Assets of approximately $915 billion and unencumbered marketable securities with a fair value of approximately $548 billion, resulting in approximately $1.5 trillion of liquidity sources; the Firm Liquidity coverage ratio (average) was 111% and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. LCR (average) was 115%.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $-147.8B, investing $-265.6B, financing $269.5B.

Working capital: Not applicable—the balance sheet is unclassified (no current-asset/current-liability split).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt increased driven by net issuances of structured notes in Markets due to client demand and an increase in the fair value of such instruments, as well as net issuances of long-term debt in Treasury and CIO, partially offset by a net reduction in Federal Home Loan Bank advances.
- CET1 capital was $288.5 billion, and the Standardized and Advanced CET1 ratios were 14.6% and 14.1%, respectively; SLR was 5.8%.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

JPMorganChase reported total net revenue of $182.4B (+2.8% YoY) and net income of $57.0B (-2.4% YoY), with diluted EPS of $20.02 (+1.4%) as share repurchases reduced the diluted share count.

Revenue grew 3% on higher Markets revenue and asset management fees, but net income declined 2% as the provision for credit losses rose 33% and the prior year included a $7.9B Visa share gain.

- Net interest income rose 3% to $95.4B and noninterest revenue rose 2% to $87.0B; the prior year included a $7.9B net gain on Visa shares that did not recur.
- Provision for credit losses increased 33% to $14.2B, including a $2.2B provision for lending-related commitments related to the Apple Card transaction.
- CET1 capital ratio (Standardized) declined to 14.6% from 15.7%, including an approximately 25 basis point decrease related to the Apple Card transaction.
- Diluted EPS of $20.02 rose 1.4% while net income declined 2.4%, reflecting a lower diluted share count of 2,781.5M versus 2,879.0M.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net Interest Income | $95,443,000,000 (2025-12-31) | $92,583,000,000 (2024-12-31) | — |  |
| Non-Interest Income | $87,004,000,000 (2025-12-31) | $84,973,000,000 (2024-12-31) | — |  |
| Total net revenue | $182,447M | $177,556M | +2.8% | Net interest income rose 3% and noninterest revenue rose 2%, with the prior year including a $7.9B net gain on Visa shares. |
| Provision for credit losses | $14,212M | $10,678M | +33.1% | Includes a $2.2B provision for lending-related commitments related to the Apple Card transaction and higher net charge-offs in Wholesale and Card Services. |
| Total noninterest expense | $95,640M | $91,797M | +4.2% | Driven by higher compensation expense, higher brokerage expense and distribution fees, higher auto lease depreciation, and continued investments in technology and marketing. |
| Income before income tax expense | $72,595M | $75,081M | −3.3% | Reflects higher provision for credit losses and noninterest expense, partially offset by higher revenue. |
| Net income | $57,048M | $58,471M | −2.4% | Reflects higher provision for credit losses and noninterest expense, partially offset by higher revenue and a lower effective tax rate. |
| Diluted earnings per share | $20.02 | $19.75 | +1.4% | Diluted EPS rose despite lower net income, reflecting a lower diluted share count from share repurchases. |
| Basic earnings per share | $20.05 | $19.79 | +1.3% | Reflects lower net income applicable to common stockholders offset by a lower weighted-average basic share count. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

The prior year (2024) included a $7.9B net gain related to Visa shares recorded in the second quarter of 2024 and a $1.0B contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation; the current year (2025) included a $588M First Republic-related gain recorded in the first quarter of 2025 and a $774M income tax benefit in Corporate recorded in the second quarter of 2025. The 2025 provision for credit losses included $2.2B related to the Apple Card transaction.

**Red flag:** Net income declined 2.4% to $57.0B while diluted EPS rose 1.4% to $20.02, with the divergence attributable to a lower diluted share count from share repurchases.

**Red flag:** Provision for credit losses rose 33.1% to $14.2B, with net charge-offs up $1.2B to $9.8B and a net addition to the allowance for credit losses of $4.4B.

**Red flag:** Net charge-off rate rose to 0.74% from 0.68%, and nonperforming assets increased 11% to $10.4B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $16.6B (prior $14.8B), share repurchases $31.6B (prior $18.8B).

Capital was deployed toward common stock repurchases and common and preferred dividends, with repurchases increasing relative to the prior year. The Firm also issued and redeemed preferred stock and issued long-term debt. The allocation was funded by operating and financing activities, including higher deposits and net proceeds from borrowings.

Return on equity was 15.7% (prior 17.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 1.3% (prior 1.5%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On January 7, 2026, JPMorganChase announced that Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card, with a forward purchase commitment entered into on December 30, 2025 to acquire the Apple credit card portfolio, expected to close in approximately 24 months.
- On December 8, 2025, JPMorganChase announced that Todd A. Combs had resigned from the Firm's Board of Directors and would join the Firm as the head of the Strategic Investment Group within the Firm's Security and Resiliency Initiative.

## Forward Signals

Management provided full-year 2026 outlook on January 13, 2026: net interest income of approximately $103 billion and net interest income excluding Markets of approximately $95 billion, market dependent; adjusted expense of approximately $105 billion, market dependent; and a net charge-off rate in Card Services of approximately 3.4%.

**Known trends**
- The Firm expects to be subject to heightened regulatory scrutiny and pervasive investigations and enforcement actions by governmental authorities.
- Higher interest rates could result in fewer originations of commercial and residential real estate loans, losses on underwriting exposures, increased financing costs for clients, loss of deposits, losses on available-for-sale securities, less liquidity in the financial markets, and higher funding costs.
- The Firm's businesses could be negatively affected by economic uncertainty resulting from political and geopolitical developments.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 7, 2026, JPMorganChase announced that Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card, with a forward purchase commitment entered into on December 30, 2025 to acquire the Apple credit card portfolio, expected to close in approximately 24 months.
- On December 8, 2025, JPMorganChase announced that Todd A. Combs had resigned from the Firm's Board of Directors and would join the Firm as the head of the Strategic Investment Group within the Firm's Security and Resiliency Initiative.

| 2 | The Firm faces significant legal risks from civil and governmental proceedings, including litigation, investigations and enforcement actions, and its exposure could exceed established reserves. | the extent of JPMorganChase’s exposure to legal matters is unpredictable and could, in some cases, exceed the amount of reserves that JPMorganChase has established for those matters |
| 3 | Adverse changes in the financial condition of clients, counterparties, central counterparties and other market participants could result in losses, and the Firm has experienced instances of borrower or counterparty fraud related to collateral. | JPMorganChase has in the past, and could in the future, experience instances in which borrowers or other counterparties engage in fraudulent activity related to the accounting, reporting or representation of collateral. |
| 4 | Changes in interest rates and credit spreads could adversely affect the Firm's earnings or its liquidity and capital levels, including through deposit loss, losses on available-for-sale securities, and higher funding costs. | Higher interest rates could also result in: •fewer originations of commercial and residential real estate loans •losses on underwriting exposures or increases in client-specific downgrades •increased financing costs for clients, which could lead to an increase in the allowance for credit losses and higher net charge-offs •the loss of deposits, including where customers transition to higher-yielding products •losses on available-for-sale (“AFS”) securities held in the investment securities portfolio •less liquidity in the financial markets, and •higher funding costs. |
| 5 | Holders of the Parent Company's debt and equity securities will absorb losses if it were to enter into a resolution, with equity holders and unsecured creditors junior to subsidiary creditors and priority and secured creditors. | If the Parent Company were to enter into a resolution, holders of eligible LTD, other unsecured creditors and holders of equity securities of the Parent Company will absorb the losses of the Parent Company and its subsidiaries. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total assets increased 11% to $4,424.9B and total stockholders' equity increased 5% to $362.4B. Long-term debt rose 8% to $435.2B and short-term borrowings rose 22% to $64.8B. The Firm's balance sheet is unclassified; no current-asset/current-liability split is reported.

Liquidity: As of December 31, 2025, the Firm had eligible end-of-period High Quality Liquid Assets of approximately $915 billion and unencumbered marketable securities with a fair value of approximately $548 billion, resulting in approximately $1.5 trillion of liquidity sources. The Firm Liquidity coverage ratio (average) was 111% and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. LCR (average) was 115%.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $-147.8B, investing $-265.6B, financing $269.5B.

Working capital: Not applicable—the Firm reports an unclassified balance sheet with no current-asset/current-liability split.

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt increased driven by net issuances of structured notes in Markets due to client demand and an increase in the fair value of such instruments, as well as net issuances of long-term debt in Treasury and CIO, partially offset by a net reduction in Federal Home Loan Bank advances.
- The Firm must periodically submit a detailed resolution plan to the Federal Reserve and the FDIC for its rapid and orderly resolution in bankruptcy, without extraordinary government support, in the event of material financial distress or failure.

The 2025 provision for credit losses included a $2.2B provision for lending-related commitments related to the Apple Card transaction, and the Standardized CET1 ratio included an approximately 25 basis point decrease related to the transaction. |
| Visa share gain and Foundation contribution | The prior year (2024) included a $7.9B net gain related to Visa shares recorded in the second quarter of 2024 and a $1.0B contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation, both of which affected the comparability of noninterest revenue and noninterest expense. |
| First Republic acquisition | The 2025 results included a $588M First Republic-related gain recorded in the first quarter of 2025 in Corporate. The 2023 results included an estimated bargain purchase gain of $2.8B associated with the First Republic acquisition. |
| Accounting standard adopted January 1, 2024 | The adoption of the Equity Method and Joint Ventures guidance under the modified retrospective method on January 1, 2024 resulted in a decrease to retained earnings of $161 million and increased the Firm's income tax expense and effective tax rate by approximately $450 million and two percentage points, respectively, in the first quarter of 2024, with no material impact to net income. |
| CECL capital transition provision | As of January 1, 2025, the benefit from the CECL capital transition provision had been fully phased out, affecting the comparability of the 2025 capital ratios to the 2024 and 2023 ratios. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

JPMorganChase reported total net revenue of $182.4B (+3% YoY) and net income of $57.0B (-2% YoY), with diluted EPS of $20.02 (+1% YoY).

Revenue growth continued but net income declined year over year, with the prior year including a $7.9B net gain on Visa shares and the current year including a $2.2B Apple Card-related provision; CET1 declined partly on the Apple Card transaction.

- Total net revenue rose 3% to $182.4B, split between net interest income of $95.4B (+3%) and noninterest revenue of $87.0B (+2%).
- Net income declined 2% to $57.0B, while diluted EPS rose 1% to $20.02, as weighted-average diluted shares fell to 2,781.5M from 2,879.0M.
- The provision for credit losses increased 33% to $14.2B, including a $2.2B provision for lending-related commitments related to the Apple Card transaction.
- CET1 capital ratio (Standardized) declined to 14.6% from 15.7%, including an approximately 25 basis point decrease related to the Apple Card transaction.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net Interest Income | $95,443,000,000 (2025-12-31) | $92,583,000,000 (2024-12-31) | — |  |
| Non-Interest Income | $87,004,000,000 (2025-12-31) | $84,973,000,000 (2024-12-31) | — |  |
| Total net revenue | $182,447M | $177,556M | +2.8% | Net interest income rose 3% and noninterest revenue rose 2%, with the prior year including a $7.9B net gain related to Visa shares. |
| Provision for credit losses | $14,212M | $10,678M | +33.1% | Net charge-offs were $9.8B and the net addition to the allowance for credit losses was $4.4B, including $2.2B related to the Apple Card transaction. |
| Total noninterest expense | $95,640M | $91,797M | +4.2% | Driven by higher compensation expense, higher brokerage expense and distribution fees, higher auto lease depreciation, continued investments in technology and marketing, and higher occupancy expense, partially offset by FDIC special assessment accrual releases and the absence of a $1.0B Visa share contribution to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation. |
| Income before income tax expense | $72,595M | $75,081M | −3.3% | Not disclosed |
| Net income | $57,048M | $58,471M | −2.4% | Not disclosed |
| Diluted earnings per share | $20.02 | $19.75 | +1.4% | Not disclosed |
| Basic earnings per share | $20.05 | $19.79 | +1.3% | Not disclosed |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

The prior year (2024) included a $7.9B net gain related to Visa shares in other income and a $1.0B contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation in noninterest expense; the current year (2025) included a $588M First Republic-related gain in the first quarter and a $2.2B provision for lending-related commitments related to the Apple Card transaction. The effective tax rate decreased to 21.4% from 22.1%, partly due to a $774M income tax benefit in Corporate recorded in the second quarter of 2025.

**Red flag:** Net income declined 2% to $57.0B while the provision for credit losses rose 33% to $14.2B, with net charge-offs up $1.2B to $9.8B and the net charge-off rate rising to 0.74% from 0.68%.

**Red flag:** The allowance for loan losses to total retained loans coverage ratio declined to 1.83% from 1.87% even as gross loans grew 11% to $1,493.4B.

**Red flag:** Nonperforming assets increased 11% to $10.4B, driven by higher consumer nonaccrual loans (including the impact of California wildfires) and higher wholesale nonaccrual loans.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $16.6B (prior $14.8B), share repurchases $31.6B (prior $18.8B).

Capital was returned to shareholders through common stock repurchases and dividends while the balance sheet expanded, with total assets up 11% and loans up 11%; the filing states stockholders' equity increased reflecting net income and net unrealized gains in AOCI, largely offset by capital actions including net repurchases of common shares and dividend payments on common and preferred stock.

Return on equity was 15.7% (prior 17.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 1.3% (prior 1.5%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On January 7, 2026, JPMorganChase announced that Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card, with a forward purchase commitment entered into on December 30, 2025 to acquire the Apple credit card portfolio, expected to close in approximately 24 months.
- On December 8, 2025, JPMorganChase announced that Todd A. Combs had resigned from the Firm's Board of Directors and would join the Firm as the head of the Strategic Investment Group within the Firm's Security and Resiliency Initiative.

## Forward Signals

Management provided full-year 2026 outlook on January 13, 2026: net interest income of approximately $103 billion and net interest income excluding Markets of approximately $95 billion, market dependent; adjusted expense of approximately $105 billion, market dependent; and a net charge-off rate in Card Services of approximately 3.4%.

**Known trends**
- Management expects net interest income to be approximately $103 billion and net interest income excluding Markets to be approximately $95 billion, market dependent.
- Management expects adjusted expense to be approximately $105 billion, market dependent.
- Management expects the net charge-off rate in Card Services to be approximately 3.4%.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 7, 2026, JPMorganChase announced that Chase will become the new issuer of Apple Card, with a forward purchase commitment entered into on December 30, 2025 to acquire the Apple credit card portfolio, expected to close in approximately 24 months.
- On December 8, 2025, JPMorganChase announced that Todd A. Combs had resigned from the Firm's Board of Directors and would join the Firm as the head of the Strategic Investment Group within the Firm's Security and Resiliency Initiative.

## Risks

| 2 | Credit risk: adverse changes in the financial condition of clients, counterparties, central counterparties and other market participants could result in losses, including from fraudulent activity related to collateral. | JPMorganChase has in the past, and could in the future, experience instances in which borrowers or other counterparties engage in fraudulent activity related to the accounting, reporting or representation of collateral. |

| 4 | Resolution risk: holders of JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s debt and equity securities will absorb losses if it were to enter into a resolution, with equity and unsecured creditors junior to subsidiary creditors. | If the Parent Company were to enter into a resolution, holders of eligible LTD, other unsecured creditors and holders of equity securities of the Parent Company will absorb the losses of the Parent Company and its subsidiaries. |
| 5 | Operational risk: dependence on operational systems and employees, as well as those of acquired businesses and external parties, and the harm that could be caused by a successful cyber attack. | Operational risks, including risks associated with JPMorganChase’s dependence on its operational systems and its employees, as well as the systems and employees of acquired businesses and external parties; the harm that could be caused by a successful cyber attack affecting JPMorganChase or by other extraordinary events |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total assets increased 11% to $4,424.9B, funded by deposits up 6% to $2,559.3B, long-term debt up 8% to $435.2B, federal funds purchased and securities loaned or sold under repurchase agreements up 49% to $442.4B, and short-term borrowings up 22% to $64.8B; total stockholders' equity rose 5% to $362.4B.

Liquidity: As of December 31, 2025, the Firm had eligible end-of-period High Quality Liquid Assets of approximately $915 billion and unencumbered marketable securities with a fair value of approximately $548 billion, resulting in approximately $1.5 trillion of liquidity sources; Firm LCR (average) was 111% and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. LCR (average) was 115%.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $-147.8B, investing $-265.6B, financing $269.5B.

Working capital: Not disclosed—the balance sheet is unclassified (no current-asset/current-liability split) for this financial institution.

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt increased driven by net issuances of structured notes in Markets due to client demand and an increase in the fair value of such instruments, as well as net issuances of long-term debt in Treasury and CIO, partially offset by a net reduction in Federal Home Loan Bank advances.
- CET1 capital was $288.5 billion, and the Standardized and Advanced CET1 ratios were 14.6% and 14.1%, respectively; SLR was 5.8%.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Coca-Cola reported Q1 2026 net operating revenues of $12,472M and net income attributable to shareowners of $3,924M ($0.91 diluted EPS), with operating income up 19% to $4,359M.

Revenue growth accelerated to 12% with operating margin up 210 basis points, and the cash-flow profile flipped from a large operating outflow to a $2.0B inflow.

- Net operating revenues rose 12% to $12,472M from $11,129M, driven by 8% concentrate sales volume growth, 2% favorable price/mix and a 3% favorable foreign currency impact, partly offset by a 1% acquisitions/divestitures drag.
- Operating income increased 19% to $4,359M and operating margin expanded to 35.0% from 32.9%, as gross margin rose to 63.0% from 62.6%.
- Net income attributable to shareowners was $3,924M ($0.91 diluted EPS) versus $3,330M ($0.77) a year earlier; the effective tax rate fell to 14.0% from 17.8%.
- Operating cash flow swung to $2,021M from a $5,202M use a year earlier, while financing activities used $3,868M versus $3,432M provided in the prior-year quarter.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net Operating Revenues | $12,472M | $11,129M | +12.1% | Management attributes the increase to 8% concentrate sales volume growth, 2% favorable price/mix and a 3% favorable foreign currency impact, partly offset by a 1% acquisitions/divestitures drag. |
| Gross Profit | $7,852M | $6,966M | +12.7% | Gross margin rose to 63.0% from 62.6%, primarily on favorable pricing initiatives and foreign currency, as well as the sale of the Nigeria finished product operations, partly offset by higher commodity costs. |
| Operating Income | $4,359M | $3,659M | +19.1% | Management cites 8% concentrate sales volume growth, favorable price/mix, lower operating expenses, lower other operating charges and a 4% favorable foreign currency impact, partly offset by increased marketing spending and higher commodity costs. |
| Net Income Attributable to Shareowners | $3,924M | $3,330M | +17.8% | The increase reflects higher operating income and a lower effective tax rate of 14.0% versus 17.8%, which included $279M of net discrete tax benefits. |
| Diluted Net Income Per Share | $0.91 | $0.77 | +18.2% | Diluted EPS moved with net income; average diluted shares outstanding were 4,314M versus 4,313M. |
| Basic Net Income Per Share | $0.91 | $0.77 | +18.2% | Basic EPS moved with net income; average basic shares outstanding were 4,302M in both periods. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported results include items outside core operations: a $10M impairment charge on African bottling operations held for sale and $13M of trade receivables factoring costs in other income (loss) — net, plus $21M of other operating charges (including $10M for an indemnification agreement, $4M for North America modernization, $4M BodyArmor noncompete amortization and $3M tax litigation expense). The prior-year quarter included a $331M gain on the sale of a portion of the CCEP ownership interest, a $25M equity method investee impairment and $47M of fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement within other operating charges. The current quarter's 14.0% effective tax rate included $279M of net discrete tax benefits, including a $194M return-to-provision benefit and $55M of net interest income on the IRS Tax Litigation Deposit.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $1.8B.

**Red flag:** The BodyArmor trademark's fair value approximates its carrying value as of April 3, 2026, after a $960M impairment in Q4 2025; management states an additional impairment charge is likely if near-term results miss revised projections or discount rates rise.

**Red flag:** The IRS transfer pricing litigation remains under litigation designation, with a $6.0B total liability for 2007-2009 tax years already paid as a deposit and pending appeal.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $2.3B (prior $89.0M), share repurchases $477.0M (prior $370.0M); capital expenditures $266.0M (prior $309.0M).

The filing frames capital allocation priorities as investing to support operations, growing the dividend, pursuing consumer-centric acquisitions and using excess cash to repurchase shares over time. Dividends and buybacks were funded from operating cash flow, which turned positive this quarter, while total debt declined sequentially.

Return on equity was 11.7% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 3.8% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- The Company expects 2026 capital expenditures of approximately $2.2 billion.
- During 2026, the Company expects to repurchase shares to offset dilution resulting from employee stock-based compensation.

## Forward Signals

The filing states that, based on current spot rates and hedging coverage in place, foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations are expected to have a favorable impact on full year 2026 net operating revenues and operating income. The Company's effective tax rate in 2026 is expected to be approximately 19.9% before considering the potential impact of any significant operating and nonoperating items. 2026 capital expenditures are expected to be approximately $2.2 billion.

**Known trends**
- The first quarter of 2026 had six additional days compared to the first quarter of 2025, contributing to differences between concentrate sales volume and unit case volume growth rates; management expects these differences to be minimal on a full year basis.
- The Company expects to reclassify into income during the next 12 months net losses of $97 million from the pretax amount recorded in AOCI as anticipated cash flows occur.
- The OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax framework and related side-by-side guidance continue to evolve, with the Company monitoring potential impacts in the countries in which it operates.

**Subsequent events**
- Not disclosed—no material events after the April 3, 2026 period end are described in the provided excerpts.

> "Based on current spot rates and our hedging coverage in place, we expect foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations will have a favorable impact on our full year 2026 net operating revenues." — The Coca-Cola Company

> "Based on current spot rates and our hedging coverage in place, we expect foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations will have a favorable impact on our full year 2026 operating income." — The Coca-Cola Company

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | BodyArmor trademark impairment risk: the remaining carrying value is $2,440 million and fair value approximates carrying value as of April 3, 2026, after a $960 million impairment in Q4 2025. | If the near-term operating results of this trademark do not achieve our revised financial projections, or if the macroeconomic conditions change, causing the discount rate to increase without an offsetting increase in the operating results, it is likely that we would be required to recognize an additional impairment charge. |
| 2 | IRS transfer pricing litigation for tax years 2007 through 2009: the Tax Court entered a decision reflecting additional federal income tax of $2.7 billion, and with applicable interest the total liability is $6.0 billion, which the Company paid as a deposit and is appealing. | On August 2, 2024, the Tax Court entered a decision reflecting additional federal income tax of $2.7 billion for the 2007 through 2009 tax years. With applicable interest, the total liability for the 2007 through 2009 tax years resulting from the Tax Court's decision is $6.0 billion |
| 3 | African bottling operations held for sale: an additional $10 million impairment charge was recorded in Q1 2026 based on revised estimates, following a $1,274 million impairment in 2025; closing of the CCHBC sale is subject to regulatory approvals and expected by the end of 2026. | During the three months ended April 3, 2026, we recorded an additional impairment charge of $10 million based on management's revised estimates. |
| 4 | Guarantees: the Company was contingently liable for guarantees of indebtedness owed by third parties of $837 million as of April 3, 2026, of which $63 million related to variable interest entities. | As of April 3, 2026, we were contingently liable for guarantees of indebtedness owed by third parties of $837 million, of which $63 million was related to variable interest entities. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| North America | $4.9B | $1.6B | +12.2% | 33% operating margin — Unit case volume rose 4%, including 5% growth in both Trademark Coca-Cola and water, sports, coffee and tea, and 2% growth in sparkling flavors; operating income increased on concentrate sales volume growth of 11%, favorable price/mix and lower operating expenses, partly offset by increased marketing spending and higher commodity costs. |
| EMEA | $3.0B | $1.3B | +13.4% | 42% operating margin — Unit case volume rose 2%, with 4% growth in both sparkling flavors and water, sports, coffee and tea, partly offset by a 15% decline in juice, value-added dairy and plant-based beverages primarily from the Nigeria finished product operations sale; operating income increased on 5% concentrate sales volume growth, favorable price/mix and a 6% favorable foreign currency impact. |
| Latin America | $1.7B | $1.0B | +13.6% | 62% operating margin — Unit case volume rose 1%, including 3% growth in water, sports, coffee and tea and 2% growth in sparkling flavors, with 2% growth in Brazil partly offset by declines of 5% in Argentina and 1% in Mexico; operating income increased on 7% concentrate sales volume growth, favorable price/mix, lower commodity costs and a 5% favorable foreign currency impact. |
| Bottling investments | $1.6B | $191.0M | +12.1% | 12% operating margin — Unit case volume rose 1%, primarily driven by growth in Africa, partly offset by the impact of refranchising certain territories of bottling operations in India; operating income increased on 11% unit case volume growth, lower commodity costs, lower operating expenses and a 12% favorable foreign currency impact, partly offset by unfavorable price/mix and the India refranchising. |
| A. Pacific | $1.5B | $536.0M | +6.1% | 36% operating margin — Unit case volume rose 5%, including 8% growth in water, sports, coffee and tea, 5% growth in Trademark Coca-Cola and 4% growth in sparkling flavors, with 8% growth in Greater China and Mongolia; operating income decreased on unfavorable price/mix, higher commodity costs and increased marketing spending, partly offset by 10% concentrate sales volume growth and a 3% favorable foreign currency impact. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt declined sequentially: long-term debt of $39,065M versus $42,119M at December 31, 2025, and current maturities of long-term debt of $4,493M versus $1,822M, while loans and notes payable fell to $332M from $1,551M. Cash and cash equivalents of $10,574M plus short-term investments of $509M and marketable securities of $2,737M; total equity of $35,734M.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and marketable securities totaled $13.8 billion as of April 3, 2026, supplemented by $6.6 billion in unused backup lines of credit for general corporate purposes that expire at various times through 2031.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $2.0B, investing $1.7B, financing $-3.9B.

Working capital: Current assets $30.4B vs. current liabilities $22.4B (current ratio 1.36x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-12-31: $31.0B vs. $21.3B (1.46x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- The Company had $6.6 billion in unused backup lines of credit for general corporate purposes as of April 3, 2026, expiring at various times through 2031.
- Outstanding commercial paper borrowings were $250 million as of April 3, 2026, down from $1,495 million at December 31, 2025.
- The Company sold $3,271 million of trade accounts receivables under its factoring program during the three months ended April 3, 2026, with factoring costs of $13 million.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Coca-Cola reported Q1 2026 net operating revenues of $12.47B (up 12.1% YoY) and net income attributable to shareowners of $3.92B ($0.91 diluted EPS), with operating income up 19% to $4.36B.

The quarter reflects a return to positive operating cash flow and double-digit revenue growth, with margin expansion across most segments, while the prior-year period included a $331M gain from the sale of a portion of the CCEP ownership interest.

- Net operating revenues rose 12% YoY to $12,472M, driven by 8% concentrate sales volume growth, 2% favorable price/mix, 3% favorable foreign currency, partially offset by a 1% negative impact from acquisitions and divestitures.
- Operating income increased 19% to $4,359M, with operating margin expanding to 35.0% from 32.9%, attributed to volume growth, favorable price/mix, lower operating expenses and lower other operating charges.
- Diluted EPS of $0.91 compared to $0.77 in the prior-year quarter, with average diluted shares outstanding of 4,314M versus 4,313M.
- Operating cash flow swung to positive $2,021M from negative $5,202M in the prior-year period, primarily due to a smaller net change in operating assets and liabilities.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net Operating Revenues | $12,472M | $11,129M | +12.1% | Driven by 8% concentrate sales volume growth, 2% favorable price/mix, and 3% favorable foreign currency fluctuations, partially offset by a 1% negative impact from acquisitions and divestitures. |
| Operating Income | $4,359M | $3,659M | +19.1% | Driven by an increase in concentrate sales volume of 8%, favorable price/mix, lower operating expenses, lower other operating charges and a favorable foreign currency exchange rate impact of 4%, partially offset by increased marketing spending and higher commodity costs. |
| Net Income Attributable to Shareowners | $3,924M | $3,330M | +17.8% | Increase reflects higher operating income and equity income, partially offset by lower other income (loss) — net, which in the prior year included a $331M gain on the sale of a portion of the CCEP ownership interest. |
| Diluted Net Income Per Share | $0.91 | $0.77 | +18.2% | EPS growth broadly in line with net income growth, with average diluted shares outstanding of 4,314M versus 4,313M. |
| Gross Profit Margin | 63.0% | 62.6% | +0.4 ppts | The increase was primarily due to the favorable impact of pricing initiatives and foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations, as well as the impact of the sale of our finished product operations in Nigeria, partially offset by higher commodity costs. |
| Operating Margin | 35.0% | 32.9% | +2.1 ppts | Expanded on higher concentrate sales volume, favorable price/mix, lower operating expenses and lower other operating charges, partially offset by increased marketing spending and higher commodity costs. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported results include several items affecting comparability. The prior-year quarter included a $331M gain on the sale of a portion of the CCEP ownership interest recorded in other income (loss) — net, and a $47M charge related to the remeasurement of the fairlife contingent consideration liability. The current quarter included a $10M impairment charge related to bottling operations in Africa held for sale, $13M of trade accounts receivable factoring costs, and $21M of other operating charges. The effective tax rate of 14.0% in Q1 2026 included $279M of net tax benefits related to discrete items, including $55M of net interest income related to the IRS Tax Litigation Deposit and a $194M tax benefit primarily related to return to provision adjustments.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $1.8B.

**Red flag:** The BodyArmor trademark carrying value of $2,440M approximates its fair value as of April 3, 2026, and management states that additional impairment charges are likely if near-term operating results do not achieve revised projections or if discount rates increase.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $2.3B (prior $89.0M), share repurchases $477.0M (prior $370.0M); capital expenditures $266.0M (prior $309.0M).

Capital allocation priorities stated as investing to support business operations, continuing to grow the dividend, enhancing the beverage portfolio through consumer-centric acquisitions, and using excess cash to repurchase shares over time. Dividends paid increased substantially year-over-year, and share repurchases were executed to offset dilution from employee stock-based compensation. The company expects 2026 capital expenditures of approximately $2.2B.

Return on equity was 11.7% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 3.8% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- The company expects to repurchase shares during 2026 to offset dilution resulting from employee stock-based compensation.

## Forward Signals

The company expects foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations to have a favorable impact on full year 2026 net operating revenues and operating income based on current spot rates and hedging coverage in place. The effective tax rate in 2026 is expected to be approximately 19.9% before considering the potential impact of any significant operating and nonoperating items. Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be approximately $2.2B. No explicit revenue or EPS guidance ranges were provided.

**Known trends**
- Sales of ready-to-drink beverages are somewhat seasonal, with the second and third calendar quarters typically accounting for the highest sales volumes.
- The first quarter of 2026 had six additional days compared to the first quarter of 2025, contributing to differences between concentrate sales volume and unit case volume growth rates; the company expects these differences to be minimal on a full year basis.
- The company is monitoring OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax developments, including a January 2026 side-by-side framework largely exempting U.S.-headquartered companies.

**Subsequent events**
- Not disclosed—no material events after the period end were disclosed in the provided excerpts.

With applicable interest, the total liability for the 2007 through 2009 tax years resulting from the Tax Court's decision is $6.0 billion, for which the IRS issued the Company invoices on September 3, 2024. |
