payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Walmart's fiscal 2026 total revenues rose 4.7% to $713.2B, net income attributable to Walmart increased to $21.9B, and diluted EPS reached $2.73.

Revenue growth decelerated to 4.7% from 5.1% in the prior year, while net income growth accelerated to 12.6% from 25.3%, aided by a $2.1B net gain on equity investments versus a $0.8B loss in the prior year.

- Total revenues of $713.2B (+4.7% YoY) and net income attributable to Walmart of $21.9B (+12.6% YoY) reflect growth across all three reportable segments.
- Operating income of $29.8B (+1.6% YoY) grew slower than revenue, with operating margin declining to 4.2% from 4.4%.
- Diluted EPS of $2.73 (+13.3% YoY) benefited from a lower diluted share count (8,022M vs. 8,081M) alongside higher net income.
- Free cash flow of $14.9B increased from $12.7B, driven by higher operating cash flow of $41.6B, partially offset by $26.6B in capital expenditures.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $713,163M | $680,985M | +4.7% | Primarily due to increases in net sales, which increased $31.9 billion or 4.7%, driven by strong positive comparable sales across U.S. segments and international markets. |
| Net sales | $706,413M | $674,538M | +4.7% | Growth was primarily driven by increases in average ticket and transactions, and also reflected growth in unit volumes, with strength in eCommerce and grocery and health and wellness. |
| Operating income | $29,825M | $29,348M | +1.6% | Operating income as a percentage of net sales decreased 13 basis points for fiscal 2026, primarily due to higher self-insured general liability claims expense, a PhonePe share-based compensation charge, and increased depreciation. |
| Consolidated net income | $22,270M | $20,157M | +10.5% | Increase was primarily due to net increases in the fair value of equity and other investments combined with higher operating income. |
| Consolidated net income attributable to Walmart | $21,893M | $19,436M | +12.6% | Attributable net income grew faster than consolidated net income due to a lower noncontrolling interest deduction ($377M vs. $721M). |
| Diluted net income per common share attributable to Walmart | $2.73 | $2.41 | +13.3% | EPS growth exceeded net income growth due to a reduction in the weighted-average diluted share count from 8,081M to 8,022M. |
| Basic net income per common share attributable to Walmart | $2.74 | $2.42 | +13.2% | Basic EPS reflects the same net income and share-count dynamics as diluted EPS. |
| Gross profit | $171,018M | $162,785M | +5.1% | Gross profit rate increased 8 basis points, primarily driven by the Walmart U.S. segment due to disciplined inventory management and growth in higher margin businesses globally. |
| Operating, selling, general and administrative expenses | $147,943M | $139,884M | +5.8% | Increase as a percentage of net sales was primarily due to higher self-insured general liability claims expense of approximately $0.9 billion, a $0.7 billion PhonePe share-based compensation charge, and increased depreciation. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported operating income of $29.8B included a $0.7B non-cash charge related to the modification of PhonePe share-based payment arrangements and approximately $0.9B of higher self-insured general liability claims expense. Other gains and losses contributed a net gain of $2.1B in fiscal 2026 versus a net loss of $0.8B in fiscal 2025, primarily from changes in the fair value of equity and other investments. The effective tax rate rose to 24.4% from 23.4%, partly because the PhonePe share-based compensation charge provided no tax benefit.

Operating cash flow was 1.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $14.9B.

**Red flag:** Operating expenses grew 5.8% YoY, faster than the 4.7% revenue growth, compressing operating margin to 4.2% from 4.4%.

**Red flag:** The $2.1B net gain on equity and other investments in other gains and losses is non-operating and contributed to the increase in consolidated net income.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $7.5B (prior $6.7B), share repurchases $8.1B (prior $4.5B); capital expenditures $26.6B (prior $23.8B).

Capital allocation prioritized higher-return areas focused on automation such as eCommerce, supply chain and store and club investments, with capital expenditures increasing to support the omnichannel growth strategy. Share repurchases accelerated, and the Board approved a new $30.0B share repurchase authorization in February 2026, replacing the remaining capacity under the prior $20.0B program. Dividends paid increased, and the fiscal 2027 annual dividend was approved at $0.99 per share, up from $0.94.

Return on equity was 22.0% (prior 21.4%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 7.7% (prior 7.5%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In February 2026, the Board of Directors approved a new $30.0 billion share repurchase authorization, which has no expiration date or other restrictions limiting the period over which the Company can make repurchases, and beginning February 23, 2026, replaced the remaining capacity under the prior authorization.
- Effective February 19, 2026, the Company approved the fiscal 2027 annual dividend of $0.99 per share, an increase over the fiscal 2026 annual dividend of $0.94 per share.

## Forward Signals

For the fiscal year ending January 31, 2027, the company projects capital expenditures will be approximately $25 billion to $27 billion, with a focus on technology, supply chain and customer-facing initiatives.

**Known trends**
- We expect continued uncertainty in our business and the global economy due to the following factors: tariffs and trade restrictions; inflationary trends; fluctuations in global currencies; swings in macroeconomic conditions and their effect on consumer confidence; changes in employment trends; volatility in fuel prices; and supply chain pressures, any of which may impact our results.

**Subsequent events**
- In February 2026, the Board of Directors approved a new $30.0 billion share repurchase authorization, which has no expiration date or other restrictions limiting the period over which the Company can make repurchases, and beginning February 23, 2026, replaced the remaining capacity under the prior authorization.
- Effective February 19, 2026, the Company approved the fiscal 2027 annual dividend of $0.99 per share, an increase over the fiscal 2026 annual dividend of $0.94 per share.

> "We expect continued uncertainty in our business and the global economy due to the following factors: tariffs and trade restrictions; inflationary trends; fluctuations in global currencies; swings in macroeconomic conditions and their effect on consumer confidence; changes in employment trends; volatility in fuel prices; and supply chain pressures, any of which may impact our results." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Failure to successfully execute the omnichannel strategy and the cost of investments in eCommerce and technology may adversely affect market position, net sales and financial performance. | Failure to successfully execute our omnichannel strategy and the cost of our investments in eCommerce and technology may materially adversely affect our market position, net sales and financial performance. |
| 2 | General or macroeconomic factors, including tariffs and trade restrictions, inflation, and currency fluctuations, may adversely affect financial performance. | General economic conditions and other economic factors, globally or in one or more of the markets we serve, may adversely affect our financial performance. |
| 3 | Cyber threats are rapidly evolving and the company has experienced cybersecurity incidents, including during fiscal 2026, which could result in regulatory fines, loss of sales, and reputational damage. | As noted above, some of our information systems and those of our third-party service providers have experienced cybersecurity incidents or breaches, including during fiscal 2026, and, although to date they have not had a material adverse effect on our operating results or business, there can be no assurance of a similar result in the future. |
| 4 | The company is involved in a number of legal proceedings and regulatory matters, including opioid-related litigation, which could result in material liabilities. | In Note 9 to our Consolidated Financial Statements, which is captioned "Contingencies" and appears in Part II of this Annual Report on Form 10-K under the caption "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data," we discuss, under the sub-captions "Settlement of Certain Opioid-Related Matters," and "Ongoing Opioid-Related Litigation," certain opioid-related matters, as well as the Prescription Opiate Litigation, and other matters, including certain risks arising therefrom. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Walmart U.S. | $485.6B | $25.2B | +4.4% | 5% operating margin |
| Walmart International | $132.0B | $5.1B | +7.0% | 4% operating margin — Net sales growth was primarily due to positive comparable sales growth across international markets, which includes strong eCommerce growth of $6.3 billion, partially offset by negative fluctuations in currency exchange rates of $2.8 billion. |
| Sam's Club U.S. | $95.5B | $2.4B | +3.2% | 3% operating margin |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt increased to $44.8B ($6.6B short-term borrowings + $3.5B long-term debt due within one year + $34.6B long-term debt) from $39.1B, while cash and cash equivalents rose to $10.7B from $9.0B. Total Walmart shareholders' equity increased to $99.6B from $91.0B.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of $10.7B, plus $15.0B of undrawn committed lines of credit in the U.S. and $2.0B of syndicated and fronted letters of credit available (of which $1.7B was issued). The company believes its sources of liquidity will be sufficient to fund operations, finance investment activities, pay dividends and fund share repurchases for at least the next 12 months and for the foreseeable future.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $41.6B, investing $-26.4B, financing $-13.6B.

Working capital: Current assets $84.9B vs. current liabilities $107.5B (current ratio 0.79x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-01-31: $79.5B vs. $96.6B (0.82x).

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Walmart's fiscal 2026 total revenues rose 4.7% to $713.2B, with consolidated net income of $22.3B and diluted EPS of $2.73, while operating income margin narrowed 13 basis points to 4.2%.

Revenue growth decelerated to 4.7% from 5.1% in the prior year, while net income growth accelerated and operating margin contracted 13 basis points due to elevated liability claims and a one-time PhonePe compensation charge.

- Total revenues increased $32.2B, or 4.7%, to $713.2B, driven by net sales growth of 4.7% to $706.4B.
- Consolidated net income rose $2.1B to $22.3B, and diluted EPS increased to $2.73 from $2.41.
- Operating income as a percentage of net sales decreased 13 basis points to 4.2%, primarily due to higher self-insured general liability claims expense of approximately $0.9B and a $0.7B PhonePe share-based compensation charge.
- Free cash flow increased to $14.9B from $12.7B, as net cash provided by operating activities rose $5.1B to $41.6B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $713,163M | $680,985M | +4.7% | Primarily due to increases in net sales, which increased $31.9 billion or 4.7%, driven by strong positive comparable sales across U.S. segments and international markets. |
| Net sales | $706,413M | $674,538M | +4.7% | Growth was primarily driven by increases in average ticket and transactions, and also reflected growth in unit volumes. |
| Operating income | $29,825M | $29,348M | +1.6% | Operating income as a percentage of net sales decreased 13 basis points primarily due to higher self-insured general liability claims expense and a PhonePe share-based compensation charge. |
| Consolidated net income | $22,270M | $20,157M | +10.5% | Increase was primarily due to net increases in the fair value of equity and other investments combined with higher operating income. |
| Consolidated net income attributable to Walmart | $21,893M | $19,436M | +12.6% | Attributable net income grew faster than consolidated net income as the noncontrolling interest share declined. |
| Diluted net income per common share attributable to Walmart | $2.73 | $2.41 | +13.3% | EPS growth exceeded net income growth as weighted-average diluted shares declined to 8,022 million from 8,081 million. |
| Basic net income per common share attributable to Walmart | $2.74 | $2.42 | +13.2% | Basic EPS increased in line with attributable net income and a lower basic share count. |
| Gross profit as a percentage of net sales | 24.2% | 24.1% | +0.1 ppts | Increase was primarily driven by the Walmart U.S. segment, due to disciplined inventory management, as well as growth in higher margin businesses globally. |
| Operating expenses as a percentage of net sales | 20.9% | 20.7% | +0.2 ppts | Increase was primarily due to higher self-insured general liability claims expense in the U.S. of approximately $0.9 billion, a charge of $0.7 billion related to modification of certain share-based compensation arrangements for the PhonePe subsidiary and increased depreciation. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of $29,825M included a $0.7B non-cash charge related to modification of PhonePe share-based payment arrangements and approximately $0.9B of higher self-insured general liability claims expense. Other (gains) and losses swung to a net gain of $2,075M from a net loss of $794M, primarily driven by changes in the fair value of equity and other investments. The effective income tax rate rose to 24.4% from 23.4%, primarily due to the PhonePe share-based compensation charge, which provided no tax benefit.

Operating cash flow was 1.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $14.9B.

**Red flag:** Other (gains) and losses swung to a $2,075M net gain from a $794M net loss, driven by fair value changes in equity and other investments, contributing to net income growth not tied to core operations.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $7.5B (prior $6.7B), share repurchases $8.1B (prior $4.5B); capital expenditures $26.6B (prior $23.8B).

Capital allocation prioritized higher-return areas focused on automation such as eCommerce, supply chain and store and club investments, with total capital expenditures increasing to support the omnichannel growth strategy. Share repurchases increased, funded primarily through free cash flow, and the Board approved a new $30.0 billion share repurchase authorization in February 2026. The fiscal 2027 annual dividend was approved at $0.99 per share, an increase over the fiscal 2026 annual dividend of $0.94 per share.

Return on equity was 22.0% (prior 21.4%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 7.7% (prior 7.5%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In February 2026, the Board of Directors approved a new $30.0 billion share repurchase authorization, which has no expiration date or other restrictions limiting the period over which the Company can make repurchases, and beginning February 23, 2026, replaced the remaining capacity under the prior authorization.
- Effective February 19, 2026, the Company approved the fiscal 2027 annual dividend of $0.99 per share, an increase over the fiscal 2026 annual dividend of $0.94 per share.

## Forward Signals

For the fiscal year ending January 31, 2027, the Company projects capital expenditures will be approximately $25 billion to $27 billion, with a focus on technology, supply chain and customer-facing initiatives.

**Known trends**
- The Company expects continued uncertainty in its business and the global economy due to tariffs and trade restrictions, inflationary trends, fluctuations in global currencies, swings in macroeconomic conditions and their effect on consumer confidence, changes in employment trends, volatility in fuel prices, and supply chain pressures.
- Less than one third of what the Company sells in the U.S. is imported, with most imports coming from China, Mexico, Vietnam, India and Canada.

**Subsequent events**
- In February 2026, the Board of Directors approved a new $30.0 billion share repurchase authorization, replacing the remaining capacity under the prior authorization.
- Effective February 19, 2026, the Company approved the fiscal 2027 annual dividend of $0.99 per share.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Costco reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $2,192M ($4.93 diluted EPS) on total revenue of $70,527M, with revenue up 11.6% YoY and net income up 15.2% YoY.

Revenue growth accelerated to 12% from 8% in the prior-year quarter, aided by higher gasoline prices and favorable foreign currency, while gross margin percentage declined 21 basis points on a reported basis.

- Total revenue rose to $70,527M from $63,205M, with net sales up 12% and membership fees up 11% to $1,373M.
- Operating income increased to $2,815M from $2,530M; operating margin held at 4.0% while net margin widened to 3.1% from 3.0%.
- Diluted EPS of $4.93 compared with $4.28, with the diluted share count roughly flat at 444,430 thousand shares.
- Gross margin percentage decreased 21 basis points to 11.04%, but excluding gasoline price inflation it was 11.26%, an increase of one basis point.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenue | $70,527M | $63,205M | +11.6% | Net sales increased 12% driven by a 10% increase in comparable sales and sales at 23 net new warehouses opened since the end of the third quarter of 2025. |
| Net sales | $69,154M | $61,965M | +11.6% | The improvement was primarily attributable to an increase in comparable sales of $6,055 or 10% during the third quarter of 2026. |
| Membership fees | $1,373M | $1,240M | +10.7% | Membership fee revenue increased driven by new member sign-ups, membership fee increases and upgrades to Executive Membership. |
| Operating income | $2,815M | $2,530M | +11.3% | Operating income rose as revenue growth outpaced the increase in merchandise costs and SG&A expenses. |
| Net income | $2,192M | $1,903M | +15.2% | Net income increased with the effective tax rate at 25.4%, compared to 26.2%. |
| Diluted EPS | $4.93 | $4.28 | +15.2% | Diluted EPS rose in line with net income, with the weighted average diluted share count roughly flat. |
| Basic EPS | $4.94 | $4.29 | +15.2% | Basic EPS increased consistent with net income growth. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported results include a smaller LIFO charge in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, which positively impacted gross margin by 14 basis points, and the absence of a charge related to a one-time expense for increased employee vacation, which positively impacted gross margin by two basis points. Year-to-date results include a non-recurring legal settlement that positively impacted gross margin by two basis points and a charge related to a tax assessment for prior years that negatively impacted SG&A by one basis point.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital allocation is framed as sustaining and expanding the warehouse base and digital capabilities, with capital expenditures financed from operating cash flow, cash and cash equivalents, and short-term investments. Shareholder returns continued through quarterly dividends and repurchases under the existing authorization, with the remaining amount available under the program at $1,359.

Return on equity was 6.5% (prior 7.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 2.5% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

## Forward Signals

## The Print

Costco reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $2,192M ($4.93 diluted EPS) on total revenue of $70,527M, with revenue up 11.6% YoY and net income up 15.2% YoY.

Revenue growth accelerated to 12% YoY from 8% in the prior-year quarter, with Canada and Other International net sales each up 13%, while gross margin percentage declined 21 basis points on gasoline price inflation.

- Total revenue rose to $70,527M from $63,205M, with net sales up 12% to $69,154M and membership fees up 11% to $1,373M.
- Net income increased to $2,192M ($4.93 diluted EPS) from $1,903M ($4.28 diluted EPS); the effective tax rate was 25.4% versus 26.2%.
- Gross margin percentage decreased 21 basis points to 11.04%, but excluding gasoline price inflation it was 11.26%, up one basis point.
- SG&A expenses as a percentage of net sales decreased 20 basis points to 8.96%, or two basis points lower excluding gasoline price inflation.

## Results That Matter

| Total revenue | $70,527M | $63,205M | +11.6% | Net sales increased 12% to $69,154M, driven by a 10% increase in comparable sales and sales at 23 net new warehouses opened since the end of the third quarter of 2025. |
| Operating income | $2,815M | $2,530M | +11.3% | Operating income rose as revenue growth outpaced the 20 basis point decrease in SG&A expenses as a percentage of net sales. |
| Net income | $2,192M | $1,903M | +15.2% | Net income increased to $2,192, $4.93 per diluted share, compared to $1,903, $4.28 per diluted share. |
| Diluted EPS | $4.93 | $4.28 | +15.2% | Diluted EPS growth matched net income growth, with weighted average diluted shares of 444,430 thousand versus 444,762 thousand. |
| Basic EPS | $4.94 | $4.29 | +15.2% | Basic EPS increased on higher net income and a slightly lower weighted average basic share count. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported operating income of $2,815M included a smaller LIFO charge versus the prior-year quarter, which positively impacted gross margin by 14 basis points, and the absence of a charge related to a one-time expense for increased employee vacation, which positively impacted gross margin by two basis points and SG&A by five basis points. Year-to-date gross margin benefited from a non-recurring legal settlement of two basis points.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Costco reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $2.19B ($4.93 diluted EPS) on total revenue of $70.53B, with revenue up 11.6% YoY and net income up 15.2% YoY.

Revenue growth accelerated to 11.6% YoY from 8.4% in the prior-year quarter, with net income growth of 15.2% outpacing revenue growth, while gross margin percentage declined 21 basis points on gasoline price inflation.

- Total revenue rose 11.6% YoY to $70.53B, driven by a 10% increase in comparable sales and sales at 23 net new warehouses opened since the end of Q3 2025.
- Net income increased 15.2% YoY to $2.19B, with diluted EPS of $4.93 versus $4.28, as operating income rose 11.3% to $2.82B.
- Membership fee revenue increased 11% to $1.37B, primarily driven by new member sign-ups, membership fee increases, and upgrades to Executive Membership.
- Gross margin as a percentage of net sales decreased 21 basis points to 11.04%, but excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation, gross margin percentage was 11.26%, an increase of one basis point.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenue | $70,527M | $63,205M | +11.6% | Net sales increased 12% driven by an increase in comparable sales and sales at 23 net new warehouses opened since the end of the third quarter of 2025. |
| Operating income | $2,815M | $2,530M | +11.3% | Not disclosed—no single driver stated for consolidated operating income; segment results and gross margin/SG&A drivers are discussed separately. |
| Net income | $2,192M | $1,903M | +15.2% | Net income increased to $2,192, $4.93 per diluted share, compared to $1,903, $4.28 per diluted share. |
| Diluted EPS | $4.93 | $4.28 | +15.2% | Diluted EPS growth tracked net income growth; weighted average diluted shares declined slightly to 444,430 thousand from 444,762 thousand. |
| Basic EPS | $4.94 | $4.29 | +15.2% | Not disclosed—no separate driver stated for basic EPS. |
| Gross margin | $7,635M | $6,969M | +9.6% | Gross margin as a percentage of net sales decreased by 21 basis points; excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation on net sales, gross margin percentage was 11.26%, an increase of one basis point. |
| SG&A expenses | $6,193M | $5,679M | +9.1% | SG&A expenses as a percentage of net sales decreased by 20 basis points; excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation, SG&A expenses as a percentage of net sales was 9.14%, a decrease of two basis points. |
| Membership fees | $1,373M | $1,240M | +10.7% | Membership fee revenue increased 11% driven by new member sign-ups, membership fee increases and upgrades to Executive Membership. |
| Net sales | $69,154M | $61,965M | +11.6% | Net sales increased $7,189 or 12% during the third quarter of 2026, primarily attributable to an increase in comparable sales of $6,055 or 10%. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of $2,815M included a smaller LIFO charge in Q3 2026 versus Q3 2025, which positively impacted gross margin by 14 basis points, and the absence of a charge related to a one-time expense for increased employee vacation, which positively impacted gross margin by two basis points. Year-to-date gross margin was positively impacted by a non-recurring legal settlement of two basis points. The effective tax rate of 25.4% for Q3 2026 was favorably impacted by discrete tax benefits related to stock compensation.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital allocation remained shareholder-return focused, with dividends and buybacks funded by operating cash flow; the company also continued to invest in new warehouse openings, remodels, depot network expansion, and digitally-enabled businesses, with capital expenditures expected to be financed with cash from operations, cash and cash equivalents, and short-term investments.

Return on equity was 6.5% (prior 7.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 2.5% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- A quarterly cash dividend of $1.47 per share was declared on April 15, 2026, and paid on May 15, 2026, up from $1.30 per share in the third quarter of 2025.
- The share repurchase program has $1,359 remaining available under the $4,000 authorization, which expires in January 2027.

## Forward Signals

The company stated it is its current intention to spend approximately $6,500 on capital expenditures during fiscal 2026, and plans to open 13 additional new warehouses, including one relocation, in the remainder of fiscal 2026. No earnings or revenue guidance was provided.

**Known trends**
- Government actions in various countries relating to tariffs affect the costs of some of our merchandise. The degree of our exposure is dependent on (among other things) the type of goods, rates imposed, and timing of the tariffs. Higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve our results.
- Our rate of square footage growth is generally higher in many of our foreign markets, due to the smaller base in those markets, and we expect that to continue.

**Subsequent events**
- A quarterly cash dividend of $1.47 per share was declared on April 15, 2026, and paid on May 15, 2026.

> "We believe that our cash and investment positions and operating cash flow, with capacity under existing and available credit agreements, will be sufficient to meet our liquidity and capital requirements for the foreseeable future" — Costco Wholesale Corporation

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tariffs on merchandise could adversely impact results, with exposure dependent on the type of goods, rates imposed, and timing. | Government actions in various countries relating to tariffs affect the costs of some of our merchandise. The degree of our exposure is dependent on (among other things) the type of goods, rates imposed, and timing of the tariffs. Higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve our results. |
| 2 | Multiple class action lawsuits and PAGA actions alleging California and Washington labor code violations, including failure to pay minimum wage, overtime, and provide meal and rest breaks. | In November 2023, a former employee filed a class action against the Company alleging claims under California law for failure to pay minimum wage, failure to pay overtime, failure to provide meal and rest breaks, failure to provide accurate wage statements, failure to reimburse expenses, failure to pay wages when due, and failure to pay sick pay. |
| 3 | Four class actions filed in March 2026 seeking refund of tariffs paid under IEEPA that were passed on to members through higher prices. | In March 2026, four class actions were filed against the Company seeking a refund of tariffs paid by the Company under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (“IEEPA”) that were passed on to members through higher prices. |
| 4 | Two class actions filed in October and November 2025 alleging violations of consumer protection laws arising from the sale of Kirkland Signature tequila products labeled '100% de Agave' but allegedly containing alcohol derived from non-agave sugars. | In October and November 2025, two class actions were filed against the Company alleging violations of consumer protection and other laws arising from the Company’s sale of Kirkland Signature tequila products in the United States |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| United States | $51.4B | $1.9B | +11.0% | 4% operating margin — Segment gross margin percentage decreased, primarily due to a negative impact from core merchandise categories, partially offset by increases in warehouse ancillary and other businesses, a smaller LIFO charge and the absence of a charge related to a one-time expense for increased employee vacation. |
| Other International | $9.7B | $436.0M | +13.0% | 5% operating margin — Gross margin increased, primarily due to increases in core merchandise categories. |
| Canada | $9.4B | $506.0M | +13.1% | 5% operating margin — Segment gross margin percentage increased, primarily due to increases in warehouse ancillary and other businesses, partially offset by decreases in core merchandise categories. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total long-term debt of $5,670M against cash and cash equivalents of $18,946M and total equity of $33,509M; net cash position.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments were $19,996M at May 10, 2026, up from $15,284M at August 31, 2025; borrowing capacity under bank credit facilities was $1,531M, with $96M of short-term borrowings outstanding.

Working capital: Current assets $45.2B vs. current liabilities $42.1B (current ratio 1.07x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-08-31: $38.4B vs. $37.1B (1.03x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt consists of Senior Notes maturing in May 2027, June 2027, April 2030, and April 2032, plus other long-term debt of $684M.
- In March 2026, the Company's Japan subsidiary repaid $69 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Legal Proceedings | The Company has recorded an immaterial accrual with respect to some matters and does not believe any pending claim will have a material adverse effect, but an unfavorable outcome could result in a charge material to an individual fiscal quarter or year. |
| Stock Repurchase Programs | The company repurchased 184,000 shares in Q3 2026 at an average price of $997.47 per share for a total cost of $183M; $1,359M remains available under the $4,000M authorization expiring January 2027. |
| Dividends | A quarterly cash dividend of $1.47 per share was declared on April 15, 2026, and paid on May 15, 2026, up from $1.30 per share in the third quarter of 2025. |
| Segment Reporting | The company operates through three reportable segments: United States, Canada, and Other International, with the CODM using segment revenue, significant expenses, and operating income to evaluate performance. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Boeing returned to profitability in FY2025 with net earnings attributable to shareholders of $2.2B and diluted EPS of $2.48, on revenue of $89.5B, versus a $11.8B loss and ($18.36) per share in 2024.

Boeing moved from a $11.8B net loss in 2024 to $2.2B of net earnings in 2025, aided by the $9.6B Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture gain and higher commercial deliveries, while absorbing $5.3B of 777X and 767 reach-forward losses and completing the $8.4B Spirit AeroSystems acquisition.

- Revenue rose to $89.5B from $66.5B, which management attributes primarily to higher BCA deliveries, lower net unfavorable BDS cumulative contract catch-up adjustments, and higher BGS government and commercial services revenue.
- The swing to profit was driven by a $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture within BGS, partially offset by $5.3B of combined 777X and 767 reach-forward losses at BCA.
- Operating cash flow turned positive at $1.1B from ($12.1B) used in 2024, while free cash flow remained negative at ($1.9B) after $2.9B of capital expenditures.
- Total backlog reached $682.2B at December 31, 2025, up from $521.3B, with contractual backlog of $639.7B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $89,463M | $66,517M | +34.5% | Management attributes the increase primarily to higher revenues at BCA, BDS and BGS. |
| Earnings/(loss) from operations | $4,281M | ($10,707M) | +140.0% | Management attributes the increase primarily to BGS, BDS and BCA, partially offset by a larger loss on Unallocated items, eliminations and other. |
| Net earnings/(loss) attributable to Boeing shareholders | $2,235M | ($11,817M) | +118.9% | Management attributes the improvement to the same segment drivers as operating earnings, including the BGS divestiture gain and lower BDS catch-up charges. |
| Diluted earnings/(loss) per share | $2.48 | ($18.36) | +113.5% | Diluted weighted average shares outstanding rose to 762.3 million from 646.9 million, reflecting 2024 common and mandatory convertible preferred stock issuance and 2025 Spirit share issuance. |
| Operating margins | 4.8% | (16.1)% | +20.9 ppts | Management attributes the margin change to lower charges on BDS fixed-price development programs, partially offset by higher combined reach-forward losses on the 777X and 767 programs at BCA. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported earnings from operations of $4,281M include a $9,672M Gain on dispositions, net, primarily the $9,566M gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture recorded in BGS. Excluding that gain, operating results reflect $5,283M of combined 777X and 767 reach-forward losses at BCA and $802M of losses on BDS's five major fixed-price development programs, primarily KC-46A Tanker ($714M). Non-GAAP core operating earnings were $3,236M versus a core operating loss of ($11,811M) in 2024.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $-1.9B.

**Red flag:** The $9,672M Gain on dispositions, net is a non-cash item added back in the operating cash flow reconciliation, meaning the reported net earnings of $2,238M were substantially aided by a divestiture gain rather than operating cash generation.

**Red flag:** Operating cash flow of $1,065M was well below net earnings of $2,238M, and free cash flow remained negative at ($1,877M) after $2,942M of capital expenditures.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $331.0M; capital expenditures $2.9B (prior $2.2B).

Capital allocation in 2025 was shaped by portfolio actions rather than recurring shareholder returns: the $10.55B all-cash Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture and the $8,371M Spirit Acquisition, which was funded largely through $4,704M of Boeing common stock issued as consideration plus $2,571M of loans, advances and other payments to Spirit and $948M of Spirit debt repaid on its behalf. Capital expenditures rose to $2,942M from $2,230M, and financing activities used $3,763M, including $3,621M of debt repayments, versus $25,209M provided in 2024 when $18,200M of common stock and $5,657M of mandatory convertible preferred stock were issued.

Return on equity was 41.0% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 1.3% (prior -7.6%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Completed the acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc. on December 8, 2025, with total consideration of $8,371M, including 22.98 million Boeing shares exchanged for 117.5 million Spirit shares.
- Closed the sale of portions of the BGS Digital Aviation Solutions business to Thoma Bravo on October 31, 2025 for proceeds of $10,550M, resulting in a gain of $9,566M.

## Forward Signals

No quantitative financial guidance is provided in the filing. Management states production-rate and certification expectations: the 737 program plans to increase the production rate from 42 to 47 per month in 2026 with FAA concurrence, and first delivery of the 777-9 is expected in 2027.

**Known trends**
- We and our suppliers are experiencing inflationary pressures, as well as supply chain disruptions as a result of global supply chain constraints and labor instability.
- After January 30, 2026, the government will enter a partial shutdown unless and until Congress and the President enact either full-year FY26 appropriations bills or an additional Continuing Resolution.
- Collectively, these tariffs, and any retaliatory actions taken by countries in response to the U.S. tariffs, could have a material impact on our financial position, results of operations and/or cash flows.

**Subsequent events**
- The Commerce, Justice Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 6938), enacted January 23, 2026, funded certain federal departments and agencies, including NASA, through FY26.

> "The program plans to increase the production rate from 42 to 47 in 2026 with the concurrence of the FAA." — The Boeing Company

> "We continue to expect first delivery of the 777-9 to occur in 2027." — The Boeing Company

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Fixed-price development programs have generated recurring reach-forward losses; BDS recorded $802M of losses on its five major fixed-price development programs in 2025, primarily KC-46A Tanker ($714M), after $5,013M in 2024. | During 2025, losses incurred on the five major fixed-price development programs totaled $802 million, primarily on KC-46A Tanker ($714 million), compared to losses of $5,013 million during 2024. |
| 2 | The 777X program recorded an incremental reach-forward loss of $4,899M in 2025 after first delivery was delayed to 2027, with a potential engine durability issue identified during inspections. | The impact of these changes on estimated revenues and costs were partially offset by the 100-unit accounting quantity increase, resulting in an incremental reach-forward loss of $4,899 million during 2025. |
| 3 | Labor instability has disrupted production: IAM District 751 struck for 53 days in 2024 and IAM District 837 struck for 101 days in 2025, and SPEEA contracts covering approximately 16,000 employees expire in October 2026. | During 2025, employees represented by IAM District 837, which represents approximately 3,200 employees at our St. Louis area sites, went out on strike for 101 days, disrupting our St. Louis operations and impacting programs including F/A-18, F-15, T-7A, MQ-25 and Weapons. |
| 4 | U.S. government funding lapses and appropriations uncertainty could delay programs and payments; funding for the DoW, NASA and DOT lapsed from October 1 through November 12, 2025, and a partial shutdown is possible after January 30, 2026. | After January 30, 2026, the government will enter a partial shutdown unless and until Congress and the President enact either full-year FY26 appropriations bills or an additional Continuing Resolution. |
| 5 | Tariffs and trade restrictions affect costs and deliveries; certain customers in China temporarily paused accepting aircraft deliveries in 2025 in response to U.S.-China tariff negotiations. | During 2025, certain customers in China temporarily paused accepting delivery of our aircraft in response to ongoing tariff negotiations between the U.S. and China. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BCA | $41.5B | $-7.1B | +81.5% | -17% operating margin — Management attributes the revenue increase to higher deliveries across all programs and the absence of $443M of 737-9 customer considerations related to the January 2024 grounding; the segment recorded combined 777X and 767 reach-forward losses of $5,283M in 2025. |
| BDS | $27.2B | $-128.0M | +13.9% | -0% operating margin — Management attributes the revenue increase primarily to $1,864M lower net unfavorable cumulative contract catch-up adjustments and higher volume; losses on the five major fixed-price development programs totaled $802M, primarily KC-46A Tanker. |
| BGS | $20.9B | $13.5B | +4.9% | 64% operating margin — Management attributes the revenue increase primarily to higher government and commercial services revenue; earnings include the $9,566M gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt rose to $54,098M ($8,461M short-term and current portion plus $45,637M long-term) against cash and cash equivalents of $10,921M and short-term and other investments of $18,479M; shareholders' equity swung to $5,454M from a ($3,908M) deficit, and total equity was $5,457M.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents decreased to $10,921M from $13,801M, while short-term and other investments increased to $18,479M from $12,481M; financing activities used $3,763M, including $3,621M of debt repayments.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $1.1B, investing $499.0M, financing $-3.8B.

Working capital: Current assets $128.5B vs. current liabilities $108.1B (current ratio 1.19x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: $128.0B vs. $97.1B (1.32x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt increased to $8,461M at December 31, 2025 from $1,278M at December 31, 2024.
- Long-term debt was $45,637M at December 31, 2025 compared with $52,586M at December 31, 2024.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Spirit Acquisition completed December 8, 2025 for total consideration of $8,371M, including $4,704M of Boeing common stock and $2,571M of settled loans, advances and other payments to Spirit. | Provisional goodwill of $9,997M was assigned to the BCA segment, and the preliminary purchase price allocation remains subject to adjustment for inventories, property, plant and equipment, goodwill, intangible assets and off-market contracts. |
| Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture closed October 31, 2025 for proceeds of $10,550M, resulting in a gain of $9,566M. | The gain is recorded in Gain on dispositions, net and is the primary driver of the increase in BGS earnings from operations. |
| Net cumulative catch-up adjustments across all long-term contracts decreased revenue by $916M and earnings from operations by $1,377M in 2025, versus $2,794M and $6,562M respectively in 2024. | Significant adjustments during the three years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 included losses on KC-46A Tanker, VC-25B, T-7A Red Hawk, MQ-25, and Commercial Crew programs. |
| The Military Aircraft reporting unit within BDS had goodwill of $1,295 and a negative carrying value at December 31, 2025. | The annual goodwill impairment test as of April 1, 2025 used a qualitative assessment and determined the fair value of each reporting unit substantially exceeded carrying values. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Boeing returned to profitability in FY2025 with net earnings attributable to shareholders of $2.2B and diluted EPS of $2.48, on revenue of $89.5B, after a $11.8B net loss in 2024.

Boeing moved from a $11.8B net loss in 2024 to $2.2B net earnings in 2025, driven by higher deliveries, lower BDS catch-up charges, and a $9.6B divestiture gain, while completing the Spirit acquisition and the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture in the fourth quarter.

- Revenue rose to $89.5B from $66.5B, which management attributes to higher BCA deliveries, lower net unfavorable BDS cumulative catch-up adjustments, and higher BGS government and commercial services revenue.
- The swing to profit was aided by a $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture recorded in Gain on dispositions, net, while BCA still recorded a $7.1B loss from operations.
- Operating cash flow turned positive at $1.1B versus $12.1B used in 2024, but capital expenditures of $2.9B left free cash flow negative at $1.9B.
- Total backlog rose to $682.2B from $521.3B, with contractual backlog of $639.7B and unobligated backlog of $42.5B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $89,463M | $66,517M | +34.5% | Management attributes the increase primarily to higher revenues at BCA, BDS and BGS. |
| Earnings/(loss) from operations | $4,281M | ($10,707M) | +140.0% | Management attributes the increase primarily to BGS, BDS and BCA, partially offset by a larger loss on Unallocated items, eliminations and other. |
| Net earnings/(loss) attributable to Boeing shareholders | $2,235M | ($11,817M) | +118.9% | Management attributes the operating improvement primarily to BGS, BDS and BCA, with BGS including the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture gain. |
| Diluted earnings/(loss) per share | $2.48 | ($18.36) | +113.5% | Diluted weighted average common shares outstanding rose to 762.3 million from 646.9 million, reflecting share issuance during 2024 and 2025. |
| Basic earnings/(loss) per share | $2.49 | ($18.36) | +113.6% | Basic net earnings available to common shareholders was $1,889M after deducting $345M of mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends accumulated during the period. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

GAAP earnings from operations of $4,281M include a $9,672M Gain on dispositions, net, of which $9,566M relates to the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture; excluding the FAS/CAS service cost adjustment of $1,045M, core operating earnings (non-GAAP) were $3,236M. Segment operating earnings of $6,267M include BGS earnings of $13,474M that management states were primarily due to the $9,566M divestiture gain, while BCA recorded a $7,079M loss from operations and BDS a $128M loss from operations.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $-1.9B.

**Red flag:** BCA recorded a $7,079M loss from operations in 2025 and combined reach-forward losses of $5,283M on the 777X and 767 programs, including an incremental $4,899M 777X reach-forward loss in 2025.

**Red flag:** BDS recorded $802M of losses on its five major fixed-price development programs in 2025, primarily KC-46A Tanker ($714M), after $5,013M of such losses in 2024.

**Red flag:** Net cumulative catch-up adjustments across all long-term contracts decreased revenue by $916M and earnings from operations by $1,377M in 2025, with significant adjustments including losses on KC-46A Tanker, VC-25B, T-7A Red Hawk, MQ-25, and Commercial Crew programs.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $331.0M; capital expenditures $2.9B (prior $2.2B).

Capital allocation in 2025 was shaped by portfolio actions rather than recurring shareholder returns: the $10.55B all-cash Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture and the $8,371M Spirit Acquisition, which was funded largely through the exchange of Boeing common stock and the settlement of loans, advances and other payments to Spirit, plus $948M of Spirit debt repaid on Spirit's behalf. Capital expenditures rose to $2,942M from $2,230M, and financing activities used $3,763M, including $3,621M of debt repayments and $331M of mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends, after 2024's $25,209M of financing inflows from common and preferred stock issuance and new borrowings.

Return on equity was 41.0% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 1.3% (prior -7.6%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Completed the acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc. on December 8, 2025, with total consideration of $8,371M, including 22.98 million Boeing shares exchanged for 117.5 million Spirit shares.
- Completed the sale of portions of the BGS segment's Digital Aviation Solutions business to Thoma Bravo on October 31, 2025 for proceeds of $10,550M, resulting in a gain of $9,566M.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide consolidated financial guidance. It states production-rate expectations: the 737 program plans to increase the production rate from 42 to 47 per month in 2026 with the concurrence of the FAA, and the 787 program began increasing the production rate to eight per month during the fourth quarter of 2025. It also states it continues to expect 777-9 first delivery in 2027 and 737-7 and 737-10 certification to occur in 2026.

**Known trends**
- After January 30, 2026, the government will enter a partial shutdown unless and until Congress and the President enact either full-year FY26 appropriations bills or an additional Continuing Resolution.
- We and our suppliers are experiencing inflationary pressures, as well as supply chain disruptions as a result of global supply chain constraints and labor instability.
- Our contracts with the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace, representing approximately 16,000 Boeing employees, are scheduled to expire in October 2026, and could also have a material impact on our financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

**Subsequent events**
- The Commerce, Justice Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 6938), enacted January 23, 2026, funded certain federal departments and agencies, including NASA, through FY26.
- In early 2026, we expect to deliver the last 737-8 aircraft produced prior to 2023.

> "The program plans to increase the production rate from 42 to 47 in 2026 with the concurrence of the FAA." — The Boeing Company

> "We continue to expect first delivery of the 777-9 to occur in 2027." — The Boeing Company

| 2 | The 777X program has incurred repeated reach-forward losses tied to certification and delivery delays; an incremental $4,899M loss was recorded in 2025 and first delivery was delayed to 2027. | The impact of these changes on estimated revenues and costs were partially offset by the 100-unit accounting quantity increase, resulting in an incremental reach-forward loss of $4,899 million during 2025. |
| 3 | Labor instability has disrupted production; IAM District 751 struck for 53 days in 2024 and IAM District 837 struck for 101 days in 2025, and SPEEA contracts expire in October 2026. | During 2025, employees represented by IAM District 837, which represents approximately 3,200 employees at our St. Louis area sites, went out on strike for 101 days, disrupting our St. Louis operations and impacting programs including F/A-18, F-15, T-7A, MQ-25 and Weapons. |
| 4 | U.S. government funding uncertainty could disrupt operations; funding lapsed from October 1 through November 12, 2025, and after January 30, 2026 the government will enter a partial shutdown unless full-year FY26 appropriations or an additional Continuing Resolution are enacted. | After January 30, 2026, the government will enter a partial shutdown unless and until Congress and the President enact either full-year FY26 appropriations bills or an additional Continuing Resolution. |
| 5 | Tariffs and trade restrictions could increase costs and reduce demand; certain customers in China temporarily paused accepting aircraft deliveries during 2025 in response to U.S.-China tariff negotiations. | During 2025, certain customers in China temporarily paused accepting delivery of our aircraft in response to ongoing tariff negotiations between the U.S. and China. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BCA | $41.5B | $-7.1B | +81.5% | -17% operating margin — Management attributes the revenue increase primarily to higher deliveries across all programs and the absence of $443 million of 737-9 customer considerations related to the January 2024 grounding; the loss from operations narrowed on higher deliveries, the absence of those considerations, lower abnormal production costs and lower research and development costs, partially offset by higher combined reach-forward losses on the 777X and 767 programs and lower program margins. |
| BDS | $27.2B | $-128.0M | +13.9% | -0% operating margin — Management attributes the revenue increase primarily to $1,864 million lower net unfavorable cumulative contract catch-up adjustments and higher volume; the loss from operations narrowed primarily due to lower net unfavorable cumulative contract catch-up adjustments of $5,196 million compared to 2024, with losses on the five major fixed-price development programs totaling $802 million in 2025. |
| BGS | $20.9B | $13.5B | +4.9% | 64% operating margin — Management attributes the revenue increase primarily to higher government and commercial services revenue; earnings from operations increased primarily due to a 2025 gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture of $9,566 million. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Long-term debt was $45,637M at December 31, 2025 (versus $52,586M at December 31, 2024), with short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt of $8,461M (versus $1,278M), against cash and cash equivalents of $10,921M (versus $13,801M) and short-term and other investments of $18,479M; total shareholders' equity was $5,454M, up from a $3,908M deficit at December 31, 2024.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents decreased to $10,921M from $13,801M, and the filing reports net cash provided by operating activities of $1,065M in 2025 versus $12,080M used in 2024; financing activities used $3,763M in 2025, including $3,621M of debt repayments and $331M of mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $1.1B, investing $499.0M, financing $-3.8B.

Working capital: Current assets $128.5B vs. current liabilities $108.1B (current ratio 1.19x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: $128.0B vs. $97.1B (1.32x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt increased to $8,461M at December 31, 2025 from $1,278M at December 31, 2024.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Boeing returned to profitability in FY2025 with net earnings attributable to shareholders of $2,235M and diluted EPS of $2.48, on revenue of $89,463M, aided by a $9,566M gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture.

The filing reflects a swing from a $11,817M net loss in 2024 to $2,235M net earnings in 2025, driven by higher deliveries, lower BDS catch-up charges, and a $9,566M divestiture gain, alongside the December 2025 Spirit acquisition and continued 777X and 767 reach-forward losses.

- Revenue rose to $89,463M from $66,517M, which management attributes to higher BCA deliveries, lower net unfavorable BDS cumulative catch-up adjustments, and higher BGS government and commercial services revenue.
- Net earnings attributable to Boeing shareholders swung to $2,235M from a $11,817M loss, and diluted EPS swung to $2.48 from ($18.36).
- Operating cash flow was $1,065M versus ($12,080M) in 2024, while free cash flow remained negative at ($1,877M).
- Total backlog rose to $682,207M from $521,336M, with BCA backlog at $567,290M.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenues | $89,463M | $66,517M | +34.5% | Management attributes the increase primarily to higher revenues at BCA, BDS and BGS. |
| Earnings/(loss) from operations | $4,281M | ($10,707M) | +140.0% | Management attributes the increase primarily to BGS, BDS and BCA, partially offset by a higher loss on Unallocated items, eliminations and other. |
| Net earnings/(loss) attributable to Boeing shareholders | $2,235M | ($11,817M) | +118.9% | Not disclosed |
| Diluted earnings/(loss) per share | $2.48 | ($18.36) | +113.5% | Not disclosed |
| Basic earnings/(loss) per share | $2.49 | ($18.36) | +113.6% | Not disclosed |
| Operating margins | 4.8% | (16.1)% | +20.9 ppts | Not disclosed |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

GAAP earnings from operations of $4,281M include a $9,672M Gain on dispositions, net, primarily the $9,566M gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture recorded in the BGS segment. Non-GAAP core operating earnings were $3,236M, which exclude the FAS/CAS service cost adjustment of $1,045M. Segment operating earnings of $6,267M include the BGS gain, while BCA and BDS reported operating losses.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $-1.9B.

**Red flag:** GAAP operating income of $4,281M includes a $9,672M gain on dispositions, net, without which operating results would be a loss.

**Red flag:** BCA recorded combined reach-forward losses of $5,283M on the 777X and 767 programs in 2025, up from $4,079M in 2024.

**Red flag:** Free cash flow remained negative at ($1,877M) despite net earnings of $2,235M.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $331.0M; capital expenditures $2.9B (prior $2.2B).

Capital allocation in 2025 was shaped by portfolio actions: the $10,550M all-cash Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture and the Spirit Acquisition, in which approximately $4.7B of Boeing shares were exchanged and certain Spirit debt and obligations were paid off or assumed. Financing cash flow turned to a net outflow after 2024's large equity and mandatory convertible preferred stock issuances. Dividends paid were on the mandatory convertible preferred stock.

Return on equity was 41.0% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 1.3% (prior -7.6%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Completed the acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc. on December 8, 2025, exchanging approximately $4.7B of Boeing shares for all of Spirit's outstanding shares.
- Completed the divestiture of portions of the BGS Digital Aviation Solutions business to Thoma Bravo for proceeds of $10,550M on October 31, 2025.

## Forward Signals

No quantitative financial guidance is provided in the filing. Management states production rate plans and certification timing expectations, including a planned 737 production rate increase from 42 to 47 per month in 2026 with FAA concurrence and first 777-9 delivery expected in 2027.

**Known trends**
- The 737 program plans to increase the production rate from 42 to 47 in 2026 with the concurrence of the FAA, and is planning for additional production rate increases beyond 47 per month as well as adding a 737 production line.
- After January 30, 2026, the government will enter a partial shutdown unless and until Congress and the President enact either full-year FY26 appropriations bills or an additional Continuing Resolution.
- The 777X program expects first delivery of the 777-9 to occur in 2027, with first delivery of the 777-8 Freighter approximately two years later and the 777-8 passenger aircraft not expected before 2030.

**Subsequent events**
- The Commerce, Justice Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 6938), enacted January 23, 2026, funded certain federal departments and agencies, including NASA, through FY26.

> "The program plans to increase the production rate from 42 to 47 in 2026 with the concurrence of the FAA." — The Boeing Company

> "We continue to expect first delivery of the 777-9 to occur in 2027." — The Boeing Company

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Fixed-price development programs have generated reach-forward losses; BDS recorded $802M of losses on its five major fixed-price development programs in 2025, primarily KC-46A Tanker ($714M), and risk remains of additional reach-forward losses. | During 2025, losses incurred on the five major fixed-price development programs totaled $802 million, primarily on KC-46A Tanker ($714 million), compared to losses of $5,013 million during 2024. |
| 2 | The 777X program recognized an incremental reach-forward loss of $4,899M in 2025 after first delivery of the 777-9 was delayed to 2027 and production rate plans were slowed. | The impact of these changes on estimated revenues and costs were partially offset by the 100-unit accounting quantity increase, resulting in an incremental reach-forward loss of $4,899 million during 2025. |
| 3 | Labor instability: IAM District 837 represented approximately 3,200 employees in a 101-day work stoppage in 2025, and Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace contracts representing approximately 16,000 employees expire in October 2026. | During 2025, employees represented by IAM District 837, which represents approximately 3,200 employees at our St. Louis area sites, went out on strike for 101 days, disrupting our St. Louis operations and impacting programs including F/A-18, F-15, T-7A, MQ-25 and Weapons. |
| 4 | Tariffs and trade restrictions: certain customers in China temporarily paused accepting aircraft deliveries in 2025 in response to U.S.-China tariff negotiations, and the U.S. maintains tariffs on aluminum, steel and copper imports. | During 2025, certain customers in China temporarily paused accepting delivery of our aircraft in response to ongoing tariff negotiations between the U.S. and China. |
| 5 | U.S. government funding lapse: funding for the DoW, NASA and the DOT lapsed from October 1 through November 12, 2025, and a partial shutdown is possible after January 30, 2026. | From October 1 through November 12, 2025, funding for U.S. government departments and agencies, including the Department of War (DoW), the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), and the Department of Transportation (DOT), including the FAA, had lapsed. |

## Segments

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Intel reported Q1 2026 revenue of $13.6B (up 7.2% YoY) but a net loss attributable to Intel of $3.7B (-$0.73 diluted EPS), driven by a $3.9B non-cash goodwill impairment on the Mobileye reporting unit.

The quarter shifted from a modest operating loss to a $3.1B operating loss on a $3.9B non-cash Mobileye goodwill impairment, while revenue and gross margin improved YoY.

- Revenue rose to $13,577M from $12,667M YoY, with gross margin expanding to 39.4% from 36.9%.
- Net loss attributable to Intel widened to $3,728M (-$0.73 diluted EPS) from $821M (-$0.19) YoY, reflecting $4,070M of restructuring and other charges including the $3.9B Mobileye goodwill impairment.
- Operating cash flow was $1,096M versus $813M YoY; free cash flow remained negative at -$2,540M as capital expenditures totaled $3,636M.
- In April 2026, Intel reacquired Apollo's 49% minority interest in Ireland SCIP for approximately $14.2B, funded with cash, short-term investments, and a $6.5B term loan.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net revenue | $13,577M | $12,667M | +7.2% | Primarily driven by higher Intel Products revenue, with DCAI revenue up 22% on higher server ASPs. |
| Gross profit | $5,347M | $4,672M | +14.4% | Primarily driven by $771 million of lower period charges primarily resulting from Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges in Q1 2025. |
| Operating income (loss) | -$3,136M | -$301M | −941.9% | Reflects $4,070M of restructuring and other charges, including $3.9B of non-cash goodwill impairment charges. |
| Net income (loss) attributable to Intel | -$3,728M | -$821M | −354.1% | Impacted by the Mobileye goodwill impairment and a $1.1 billion net loss from the change in fair value of the Escrowed Shares derivative liability. |
| Earnings (loss) per share attributable to Intel—diluted | -$0.73 | -$0.19 | −284.2% | Weighted average diluted shares rose to 5,083 million from 4,343 million YoY. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported operating loss of $3,136M includes $4,070M of restructuring and other charges, of which $3,965M were asset impairment charges (substantially the $3.9B Mobileye goodwill impairment). Excluding these, segment operating income was $4,058M for Intel Products, offset by a $2,437M Intel Foundry operating loss. Net loss also includes a $1,090M mark-to-market loss on Escrowed Shares and a $223M benefit from the change in fair value of Ireland SCIP liquidated damages.

Operating cash flow was positive despite a net loss; free cash flow of $-2.5B.

**Red flag:** Goodwill impairment of $3.9B on the Mobileye reporting unit; an additional 1% increase in the discount rate would have resulted in a further impairment of approximately $682 million.

**Red flag:** Escrowed Shares derivative liability fair value rose to $3.6B at March 28, 2026 from $2.7B at December 27, 2025, with a $1.1B mark-to-market loss recognized in the quarter.

**Red flag:** Inventories increased to $12,426M from $11,618M at December 27, 2025, with work in process rising to $9,004M from $7,840M.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $3.6B (prior $5.2B).

Capital expenditures of $3,636M exceeded operating cash flow of $1,096M, resulting in negative free cash flow; the company funded the $14.2B Ireland SCIP minority interest repurchase through existing cash, short-term investments, and a $6.5B term loan, and intends to refinance the term loan subject to market conditions. No shares were repurchased during the quarter.

Return on equity was -3.3% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets -1.8% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In April 2026, Intel reacquired Apollo's 49% minority ownership interest in Ireland SCIP for approximately $14.2 billion, funded with cash, short-term investments, and a $6.5 billion term loan.
- Mobileye closed the acquisition of Mentee Robotics on February 3, 2026 for a purchase price of $637 million, consisting primarily of $596 million in cash.

## Forward Signals

No formal financial guidance was provided in the filing. Management stated it expects supply constraints to persist throughout 2026 and that total R&D and MG&A expenses are expected to decrease in 2026 relative to recent historical periods.

**Known trends**
- Market demand exceeded available product supply in Q1 2026 due to internal and external supply constraints, and management expects these supply constraints to persist throughout 2026.
- Industry-wide shortages of substrates, memory and other critical components may further limit the ability to fully meet customer demand.
- If sufficient committed demand for Intel 14A is not secured, it may not be economical to develop and manufacture Intel 14A and successor leading-edge nodes on a go-forward basis.

**Subsequent events**
- On April 8, 2026, Intel acquired Apollo's 49% minority ownership interest in Ireland SCIP for approximately $14.2 billion, funded with cash, short-term investments, and a $6.5 billion 364-day senior unsecured term loan facility with an interest rate of 4.79%.
- In April 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce removed a stockholder derivative lawsuit challenging the Warrant and Common Stock Agreement to the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware.

> "We expect these supply constraints to persist throughout 2026, and industry‑wide shortages of substrates, memory and other critical components may further limit our ability to fully meet customer demand." — Intel Management

> "if we are unable to secure sufficient committed demand for Intel 14A through product design wins with potential significant external customers and our Intel products roadmap, we face the prospect that it will not be economical to develop and manufacture Intel 14A and successor leading-edge nodes on a go-forward basis" — Intel Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Goodwill impairment risk on the Mobileye reporting unit; a further 1% increase in the discount rate would have resulted in an additional impairment of approximately $682 million. | an additional 1% increase in the discount rate would have resulted in a further impairment of our Mobileye reporting unit's goodwill of approximately $682 million in the first quarter of 2026 |
| 2 | Geopolitical conflict risk: Iranian strikes on energy fields in Qatar caused a global helium shortage essential to semiconductor manufacturing, and Intel was named near the top of a list of U.S. companies whose Middle East facilities Iran indicated it would target. | In late March 2026, Iran published a list of U.S. companies with operations in the Middle East whose facilities they indicated they would target in retaliation for continued strikes on Iran, with Intel being near the top of that list. |
| 3 | Legal contingencies: accrued liabilities of $1.0 billion related to VLSI litigation and $310 million related to an EC-imposed fine as of March 28, 2026. | As of March 28, 2026, we have accrued liabilities of $1.0 billion related to litigation involving VLSI and $310 million, including revaluation effects and accrued interest, related to an EC-imposed fine |
| 4 | Ireland SCIP delay-related liquidated damages: required to substantially complete construction of Fab 34 or pay delay-related liquidated damages to Apollo beginning in the second half of 2026, not to exceed $1.1 billion in total. | we were required to substantially complete construction of Fab 34 in accordance with contractual parameters and timelines or we would be required to pay delay-related liquidated damages to Apollo, the other investor, beginning in the second half of 2026, not to exceed $1.1 billion in total |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intel Products | $12.8B | $4.1B | +8.7% | 32% operating margin — Revenue increased on higher DCAI revenue driven by a 27% increase in server ASPs, partially offset by a 5% decrease in server volume; CCG revenue rose on a 16% increase in client ASPs partially offset by a 13% decrease in volume. |
| Client Computing | $7.7B | $2.5B | +1.3% | 33% operating margin — Client revenue (notebook and desktop) was $6.6 billion, up $54 million, primarily driven by a 16% increase in ASPs from a higher mix of premium products and demand-based pricing actions, partially offset by a 13% decrease in volume. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Intel reported Q1 2026 net loss attributable to Intel of $(3,728)M ($(0.73) diluted EPS) on net revenue of $13,577M, with the loss driven substantially by $3.9B of non-cash goodwill impairment charges related to the Mobileye reporting unit.

The quarter's results were reshaped by a $3.9B non-cash Mobileye goodwill impairment and $4,070M of total restructuring and other charges, alongside a $1.1B mark-to-market loss on the Escrowed Shares derivative liability, versus a prior-year quarter with minimal such charges.

- Net revenue rose 7.2% YoY to $13,577M from $12,667M, while gross margin expanded to 39.4% from 36.9%.
- Net loss attributable to Intel widened to $(3,728)M from $(821)M, and diluted EPS was $(0.73) versus $(0.19), reflecting $4,070M of restructuring and other charges including $3.9B of non-cash goodwill impairment.
- Operating cash flow was $1,096M versus $813M, and free cash flow (OCF less CapEx) was $(2,540)M versus $(4,370)M.
- In April 2026, Intel reacquired Apollo's 49% minority ownership interest in Ireland SCIP for approximately $14.2B, funded with existing cash, short-term investments and a $6.5B term loan.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net revenue | $13,577M | $12,667M | +7.2% | Management attributes the increase primarily to higher Intel Products revenue, driven by a 22% increase in DCAI revenue from higher server ASPs. |
| Gross profit | $5,347M | $4,672M | +14.4% | Management attributes the increase primarily to $771 million of lower period charges primarily resulting from Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges in Q1 2025. |
| Operating income (loss) | $(3,136)M | $(301)M | −941.9% | The change reflects $4,070M of restructuring and other charges in Q1 2026, including $3.9B of non-cash goodwill impairment, versus $156M in the prior-year quarter. |
| Net income (loss) attributable to Intel | $(3,728)M | $(821)M | −354.1% | The wider loss reflects the goodwill impairment and restructuring charges, partially offset by higher gross profit. |
| Earnings (loss) per share attributable to Intel—diluted | $(0.73) | $(0.19) | −284.2% | Weighted average diluted shares were 5,083 million versus 4,343 million; due to net losses, potentially dilutive securities had an anti-dilutive effect and were excluded. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported operating loss of $(3,136)M includes $4,070M of restructuring and other charges, of which $3,965M were asset impairment charges (including $3.9B of non-cash Mobileye goodwill impairment). Excluding these, segment operating income was $4,058M for Intel Products, $(2,437)M for Intel Foundry, and $102M for All Other. Interest and other, net of $(738)M included a $1.1B mark-to-market loss on the Escrowed Shares derivative liability, partially offset by a $223M benefit from the change in fair value of Ireland SCIP liquidated damage provisions.

Operating cash flow was positive despite a net loss; free cash flow of $-2.5B.

**Red flag:** Net loss attributable to Intel of $(3,728)M included a $3.9B non-cash goodwill impairment charge related to the Mobileye reporting unit, and the filing states the unit may become subject to further impairment in future periods.

**Red flag:** Interest and other, net included a $1.1B net loss from the change in fair value of the Escrowed Shares derivative liability, with the derivative liability fair value rising to $3.6B at March 28, 2026 from $2.7B at December 27, 2025.

**Red flag:** The company recorded a $335M tax provision on a pre-tax loss of $(3,946)M, with management stating it was not able to benefit from current year domestic losses due to the domestic valuation allowance.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $3.6B (prior $5.2B).

Capital allocation in the quarter reflected continued investment in manufacturing and process technology alongside restructuring actions; capital expenditures were $3,636M, and the company settled $1.5B of senior notes due February 2026. In April 2026, Intel used a combination of existing cash, short-term investments and a $6.5B term loan to repurchase Apollo's 49% minority interest in Ireland SCIP for approximately $14.2B, and stated it intends to refinance the term loan facility, subject to market conditions.

Return on equity was -3.3% (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets -1.8% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In April 2026, Intel reacquired Apollo's 49% minority ownership interest in Ireland SCIP for aggregate cash consideration of approximately $14.2 billion, funded through existing cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments and a $6.5 billion term loan facility.
- Intel amended its 364-day $5.0 billion credit facility agreement to a three-year $3.0 billion credit facility maturing January 2029.
- No shares were repurchased during the quarter; as of March 28, 2026, $7.2 billion remained available under the repurchase authorization.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide quantitative revenue or EPS guidance. Management states it expects supply constraints to persist throughout 2026, that it expects total R&D and MG&A expenses to decrease in 2026 relative to recent historical periods, and that it anticipates net income attributable to non-controlling interests in 2026 will slightly decrease compared to 2025.

**Known trends**
- Market demand exceeded available product supply in Q1 2026 due to internal and external supply constraints, and management expects these supply constraints to persist at least through the first half of 2026 for CCG and throughout the remainder of 2026 for DCAI.
- Industry-wide shortages of substrates, memory and other critical components may further limit the company's ability to fully meet customer demand.
- If Intel is unable to secure sufficient committed demand for Intel 14A through product design wins with potential significant external customers and its Intel products roadmap, it faces the prospect that it will not be economical to develop and manufacture Intel 14A and successor leading-edge nodes on a go-forward basis.

**Subsequent events**
- On April 8, 2026, Intel acquired from Apollo its 49% minority ownership interest in Ireland SCIP for aggregate cash consideration of approximately $14.2 billion, funded through existing cash and short-term investments and a $6.5 billion term loan facility.
- In April 2026, Intel executed and drew on a $6.5 billion 364-day senior unsecured term loan facility with an interest rate of 4.79%.
