| Change in accounting principle for payment stablecoins | Effective December 31, 2025, the company voluntarily elected to change its method of accounting for payment stablecoins to classify them as cash equivalents and apply its crypto lending, borrowing, and collateral policies; the change was applied retrospectively with no effect on previously reported total assets, total liabilities, equity, net income, or earnings per share. |
| Revision of revenue presentation for corporate payment stablecoin balances | Revenue earned on corporate payment stablecoin balances is now presented in Other revenue rather than Net revenue, with no impact to Total revenue; $23.5 million for Q1 2025 was reclassified. |
| Deribit acquisition | On August 14, 2025, the company acquired Deribit for total consideration of $4.3 billion, consisting of $721.5 million in cash and $3.57 billion in Class A common stock, with goodwill of $2.82 billion and intangible assets of $1.39 billion. |
| Share repurchase program | In January 2026, the Board approved a $2.0 billion increase in the authorization under the Repurchase Program from $2.0 billion to $4.0 billion; as of March 31, 2026, $1.9 billion had been utilized to repurchase 6,278,390 shares, and $2.1 billion remained available. |

## The Print

Beyond Meat reported Q1 2026 net loss of $28.5M (diluted EPS -$0.06) on net revenues of $58.2M, a 15.3% YoY decline, while gross margin turned positive at 3.4% from a prior-year gross loss.

The quarter marks a return to positive gross margin and a materially smaller net loss versus the prior-year period, alongside continued revenue contraction and a shift toward a broader plant-based protein portfolio.

- Net revenues fell 15.3% YoY to $58.2M, driven by a 19.5% decrease in volume of products sold, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound.
- Gross profit swung to $2.0M (3.4% margin) from a $6.9M gross loss (-10.1% margin) in the prior-year period, a 1,350 basis point improvement.
- Net loss narrowed to $28.5M from $61.1M, aided by $12.6M in total other income, net, including an $11.9M non-cash derivative remeasurement gain and $6.1M gain on debt extinguishment.
- Operating cash outflow improved to $5.0M from $26.1M, and free cash flow (OCF minus CapEx) was -$7.6M versus -$30.6M a year earlier.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net revenues | $58,206 thousand | $68,731 thousand | −15.3% | Management attributes the decline primarily to a 19.5% decrease in volume of products sold, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound. |
| Gross profit (loss) | $1,985 thousand | $(6,926) thousand | +128.7% | Management states gross profit and gross margin were positively impacted by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound and a 7.6% decrease in cost of goods sold per pound. |
| Gross margin | 3.4% | (10.1)% | +13.5 ppts | The decrease in cost of goods sold per pound primarily reflected lower inventory provision and reduced manufacturing expenses, including depreciation, partially offset by increased materials costs. |
| Loss from operations | $(41,104) thousand | $(64,370) thousand | +36.1% | The reduction in loss from operations was primarily driven by higher gross profit reflecting an increase in net revenue per pound and a decrease in cost per pound, as well as lower research and development expenses and reduced SG&A expenses. |
| Net loss | $(28,482) thousand | $(61,087) thousand | +53.4% | The decrease in net loss was primarily driven by the decrease in loss from operations, and the increase in Total other income (expense), net. |
| Net loss per share available to common stockholders—basic and diluted | $(0.06) | $(0.80) | +92.5% | The per-share improvement reflects the smaller net loss and a substantially larger weighted average share count of 455,272,616 versus 76,194,916 in the prior-year period. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net loss of $28.5M included $12.6M in total other income, net, comprising an $11.9M non-cash gain from remeasurement of derivative liability, $6.1M gain on debt extinguishment, $1.5M interest income and $1.3M gain from remeasurement of warrant liability, partially offset by $6.7M interest expense and $1.3M net realized and unrealized foreign currency transaction losses. Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes these items, was -$27.8M versus -$50.5M in the prior-year period.

Free cash flow of $-7.6M.

**Red flag:** The company corrected previously issued interim financial statements for the three months ended March 29, 2025, related to inventory valuation and debt issuance costs, which increased the prior-period net loss by $8.2M.

**Red flag:** The company failed to timely deliver certain audited annual financial statements to its lender by March 31, 2026, resulting in a default under the Loan and Security Agreement that was subsequently remedied upon filing of the 2025 Form 10-K.

**Red flag:** The company received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on March 4, 2026 regarding the minimum bid price requirement, which if not satisfied could result in delisting.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $2.5M (prior $4.5M).

Capital allocation in the quarter was directed toward sustaining operations and managing the capital structure rather than shareholder returns; the company made no dividend or buyback payments and instead used cash for capital expenditures, finance lease obligations and tax withholding on equity award settlements, while continuing to rely on PIK interest elections on its 2030 Notes and Delayed Draw Term Loans to preserve cash.

Return on assets -4.9% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- The company issued 5,315,857 shares of common stock upon conversion of $6.2M aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes during the quarter, and subsequent to quarter end an additional $62.6M aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes converted into 52,092,284 shares.
- On May 1, 2026, the aggregate remaining principal amount of the 2030 Notes was increased by approximately $10.4M in PIK interest at a rate of 9.5% for the period from October 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026.
- On April 15, 2026, the company entered into a ten-year Distribution Agreement with Big Geyser, Inc. as exclusive distributor of its Beyond Immerse beverage line in the northeast United States.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide quantitative revenue or earnings guidance. Management states it expects research and development expenses in 2026 to decrease compared to 2025 levels, expects interest expense to increase from current levels in 2026, expects to continue to make the PIK election throughout the term of the 2030 Notes, and expects to record significant mark-to-market adjustments from remeasurement of derivatives and other liabilities carried at fair value at each reporting period.

**Known trends**
- Demand in the plant-based meat category and for the company's products has continued to decline persistently over the past three years, particularly in the refrigerated subsegment.
- The company expects to continue to operate at a loss for the foreseeable future and may seek to raise additional capital through equity and/or debt securities.
- The company expects to experience greater demand for certain products during the U.S. summer grilling season, though it states it is unable to assess the ultimate impact of seasonality given current uncertainty.

**Subsequent events**
- Subsequent to quarter end, an additional $62.6M in aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes were converted into 52,092,284 shares of common stock, with 3,869,808 anti-dilution RSUs issued and 2,641,921 shares reserved for anti-dilution increases with respect to PSU awards.
- On May 1, 2026, the aggregate remaining principal amount of the 2030 Notes was increased by approximately $10.4M in PIK interest at a rate of 9.5%.
- On April 15, 2026, the company entered into a Distribution Agreement with Big Geyser, Inc. for the Beyond Immerse beverage line with an initial term of ten years.
- Effective May 4, 2026, the company hired the son of Seth Goldman, Chair of the Board of Directors, as Senior Manager of Community Engagement with a base salary of $130,000 and a target annual bonus of 10%.

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt includes $300.5M carrying amount of 2030 Notes, $81.7M Delayed Draw Term Loans, net, $29.5M of 2027 Notes (current), $75.7M finance lease liabilities and a $26.1M 2030 Notes Embedded Derivative liability, against $191.0M in unrestricted cash and cash equivalents and $14.8M in restricted cash. Total stockholders' deficit widened to $(21.1)M from $(1.0)M at December 31, 2025.

Liquidity: The company had $191.0M in unrestricted cash and cash equivalents and $14.8M in restricted cash as of March 28, 2026, with no amounts available under the Delayed Draw Term Loan Facility. Management states existing cash balances are sufficient to fund operations and foreseeable cash requirements through the next twelve months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $-5.0M, investing $-1.8M, financing $-4.5M.

Working capital: Current assets $311.0M vs. current liabilities $109.0M (current ratio 2.85x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-12-31: $341.5M vs. $74.9M (4.56x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- The 2030 Notes Indenture includes a covenant requiring minimum liquidity of $15.0 million, to be tested quarterly, and a cap of $60.0 million on the amount of cash that can be used to repay the 2027 Notes at maturity.
- The Loan and Security Agreement requires the company to maintain liquidity of at least $15.0 million and does not permit cash interest payments on subordinated and unsecured debt to exceed $20.0 million in any fiscal year.
- The Delayed Draw Term Loans mature on February 7, 2030, extendable with lender consent to no later than May 7, 2035, and accrue interest at 12.0% per annum (17.5% after the Initial Maturity Date if extended).
- The 2030 Notes mature on October 15, 2030, bear interest at 7.00% per annum (or 9.50% PIK at the company's option), and are convertible at approximately $1.7459 per share.

## The Print

Beyond Meat reported Q1 2026 net revenues of $58.2M (down 15.3% YoY) and a net loss of $28.5M, or $(0.06) per diluted share, versus a $(0.80) loss a year earlier.

The quarter shifted from a gross loss to a positive gross margin and a smaller operating loss, while the balance sheet moved further into stockholders' deficit and the company lost access to its ATM Program.

- Net revenues fell 15.3% YoY to $58.2M on a 19.5% decline in volume of products sold, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound.
- Gross margin turned positive at 3.4% from a (10.1)% gross margin loss, and net loss narrowed to $28.5M from $61.1M, aided by $12.6M of total other income, net.
- Net cash used in operating activities improved to $(5.0)M from $(26.1)M, and free cash flow was $(7.6)M versus $(30.6)M a year earlier.
- Stockholders' deficit widened to $(21.1)M from $(1.0)M at December 31, 2025, and the company disclosed it no longer satisfies Form S-3 eligibility and cannot access its ATM Program.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net revenues | $58,206 thousand | $68,731 thousand | −15.3% | Management attributes the decline primarily to a 19.5% decrease in volume of products sold, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound. |
| Gross profit (loss) | $1,985 thousand | $(6,926) thousand | +128.7% | Management states gross profit and gross margin were positively impacted by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound and a (7.6)% decrease in cost of goods sold per pound. |
| Loss from operations | $(41,104) thousand | $(64,370) thousand | +36.1% | Management attributes the reduction to higher gross profit, lower research and development expenses, and reduced SG&A expenses primarily due to lower marketing, legal, and salary and related expenses. |
| Net loss | $(28,482) thousand | $(61,087) thousand | +53.4% | Management attributes the decrease in net loss primarily to the decrease in loss from operations and the increase in Total other income (expense), net. |
| Net loss per share available to common stockholders—basic and diluted | $(0.06) | $(0.80) | +92.5% | The per-share loss narrowed alongside the smaller net loss, with weighted average common shares outstanding—basic and diluted rising to 455,272,616 from 76,194,916. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net loss of $(28.5)M included $12.6M of total other income, net, consisting primarily of an $11.9M non-cash gain from remeasurement of derivative liability, $6.1M gain on debt extinguishment, $1.5M interest income, and $1.3M gain from remeasurement of warrant liability, partially offset by $(6.7)M interest expense and $(1.3)M net realized and unrealized foreign currency transaction losses. Adjusted EBITDA was $(27.8)M versus $(50.5)M a year earlier.

Free cash flow of $-7.6M.

**Red flag:** The company corrected previously issued interim financial statements for the three months ended March 29, 2025 relating to inventory valuation and debt issuance costs, which increased the reported prior-period net loss to $(61.1)M from $(52.9)M as previously reported.

**Red flag:** The company disclosed it was in default under the Loan and Security Agreement for failing to timely deliver certain audited annual financial statements by March 31, 2026, a default it states was remedied upon filing of the 2025 Form 10-K on April 9, 2026.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $2.5M (prior $4.5M).

Capital allocation in the period was directed toward sustaining operations and servicing a debt structure that has been restructured, with capital expenditures declining versus the prior-year period and financing outflows tied to equity-award withholding taxes and finance lease payments. The company states it may seek to raise additional capital through equity and/or debt securities, which it notes could result in additional dilution.

Return on assets -4.9% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Subsequent to the quarter, an additional $62.6 million in aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes were converted into shares of common stock, with 52,092,284 Conversion Shares issued to converting noteholders.
- On April 15, 2026, the company entered into a ten-year Distribution Agreement with Big Geyser, Inc. as exclusive distributor of its Beyond Immerse beverage line in a defined northeast U.S. territory.

## Forward Signals

No quantitative revenue or earnings guidance was provided. Management states it expects to continue to operate at a loss for the foreseeable future and that it expects research and development expenses in 2026 to decrease compared to 2025 levels.

**Known trends**
- Management states demand for plant-based meat products has continued to decline persistently over the past three years and that it expects to continue to invest in promotional discounting.
- Management states it expects interest expense to increase from current levels in 2026 in connection with amortization of the 2030 Notes Embedded Derivative liability and debt discount, and interest expense associated with the Delayed Draw Term Loans.
- Management states it expects to record significant mark-to-market adjustments arising from the remeasurement of derivatives and other liabilities carried at fair value at each reporting period.

**Subsequent events**
- Subsequent to the quarter, an additional $62.6 million in aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes were converted into common stock, with 52,092,284 Conversion Shares and 3,869,808 anti-dilution RSUs issued.
- On May 1, 2026, the aggregate remaining principal amount of the 2030 Notes was increased by approximately $10.4 million in PIK interest at a rate of 9.5% for the period from October 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026.
- On April 15, 2026, the company entered into a Distribution Agreement with Big Geyser, Inc. for the Beyond Immerse beverage line with an initial ten-year term.
- Effective May 4, 2026, the company hired the son of Seth Goldman, Chair of the Board of Directors, as Senior Manager of Community Engagement with a base salary of $130,000.

## The Print

Beyond Meat reported Q1 2026 net revenues of $58.2M (down 15.3% YoY) and a net loss of $28.5M, or $(0.06) per diluted share, versus a $(0.80) loss a year earlier.

The company returned to positive gross margin and cut its net loss by more than half versus the prior-year quarter, while continuing to report revenue declines and a widening stockholders' deficit.

- Net revenues fell 15.3% to $58.2M from $68.7M, driven by a 19.5% decline in volume of products sold, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound.
- Net loss narrowed to $28.5M from $61.1M, aided by a $12.6M total other income, net, including an $11.9M non-cash derivative remeasurement gain and a $6.1M gain on debt extinguishment.
- Gross margin turned positive at 3.4% versus a (10.1)% gross margin loss in the prior-year period, as cost of goods sold per pound declined 7.6%.
- Total stockholders' deficit widened to $(21.1)M from $(1.0)M at December 31, 2025, and the company disclosed it can no longer access its ATM Program.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net revenues | $58,206 thousand | $68,731 thousand | −15.3% | Management attributes the decline primarily to a 19.5% decrease in volume of products sold, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound. |
| Gross profit (loss) | $1,985 thousand | $(6,926) thousand | +128.7% | Management attributes the improvement to a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound and a 7.6% decrease in cost of goods sold per pound, reflecting lower inventory provision and reduced manufacturing expenses. |
| Loss from operations | $(41,104) thousand | $(64,370) thousand | +36.1% | Management attributes the reduction to higher gross profit, lower research and development expenses, and reduced SG&A expenses primarily due to lower marketing, legal, and salary and related expenses. |
| Net loss | $(28,482) thousand | $(61,087) thousand | +53.4% | Management attributes the decrease primarily to the decrease in loss from operations and the increase in Total other income (expense), net. |
| Net loss per share available to common stockholders—basic and diluted | $(0.06) | $(0.80) | +92.5% | Weighted average common shares outstanding—basic and diluted rose to 455,272,616 from 76,194,916, reflecting share issuance in connection with the 2025 Exchange Offer and 2030 Notes conversions. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

The $28.5M net loss included $12.6M of total other income, net, comprising an $11.9M non-cash gain from remeasurement of the 2030 Notes Embedded Derivative liability, a $6.1M gain on debt extinguishment from 2030 Notes conversions, a $1.3M gain from remeasurement of the warrant liability, and $1.5M of interest income, partially offset by $6.7M of interest expense and $1.3M of net realized and unrealized foreign currency transaction losses. Adjusted EBITDA was $(27.8)M versus $(50.5)M in the prior-year period.

Free cash flow of $-7.6M.

**Red flag:** The company corrected previously issued interim financial statements for the three months ended March 29, 2025 relating to inventory valuation and debt issuance costs, restating net loss to $(61,087) thousand from $(52,916) thousand as previously reported.

**Red flag:** The company disclosed it failed to timely deliver certain audited annual financial statements to its lender by March 31, 2026, was in default under the Loan and Security Agreement, and provided notice thereof; the default was remedied upon filing of the 2025 Form 10-K on April 9, 2026.

**Red flag:** The company received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on March 4, 2026 regarding the minimum bid price requirement, which if not satisfied could result in delisting.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $2.5M (prior $4.5M).

Capital allocation in the quarter was directed toward sustaining operations and managing the capital structure rather than returning capital to shareholders; the company funded operations primarily through sales of products and existing cash, made capital expenditures for production equipment and facilities, and continued to rely on the PIK election on the 2030 Notes and the fully drawn $100.0M Delayed Draw Term Loan Facility.

Return on assets -4.9% (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- The company no longer satisfies the eligibility requirements for use of a registration statement on Form S-3 and, as a result, is unable to access its ATM Program.
- In the three months ended March 28, 2026, the company issued 5,315,857 Conversion Shares upon conversion of $6.2 million in aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes.
- On March 28, 2026, the company entered into a Sales Agreement with Roquette Frères for the supply of pea protein, committing to purchase pea protein inventory totaling $23.5 million, of which $11.8 million is expected to be purchased in 2026 and $11.7 million in 2027.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide quantitative revenue, earnings, or margin guidance. Management states it expects research and development expenses in 2026 to decrease compared to the levels in 2025, expects interest expense to increase from current levels in 2026, expects to record significant mark-to-market adjustments from remeasurement of derivatives and other liabilities carried at fair value at each reporting period, and expects to elect the PIK option through the term of the 2030 Notes.

**Known trends**
- Demand for plant-based meat products has continued to decline persistently over the past three years, and management states it expects to continue to operate at a loss for the foreseeable future.
- The company expects to experience greater demand for certain products during the U.S. summer grilling season, with U.S. retail channel net revenues in the second quarter historically higher than the first quarter.
- Management states the strategic repositioning to 'Beyond The Plant Protein Company' and beverage expansion will require incremental investment in marketing, distribution infrastructure and working capital.

**Subsequent events**
- Subsequent to March 28, 2026, an additional $62.6 million in aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes were converted into shares of common stock, with 52,092,284 Conversion Shares issued and 3,869,808 anti-dilution RSUs issued to MIP award recipients.
- On May 1, 2026, the aggregate remaining principal amount of the 2030 Notes was increased by approximately $10.4 million in PIK interest at a rate of 9.5% for the period from October 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026.
- On April 15, 2026, the company entered into a Distribution Agreement with Big Geyser, Inc. appointing Big Geyser as exclusive distributor of the 'Beyond Immerse' beverage line in a defined northeast U.S. territory, with an initial ten-year term.
- Effective May 4, 2026, the company hired the son of Seth Goldman, the company's Chair of the Board of Directors, as Senior Manager of Community Engagement with a base salary of $130,000 and a target annual bonus of 10%.

Leverage: Total debt includes $300.5M carrying amount of 2030 Notes, $107.7M of Delayed Draw Term Loans including PIK interest, $29.5M of 2027 Notes, and $79.9M of finance lease liabilities, against $191.0M of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents; total stockholders' deficit widened to $(21.1)M from $(1.0)M at December 31, 2025.

the_print.headline: Beyond Meat reported Q1 2026 net revenues of $58.2M (down 15.3% YoY) and a net loss of $28.5M, or $(0.06) per diluted share, versus a $(0.80) loss a year earlier.
key_takeaways: Net revenues fell 15.3% to $58.2M from $68.7M, driven by a 19.5% decline in volume of products sold, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound.
Net loss narrowed to $28.5M from $61.1M, aided by a $12.6M total other income, net, including an $11.9M non-cash derivative remeasurement gain and a $6.1M gain on debt extinguishment.
Gross margin turned positive at 3.4% versus a (10.1)% gross margin loss in the prior-year period, as cost of goods sold per pound declined 7.6%.
Total stockholders' deficit widened to $(21.1)M from $(1.0)M at December 31, 2025, and the company disclosed it can no longer access its ATM Program.
the_print.what_changed: The company returned to positive gross margin and cut its net loss by more than half versus the prior-year quarter, while continuing to report revenue declines and a widening stockholders' deficit.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Alibaba's FY2026 revenue rose 3% to CNY 1,023.7B but operating income fell 64% to CNY 50.2B as sales and marketing expenses rose 70% to CNY 245.0B.

Operating margin compressed to 4.9% from 14.1% as sales and marketing expenses rose 70% to CNY 245.0B, driven by investment in quick commerce, user experiences, and Qwen app user acquisition.

- Revenue of CNY 1,023.7B (US$148.4B) in FY2026, up 3% YoY; excluding disposed Sun Art and Intime businesses, like-for-like revenue grew 11%.
- Net income of CNY 102.1B (US$14.8B), down 19% YoY; operating income fell 64% to CNY 50.2B as operating margin compressed to 4.9% from 14.1%.
- Cloud Intelligence Group revenue rose 34% to CNY 158.1B and Quick commerce revenue rose 47% to CNY 78.5B, while sales and marketing expenses rose 70% to CNY 245.0B.
- Diluted earnings per ADS of CNY 44.00 (US$6.38), down from CNY 53.59 in FY2025; each ADS represents eight ordinary shares.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | CNY 1,023,670M (US$148,401M) | CNY 996,347M | — | Excluding revenue from the disposed businesses of Sun Art and Intime, revenue on a like-for-like basis would have grown by 11% year-over-year. |
| Income from operations | CNY 50,150M (US$7,270M) | CNY 140,905M | — | The year-over-year decrease was primarily attributable to the decrease in adjusted EBITA and increase in impairment of goodwill, partly offset by the decrease in one-time provisions and non-cash share-based expenses. |
| Net income | CNY 102,127M (US$14,805M) | CNY 125,976M | — | Primarily attributable to the decrease in income from operations, partly offset by the year-over-year increase in net gain from mark-to-market changes of our equity investments, as well as net gains from disposal of investments, including local consumer service business of Trendyol in fiscal year 2026, compared to losses on disposal of Sun Art and Intime in fiscal year 2025. |
| Diluted earnings per ADS | CNY 44.00 (US$6.38) | CNY 53.59 | — | Each ADS represents eight ordinary shares. |
| Non-GAAP net income | CNY 60,658M (US$8,794M) | CNY 158,122M | — | Non-GAAP net income excludes non-cash share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, gain or loss on deemed disposals/disposals/revaluation of investments, impairment of goodwill and investments and others, and adjustments for the tax effects. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income fell 64% to CNY 50.2B while net income fell only 19% to CNY 102.1B, as interest and investment income, net swung to a gain of CNY 87.5B from CNY 20.8B, driven by mark-to-market gains on equity investments and net gains from disposal of investments including Trendyol's local consumer service business. Non-GAAP net income, which excludes these investment gains and other non-cash items, fell 62% to CNY 60.7B, indicating the reported net income decline understates the operating deterioration.

Operating cash flow was 0.7x net income (cash conversion).

**Red flag:** Sales and marketing expenses rose 70% to CNY 245.0B, outpacing revenue growth of 3%, compressing operating margin to 4.9% from 14.1%.

**Red flag:** Goodwill impairment of CNY 9,515M in FY2026, up 54% from CNY 6,171M in FY2025, both related to the All others segment.

**Red flag:** Operating cash flow fell 53% to CNY 76.2B from CNY 163.5B, attributed to investment in quick commerce and increased cloud infrastructure expenditure.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid CNY 33.7B (prior CNY 29.1B), share repurchases CNY 7.6B (prior CNY 86.7B).

Capital allocation shifted toward investment in quick commerce, user experiences, and cloud/AI infrastructure, with capital expenditures rising to CNY 126.1B from CNY 86.0B. Share repurchases declined to CNY 7.6B from CNY 86.7B, while dividends paid rose to CNY 33.7B from CNY 29.1B. The company issued convertible unsecured senior notes and exchangeable bonds to fund cloud infrastructure and international commerce investments.

Return on equity was 9.8% (prior 12.9%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 5.4% (prior 7.2%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In May 2025, agreed to sell 85% of the equity interest in Trendyol GO for approximately US$0.7 billion (RMB5 billion), completed during the year ended March 31, 2026.
- In July 2025, issued zero coupon exchangeable bonds due 2032 for approximately HK$12 billion, with net proceeds intended for cloud infrastructure and international commerce investments.
- In September 2025, issued zero coupon convertible unsecured senior notes due 2032 for approximately US$3.2 billion, with net proceeds focused on cloud infrastructure and international commerce.

## Forward Signals

No specific financial guidance provided. The company stated it has been and will continue investing at scale in cloud computing and AI capabilities as well as consumption, including quick commerce.

**Known trends**
- The company has been and will continue investing at scale in cloud computing and AI capabilities as well as consumption, including quick commerce.
- Our investment in the above-mentioned new and existing businesses has and may lower our margins but we believe the investment will deliver overall long-term growth.

**Subsequent events**
- Not disclosed—no material events after March 31, 2026 disclosed in the provided excerpts.

> "We have been and will continue investing at scale in cloud computing and AI capabilities as well as consumption, including quick commerce." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | VIE structure risk: Alibaba is a Cayman Islands holding company that does not directly own its operating entities; investors in ADSs purchase equity securities of a holding company rather than the VIEs, and may never hold equity interests in the VIEs. | Investors in our ADSs and Shares are purchasing equity securities of a Cayman Islands holding company rather than equity securities issued by our consolidated subsidiaries and the VIEs, and investors may never hold equity interests in the VIEs under current PRC laws and regulations. |
| 2 | PRC regulatory risk: The PRC government has significant oversight and discretion over the conduct of the company's business and may intervene in or influence operations through adopting and enforcing rules and regulatory requirements. | The PRC government has significant oversight and discretion over the conduct of our business, and may intervene in or influence our operations through adopting and enforcing rules and regulatory requirements. |
| 3 | Margin compression risk: Investment in new and existing businesses has and may lower margins, with operating margin falling to 4.9% in FY2026 from 14.1% in FY2025. | Our investment in the above-mentioned new and existing businesses has and may lower our margins but we believe the investment will deliver overall long-term growth. |
| 4 | Goodwill and intangible asset impairment risk: The company recognized goodwill impairment of CNY 9,515M in FY2026 and CNY 6,171M in FY2025, and may incur impairment charges in the future. | We have incurred impairment charges in the past and may incur impairment charges in the future. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total assets of CNY 1,909.6B and total shareholders' equity of CNY 1,060.9B as of March 31, 2026. Cash and cash equivalents of CNY 131.5B, plus short-term investments and other treasury investments that are unrestricted for withdrawal and use of CNY 155.2B and CNY 234.1B respectively, totaling CNY 520.8B (US$75.5B). Other bank borrowings of CNY 71.8B (US$10.4B) and RMB3.9B (US$0.6B) drawn under the ancillary facility arrangement.

Liquidity: The company believes that its current levels of cash and cash flows from operations will be sufficient to meet its anticipated cash needs for at least the next twelve months. Unutilised commitment of approximately US$2.6B under the revolving credit facility and a US$3.33B revolving credit facility not yet drawn as of March 31, 2026.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating CNY 76.2B, investing CNY -67.3B, financing CNY -20.6B.

Working capital: Current assets CNY 610.8B vs. current liabilities CNY 476.4B (current ratio 1.28x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-03-31: CNY 674.0B vs. CNY 435.3B (1.55x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- The company is not subject to any financial covenant or other significant operating covenants under the unsecured senior notes.
- The revolving credit facility expiration date was extended to September 30, 2028, with an option to further extend to September 30, 2030.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Segment reporting structure change | During fiscal year 2026, the company combined Taobao and Tmall Group, Ele.me and Fliggy into Alibaba China E-commerce Group and reclassified Cainiao, Amap and Hujing Digital Media and Entertainment Group into 'All others'. Comparative figures for fiscal years 2024 and 2025 were reclassified to conform with the new reporting structure, affecting year-over-year comparability. |
| PRC withholding tax on distributable earnings | As of March 31, 2026, the company has accrued withholding tax on substantially all earnings distributable by its subsidiaries in China, except for RMB278.9 billion (US$40.4 billion) reserved for permanent reinvestment in China. |
| Restricted net assets of PRC subsidiaries | As of March 31, 2026, restricted net assets totaled RMB344.6 billion (US$50.0 billion), which are not distributable as cash dividends. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Alibaba's FY2026 revenue rose 3% to CNY 1,023.7B while net income fell 19% to CNY 102.1B and operating income dropped 64% to CNY 50.2B as sales and marketing expenses rose 70%.

Operating income fell 64% and operating margin compressed to 4.9% from 14.1% as sales and marketing expenses rose 70%, while net income was partly cushioned by a CNY 87.5B net interest and investment income gain.

- Revenue of CNY 1,023.7B (US$148.4B) rose 3% YoY; on a like-for-like basis excluding disposed Sun Art and Intime businesses, revenue would have grown 11%.
- Net income of CNY 102.1B fell 19% YoY and operating income of CNY 50.2B fell 64%, with operating margin compressing to 4.9% from 14.1%.
- Sales and marketing expenses rose 70% to CNY 245.0B, driven by investment in user experiences of Alibaba China E-commerce Group and user acquisition of the Qwen app.
- Cloud Intelligence Group revenue rose 34% to CNY 158.1B, while All others segment revenue fell 25% to CNY 254.4B on the Sun Art and Intime disposals.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | CNY 1,023,670M | CNY 996,347M | +2.7% | Excluding revenue from the disposed businesses of Sun Art and Intime, revenue on a like-for-like basis would have grown 11% year-over-year. |
| Income from operations | CNY 50,150M | CNY 140,905M | −64.4% | The year-over-year decrease was primarily attributable to the decrease in adjusted EBITA and increase in impairment of goodwill, partly offset by the decrease in one-time provisions and non-cash share-based expenses. |
| Net income | CNY 102,127M | CNY 125,976M | −18.9% | Primarily attributable to the decrease in income from operations, partly offset by the year-over-year increase in net gain from mark-to-market changes of equity investments and net gains from disposal of investments. |
| Net income attributable to Alibaba Group Holding Limited | CNY 103,592M | CNY 130,109M | −20.4% | Not disclosed—no separate driver stated for this line beyond the consolidated net income movement. |
| Diluted earnings per share | CNY 5.50 | CNY 6.70 | −17.9% | Not disclosed—no separate driver stated for the per-share line. |
| Diluted earnings per ADS | CNY 44.00 | CNY 53.59 | −17.9% | Each ADS represents eight Shares. |
| Non-GAAP net income | CNY 60,658M | CNY 158,122M | −61.6% | Not disclosed—no separate driver stated for the non-GAAP line. |
| Adjusted EBITA | CNY 76,416M | CNY 173,065M | −55.9% | Not disclosed—no separate driver stated for the consolidated adjusted EBITA line. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income fell 64% to CNY 50.2B while net income fell only 19% to CNY 102.1B, cushioned by interest and investment income, net of CNY 87.5B versus CNY 20.8B in the prior year, primarily due to the year-over-year increase in net gain from mark-to-market changes of equity investments and net gains from disposal of investments. Non-GAAP net income, which excludes share-based compensation, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, gain or loss on deemed disposals/disposals/revaluation of investments, and impairment of goodwill and investments, fell 62% to CNY 60.7B, a sharper decline than reported net income.

Operating cash flow was 0.7x net income (cash conversion).

**Red flag:** Non-GAAP net income fell 62% to CNY 60.7B, a steeper decline than the 19% drop in reported net income, indicating reported net income was supported by non-operating investment gains.

**Red flag:** Interest and investment income, net swung to a CNY 87.5B gain from CNY 20.8B, driven by mark-to-market changes of equity investments and disposal gains, a non-operating source.

**Red flag:** Impairment of goodwill rose 54% to CNY 9.5B in fiscal year 2026 from CNY 6.2B, related to the All others segment.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid CNY 33.7B (prior CNY 29.1B), share repurchases CNY 7.6B (prior CNY 86.7B).

Capital expenditures rose to CNY 126.1B in fiscal year 2026 from CNY 86.0B, directed at cloud and AI infrastructure, while share repurchases fell to CNY 7.6B from CNY 86.7B and dividends paid rose to CNY 33.7B from CNY 29.1B. The filing states the company has been and will continue investing at scale in cloud computing and AI capabilities as well as consumption, including quick commerce.

Return on equity was 9.8% (prior 12.9%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 5.4% (prior 7.2%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In July 2025, issued zero coupon exchangeable bonds due 2032 by reference to ordinary shares of subsidiary Alibaba Health for an aggregate principal amount of approximately HK$12 billion.
- In September 2025, issued zero coupon convertible unsecured senior notes due 2032 for an aggregate principal amount of approximately US$3.2 billion.
- In May 2025, agreed to sell 85% of the equity interest in Trendyol GO for cash consideration of approximately US$0.7 billion (RMB5 billion), completed during the year ended March 31, 2026.

## Forward Signals

No quantitative guidance given. The filing states the company has been and will continue investing at scale in cloud computing and AI capabilities as well as consumption, including quick commerce, and that it expects to fund additional investments through cash generated from operations and through debt and equity financing.

**Known trends**
- We have been and will continue investing at scale in cloud computing and AI capabilities as well as consumption, including quick commerce.
- Our investment in the above-mentioned new and existing businesses has and may lower our margins but we believe the investment will deliver overall long-term growth.

**Subsequent events**

**Maturities & covenants**

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Alibaba's FY2026 revenue rose 3% to CNY 1,023.7B but operating income fell 64% to CNY 50.2B as sales and marketing expenses rose 70% to CNY 245.0B.

Operating margin compressed from 14.1% to 4.9% as the company invested at scale in quick commerce, user experience, and cloud/AI infrastructure, while revenue growth decelerated to 3% on a reported basis.

- Revenue of CNY 1,023.7B (US$148.4B) rose 3% YoY; on a like-for-like basis excluding disposed Sun Art and Intime businesses, revenue would have grown 11%.
- Operating income fell 64% to CNY 50.2B (operating margin 4.9% vs 14.1%), driven by a 70% increase in sales and marketing expenses to CNY 245.0B.
- Net income of CNY 102.1B (US$14.8B) declined 19% YoY; diluted EPS was CNY 5.50 (CNY 44.00 per ADS) versus CNY 6.70 (CNY 53.59 per ADS).
- Cloud Intelligence Group revenue rose 34% to CNY 158.1B, while Alibaba China E-commerce Group adjusted EBITA fell 44% to CNY 107.5B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | CNY 1,023,670M | CNY 996,347M | +2.7% | Growth driven by Cloud Intelligence Group (+34%) and Quick commerce (+47%), partly offset by a 25% decline in All others segment revenue following the disposal of Sun Art and Intime. |
| Income from operations | CNY 50,150M | CNY 140,905M | −64.4% | Decrease primarily attributable to the decrease in adjusted EBITA and increase in impairment of goodwill, partly offset by the decrease in one-time provisions and non-cash share-based expenses. |
| Net income | CNY 102,127M | CNY 125,976M | −18.9% | Decrease primarily attributable to the decrease in income from operations, partly offset by the year-over-year increase in net gain from mark-to-market changes of equity investments and net gains from disposal of investments. |
| Diluted earnings per share | CNY 5.50 | CNY 6.70 | −17.9% | Decline reflects lower net income attributable to ordinary shareholders. |
| Diluted earnings per ADS | CNY 44.00 | CNY 53.59 | −17.9% | Each ADS represents eight ordinary shares. |
| Operating margin | 4.9% | 14.1% | −9.2 ppts | Compression driven by the 70% increase in sales and marketing expenses as a percentage of revenue from 14% to 24%. |
| Net margin | 10.1% | 13.1% | −3.0 ppts | Net margin declined as operating income fell faster than revenue. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income of CNY 102.1B included a CNY 87.5B net interest and investment income (versus CNY 20.8B prior year), largely from mark-to-market gains on equity investments and disposal gains including Trendyol GO. Non-GAAP net income, which excludes these items, fell 62% to CNY 60.7B from CNY 158.1B. Adjusted EBITA fell 56% to CNY 76.4B. Impairment of goodwill rose 54% to CNY 9.5B, and impairment of intangible assets was CNY 1.7B.

Operating cash flow was 0.7x net income (cash conversion).

**Red flag:** Non-GAAP net income declined 62% to CNY 60.7B, a sharper decline than reported net income (-19%), indicating reported profitability was substantially supported by non-operating investment gains.

**Red flag:** Operating cash flow fell 53% to CNY 76.2B, attributed to investment in quick commerce and increased cloud infrastructure expenditure.

**Red flag:** Free cash flow turned negative at CNY -46.6B, compared to positive CNY 73.9B in the prior year.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid CNY 33.7B (prior CNY 29.1B), share repurchases CNY 7.6B (prior CNY 86.7B).

Capital allocation shifted toward heavy investment in quick commerce, user experience, and cloud/AI infrastructure, with capital expenditures rising to CNY 126.1B from CNY 86.0B. Share repurchases declined sharply to CNY 7.6B from CNY 86.7B, while dividends paid rose to CNY 33.7B from CNY 29.1B. The company issued convertible and exchangeable notes to fund cloud infrastructure and international commerce.

Return on equity was 9.8% (prior 12.9%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 5.4% (prior 7.2%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In July 2025, issued approximately HK$12 billion zero coupon exchangeable bonds due 2032 by reference to Alibaba Health shares.
- In September 2025, issued approximately US$3.2 billion zero coupon convertible unsecured senior notes due 2032.
- In May 2025, agreed to sell 85% of Trendyol GO for approximately US$0.7 billion (RMB 5 billion), completed during fiscal year 2026.

## Forward Signals

No specific financial guidance was provided. Management stated it has been and will continue investing at scale in cloud computing and AI capabilities as well as consumption, including quick commerce.

**Known trends**
- Continued investment in cloud and AI infrastructure, which management states has and may lower margins.
- Investment in user growth and quick commerce, which increased sales and marketing expenses to 24% of revenue.

**Subsequent events**
- Not disclosed—no material subsequent events were identified in the provided excerpts.

> "We have been and will continue investing at scale in cloud computing and AI capabilities as well as consumption, including quick commerce." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | VIE structure risk: Alibaba is a Cayman Islands holding company that does not directly own its operating entities; investors in ADSs hold equity of the holding company, not the VIEs, and may never hold equity interests in the VIEs. | Investors in our ADSs and Shares are purchasing equity securities of a Cayman Islands holding company rather than equity securities issued by our consolidated subsidiaries and the VIEs, and investors may never hold equity interests in the VIEs under current PRC laws and regulations. |
| 2 | PRC regulatory risk: The PRC government has significant oversight and discretion over the conduct of Alibaba's business and may intervene in or influence operations through adopting and enforcing rules and regulatory requirements. | The PRC government has significant oversight and discretion over the conduct of our business, and may intervene in or influence our operations through adopting and enforcing rules and regulatory requirements. |
| 3 | Margin and net income risk from sustained investment: Management states that investment in new and existing businesses has and may lower margins, and that strategic investments and acquisitions may adversely affect future financial results including margins and net income. | Our investment in the above-mentioned new and existing businesses has and may lower our margins but we believe the investment will deliver overall long-term growth. |
| 4 | Impairment risk: Alibaba recognized goodwill impairment of CNY 9,515 million in fiscal year 2026 and intangible asset impairment of CNY 1,729 million, and states it may incur impairment charges in the future. | We recognized impairment charges on goodwill of RMB6,171 million and RMB9,515 million (US$1,380 million) in fiscal years 2025 and 2026 respectively. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total liabilities of CNY 783.3B against total shareholders' equity of CNY 1,060.9B; cash and cash equivalents of CNY 131.5B plus short-term investments and other treasury investments totaling CNY 520.8B.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of CNY 131.5B, short-term investments and other treasury investments unrestricted for withdrawal and use of CNY 155.2B and CNY 234.1B respectively, totaling CNY 520.8B (US$75.5B). The company believes current levels of cash and cash flows from operations will be sufficient to meet anticipated cash needs for at least the next twelve months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating CNY 76.2B, investing CNY -67.3B, financing CNY -20.6B.

Working capital: Current assets CNY 610.8B vs. current liabilities CNY 476.4B (current ratio 1.28x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2025-03-31: CNY 674.0B vs. CNY 435.3B (1.55x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- As of March 31, 2026, total outstanding borrowing of RMB3.9 billion (US$0.6 billion) under the ancillary facility arrangement by way of short-term loan facilities and unutilised commitment of approximately US$2.6 billion.
- Other bank borrowings of RMB71,774 million (US$10,405 million) as of March 31, 2026, primarily used for capital expenditures and other working capital purposes.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| Segment reporting reclassification | During fiscal year 2026, Alibaba combined Taobao and Tmall Group, Ele.me and Fliggy into Alibaba China E-commerce Group and reclassified Cainiao, Amap and Hujing Digital Media and Entertainment Group into 'All others'. Comparative figures for fiscal years 2024 and 2025 were reclassified to conform with the new reporting structure, affecting year-over-year comparability. |
| PRC withholding tax on distributable earnings | As of March 31, 2026, Alibaba has accrued withholding tax on substantially all earnings distributable by its PRC subsidiaries, except for RMB278.9 billion (US$40.4 billion) reserved for permanent reinvestment in China. If the plan to reinvest indefinitely changes, the company would be required to accrue or pay withholding tax, adversely affecting the effective tax rate. |
| Restricted net assets of PRC subsidiaries | As of March 31, 2026, restricted net assets totaled RMB344.6 billion (US$50.0 billion), which are not distributable as cash dividends, potentially limiting the holding company's ability to fund operations or pay dividends outside the PRC. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

ASML's FY2025 total net sales rose 15.6% to EUR 32.7B and net income rose 26.9% to EUR 9.6B, with basic EPS of EUR 24.73.

Revenue growth accelerated to 15.6% with margin expansion and a 26.9% increase in net income, while capital returned to shareholders rose to EUR 8.5B and a new share buyback program of up to EUR 12B was announced.

- Total net sales of EUR 32,667.3M, up 15.6% YoY, driven by a 12.4% increase in net system sales and a 26.2% increase in net service and field option sales.
- Net income of EUR 9,609.4M (29.4% of net sales) versus EUR 7,571.6M (26.8%) in 2024; basic EPS EUR 24.73 versus EUR 19.25.
- Gross margin expanded to 52.8% from 51.3% and income from operations rose 25.3% to EUR 11,301.4M, with the effective tax rate declining to 17.7% from 18.6%.
- Customers in China represented 29.1% of 2025 total net sales (2024: 36.1%), and the largest customer accounted for 23.9% of total net sales (2024: 16.6%).

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net sales | EUR 32,667.3M | EUR 28,262.9M | +15.6% | Growth driven by a 12.4% increase in net system sales and a 26.2% increase in net service and field option sales. |
| Gross profit | EUR 17,258.0M | EUR 14,492.0M | +19.1% | Increase mainly driven by a favorable NXE product mix and higher net service and field option sales and margins, partially offset by the dilutive impact of EXE systems recognized in sales. |
| Income from operations | EUR 11,301.4M | EUR 9,022.6M | +25.3% | Operating margin expanded to 34.6% from 31.9% as gross margin improved and R&D and SG&A costs grew more slowly than sales. |
| Net income | EUR 9,609.4M | EUR 7,571.6M | +26.9% | Net income represented 29.4% of total net sales; the increase in basic net income per ordinary share was primarily driven by higher net income. |
| Basic net income per ordinary share | EUR 24.73 | EUR 19.25 | +28.5% | Increase primarily driven by higher net income. |
| Diluted net income per ordinary share | EUR 24.71 | EUR 19.24 | +28.4% | Diluted weighted average shares of 388.9M versus 393.6M in 2024. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income rose 25.3% to EUR 11,301.4M on higher gross margin and slower growth in R&D (up 9.2% to EUR 4,698.8M) and SG&A (up 7.9% to EUR 1,257.8M). Interest and other, net swung to a EUR 104.7M gain from EUR 19.8M, and profit from equity method investments was EUR 216.7M versus EUR 209.8M. The effective tax rate declined to 17.7% from 18.6%, which the filing attributes to a correction for a historic tax position recognized in 2024 that pertained to multiple years, for which the underlying tax position has a lower impact in 2025.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of EUR 11.1B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid EUR 2.6B (prior EUR 2.5B), share repurchases EUR 6.0B (prior EUR 500.0M); capital expenditures EUR 1.6B (prior EUR 2.1B).

Capital allocation combined a growing dividend with a step-up in share repurchases, funded by operating cash flow rather than debt; the filing states the company will continue to invest in its business and expects to return significant amounts of cash to shareholders through growing dividends and share buybacks.

Return on equity was 49.0% (prior 41.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 19.0% (prior 15.6%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On January 28, 2026 ASML announced a new share buyback program to be executed by December 31, 2028, intending to repurchase shares of an amount up to EUR 12 billion, of which up to 2.0 million shares are expected to be used to cover employee share plans.
- ASML intends to declare a total dividend for 2025 of EUR 7.50 per ordinary share, a 17.2% increase compared to the 2024 total dividend of EUR 6.40 per ordinary share, with a final dividend proposal of EUR 2.70 per ordinary share.
- During 2025 ASML took an approximately 11% share on a fully diluted basis in Mistral AI, with a EUR 1,302.2 million investment in Mistral in 2025.

## Forward Signals

For 2026, ASML expects full-year revenue between EUR 34 billion and EUR 39 billion and gross margin between 51% and 53%, alongside an annualized effective tax rate of around 17%. For Q1 2026 it guides total net sales between EUR 8.2 billion and EUR 8.9 billion, gross margin between 51% and 53%, R&D costs of around EUR 1.2 billion and SG&A costs of around EUR 0.3 billion. It reiterates a 2030 revenue opportunity between EUR 44 billion and EUR 60 billion with gross margin between 56% and 60%.

**Known trends**
- ASML expects EUV revenue to be significantly higher in 2026 driven by advanced node ramps, non-EUV revenue to be similar to 2025, and another year of growth in net service and field option sales.
- The 2026 outlook strengthened in the final months of 2025 mainly due to the anticipated increase and acceleration of capacity expansion plans by advanced Logic and DRAM customers to meet end-market demand driven by AI.
- ASML expects global semiconductor sales to grow at a 9% CAGR (2025-2030) and surpass $1 trillion by 2030, translating into expected overall wafer demand growth of 780K wafer starts per month per year on average.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 28, 2026 ASML announced a new share buyback program to be executed by December 31, 2028, intending to repurchase shares of an amount up to EUR 12 billion.
- On October 9, 2025, ASML announced that the Supervisory Board intends to add the role of Chief Technology Officer to the Board of Management effective per the 2026 Annual General Meeting, bringing the Board of Management to six members.

> "Looking ahead to 2026, we anticipate total net sales of between €34 billion and €39 billion." — Roger Dassen, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

> "In line with our 2024 Investor Day announcements, we expect a 2030 revenue opportunity between €44 billion and €60 billion with a gross margin expected between 56% and 60%." — Roger Dassen, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

| 2 | Customer concentration: total net sales to the largest customer were EUR 7,796.7M, or 23.9% of total net sales in 2025, versus EUR 4,682.4M, or 16.6%, in 2024, and 38.0% of 2025 total net sales were made to the two largest customers. | Total net sales to our largest customer amounted to €7,796.7 million, or 23.9% of total net sales in 2025, compared with €4,682.4 million, or 16.6% of total net sales in 2024. |
| 3 | Dependence on a limited number of critical single-source suppliers, including Carl Zeiss SMT as sole supplier of optics, whose production capacity limits the number of lithography systems ASML can produce. | The number of lithography systems we are able to produce is limited by the production capacity of one of our key suppliers, Carl Zeiss SMT, our sole supplier of lenses, mirrors, illuminators, collectors and other critical optical components (which we refer to as optics). |
| 4 | Geopolitical exposure: customers in Taiwan represented 25.5% of 2025 total net sales (2024: 15.4%) and customers in South Korea represented 25.0% (2024: 22.7%). | Changes in cross-strait relations, Taiwanese government policies, or broader political, economic, or social developments could affect our ability to serve customers in Taiwan – who represented 25.5% of our 2025 total net sales and 15.4% of our 2024 total net sales. |
| 5 | Counterparty credit risk is concentrated: the three largest customers accounted for EUR 1,294.2M, or 35.4%, of accounts receivable and finance receivables at December 31, 2025, versus EUR 2,641.9M, or 54.1%, at December 31, 2024. | Our three largest customers (based on total net sales) accounted for €1,294.2 million, or 35.4% of accounts receivable and finance receivables, at December 31, 2025, compared with €2,641.9 million, or 54.1%, at December 31, 2024. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Long-term debt (non-current portion) declined to EUR 2,709.0M from EUR 3,677.3M, while cash and cash equivalents of EUR 12,916.0M plus short-term investments of EUR 405.9M exceeded total debt; shareholders' equity rose to EUR 19,612.2M from EUR 18,476.8M.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled EUR 13,321.9M at year-end 2025 (2024: EUR 12,741.3M); ASML maintains an available committed credit facility of EUR 1.5 billion with no amounts outstanding and non-committed lines of credit up to EUR 3.0 billion.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating EUR 12.7B, investing EUR -3.8B, financing EUR -8.7B.

Working capital: Current assets EUR 30.6B vs. current liabilities EUR 24.3B (current ratio 1.26x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: EUR 30.7B vs. EUR 20.1B (1.53x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Total debt maturities of EUR 4,459.3M, with EUR 1,694.8M due in 2026, EUR 751.8M in 2027, EUR 1.8M in 2028, EUR 751.8M in 2029, EUR 751.8M in 2030 and EUR 507.3M thereafter.
- ASML repaid an outstanding EUR 1,000.0 million bond that was due on December 6, 2025.
- As of December 31, 2025, ASML had EUR 693.0 million outstanding under its EUR 1.5 billion Euro Commercial Paper program with a weighted-average interest rate of 2.03%.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

ASML's FY2025 total net sales rose 15.6% to EUR 32.7B and net income rose 26.9% to EUR 9.6B, with basic EPS of EUR 24.73.

Revenue growth accelerated to 15.6% from the prior year, gross margin expanded 150bps, and the customer and geographic mix shifted toward Taiwan and South Korea and away from China.

- Total net sales of EUR 32.7B (+15.6% YoY), split EUR 24.5B net system sales (+12.4%) and EUR 8.2B net service and field option sales (+26.2%).
- Net income of EUR 9.6B (+26.9% YoY) and basic EPS of EUR 24.73 (2024: EUR 19.25); gross margin expanded to 52.8% from 51.3%.
- Net sales to China fell to 29.1% of total net sales from 36.1% in 2024, while Taiwan rose to 25.5% from 15.4% and South Korea to 25.0% from 22.7%.
- The largest customer accounted for EUR 7,796.7M, or 23.9% of total net sales, up from 16.6% in 2024; the two largest customers were 38.0% of total net sales.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net sales | EUR 32,667.3M | EUR 28,262.9M | +15.6% | Growth driven by a 12.4% increase in net system sales and a 26.2% increase in net service and field option sales. |
| Net system sales | EUR 24,474.3M | EUR 21,768.7M | +12.4% | Increase primarily driven by greater NXE and NXT immersion adoption supported by leading-edge foundry investments for AI demand, partially offset by a decrease in ArF dry, KrF and i-line sales volumes. |
| Net service and field option sales | EUR 8,193.0M | EUR 6,494.2M | +26.2% | Increase mainly due to the growing installed base of systems, higher levels of lithography tool use for certain customers, and more NXE field upgrades. |
| Gross profit | EUR 17,258.0M | EUR 14,492.0M | +19.1% | Gross profit and gross margin increased, mainly driven by a favorable NXE product mix and higher net service and field option sales and margins, partially offset by the dilutive impact of EXE systems recognized in sales. |
| Gross margin | 52.8% | 51.3% | +1.5 ppts | Favorable NXE product mix and higher net service and field option sales and margins, partially offset by the dilutive impact of EXE systems recognized in sales. |
| Income from operations | EUR 11,301.4M | EUR 9,022.6M | +25.3% | Operating margin expanded to 34.6% from 31.9% as gross profit growth outpaced a 9.2% increase in R&D costs and a 7.9% increase in SG&A costs. |
| Net income | EUR 9,609.4M | EUR 7,571.6M | +26.9% | The increase in basic net income per ordinary share was primarily driven by higher net income. |
| Basic net income per ordinary share | EUR 24.73 | EUR 19.25 | +28.5% | Primarily driven by higher net income. |
| Diluted net income per ordinary share | EUR 24.71 | EUR 19.24 | +28.4% | Primarily driven by higher net income. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Income from operations of EUR 11,301.4M was the primary driver of net income of EUR 9,609.4M. Below the operating line, Interest and other, net swung to a EUR 104.7M gain from EUR 19.8M, and Profit from equity method investments was EUR 216.7M (2024: EUR 209.8M), which included a EUR 76.4M cost due to intercompany profit elimination (2024: EUR 20.8M gain). The effective tax rate decreased to 17.7% from 18.6%, primarily due to a correction for a historic tax position recognized in 2024 that pertained to multiple years.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of EUR 11.1B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid EUR 2.6B (prior EUR 2.5B), share repurchases EUR 6.0B (prior EUR 500.0M); capital expenditures EUR 1.6B (prior EUR 2.1B).

Capital allocation combined a higher dividend with a step-up in share repurchases, funded by operating cash flow. The company intends to declare a total dividend for 2025 of EUR 7.50 per ordinary share, a 17.2% increase over the 2024 total dividend of EUR 6.40, and on January 28, 2026 announced a new share buyback program of up to EUR 12B to be executed by December 31, 2028.

Return on equity was 49.0% (prior 41.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 19.0% (prior 15.6%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On January 28, 2026 ASML announced a new share buyback program to be executed by December 31, 2028, intending to repurchase shares of an amount up to EUR 12 billion, of which up to 2.0 million shares are expected to be used to cover employee share plans.
- The previous buyback program finished in December 2025, pursuant to which ASML repurchased a total of EUR 7.6 billion out of the up to EUR 12.0 billion program.
- ASML intends to declare a total dividend for 2025 of EUR 7.50 per ordinary share, a 17.2% increase compared to the 2024 total dividend of EUR 6.40 per ordinary share.

## Forward Signals

For 2026, ASML anticipates total net sales of between EUR 34 billion and EUR 39 billion and a gross margin between 51% and 53%, alongside an annualized effective tax rate of around 17%. For Q1 2026, guidance is total net sales between EUR 8.2 billion and EUR 8.9 billion, gross margin between 51% and 53%, R&D costs of around EUR 1.2 billion and SG&A costs of around EUR 0.3 billion. For 2030, the company reiterates a revenue opportunity between EUR 44 billion and EUR 60 billion with gross margin between 56% and 60%.

**Known trends**
- ASML expects EUV revenue to increase significantly in 2026 as a result of the dynamics in advanced Logic and DRAM, while non-EUV revenues for 2026 are anticipated to be similar to 2025.
- The company expects another year of revenue growth in service and field option sales, driven by the growing EUV installed base and customers' plans for performance upgrades.
- ASML expects Logic-related revenues to remain strong and Memory revenues to be significantly higher compared to 2025.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 28, 2026 ASML announced a new share buyback program to be executed by December 31, 2028, intending to repurchase shares of an amount up to EUR 12 billion.
- On October 9, 2025, ASML announced that the Supervisory Board intends to add the role of Chief Technology Officer to the Board of Management effective per the 2026 Annual General Meeting, bringing the Board of Management to six members.

> "In line with our 2024 Investor Day announcements, we expect a 2030 revenue opportunity between €44 billion and €60 billion with a gross margin expected between 56% and 60%." — Roger Dassen, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

| 3 | Single-source supplier dependence: Carl Zeiss SMT is the sole supplier of lenses, mirrors, illuminators, collectors and other critical optical components, and the number of lithography systems ASML can produce is limited by that supplier's production capacity. | The number of lithography systems we are able to produce is limited by the production capacity of one of our key suppliers, Carl Zeiss SMT, our sole supplier of lenses, mirrors, illuminators, collectors and other critical optical components (which we refer to as optics). |
| 4 | Counterparty credit concentration: the three largest customers accounted for EUR 1,294.2M, or 35.4%, of accounts receivable and finance receivables at December 31, 2025, compared with EUR 2,641.9M, or 54.1%, at December 31, 2024. | Our three largest customers (based on total net sales) accounted for €1,294.2 million, or 35.4% of accounts receivable and finance receivables, at December 31, 2025, compared with €2,641.9 million, or 54.1%, at December 31, 2024. |

## Segments

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Long-term debt (non-current portion) decreased to EUR 2,709.0M from EUR 3,677.3M, and total long-term debt fell to EUR 3,699.2M from EUR 4,687.6M, after the EUR 1,000M 3.500% senior notes due December 6, 2025 were repaid. Cash and cash equivalents of EUR 12,916.0M plus short-term investments of EUR 405.9M exceeded long-term debt. Shareholders' equity rose to EUR 19,612.2M from EUR 18,476.8M.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments totaled EUR 13,321.9M at year-end 2025 (2024: EUR 12,741.3M). ASML maintains an available committed credit facility of EUR 1.5 billion with no amounts outstanding, maturing May 2030 with one uncommitted one-year extension option, plus non-committed lines of credit of up to EUR 3.0 billion with no amounts drawn. As of December 31, 2025, EUR 693.0M was outstanding under the EUR 1.5 billion Euro Commercial Paper program at a weighted-average interest rate of 2.03%.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating EUR 12.7B, investing EUR -3.8B, financing EUR -8.7B.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

ASML's FY2025 total net sales rose 15.6% to EUR 32.7B and net income rose 26.9% to EUR 9.6B, with basic EPS of EUR 24.73.

Revenue growth accelerated to 15.6% from the prior year, gross margin expanded 150 basis points, and financing cash outflows increased sharply on a EUR 5.45B increase in share repurchases.

- Total net sales of EUR 32.7B (+15.6% YoY), driven by a 12.4% increase in net system sales and a 26.2% increase in net service and field option sales.
- Net income of EUR 9.6B (+26.9% YoY) and basic EPS of EUR 24.73 (2024: EUR 19.25); gross margin expanded to 52.8% from 51.3%.
- The company returned EUR 8.5B to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks in 2025, and announced a new share buyback program of up to EUR 12B to be executed by December 31, 2028.
- Customers in China represented 29.1% of 2025 total net sales (2024: 36.1%), and Taiwan 25.5% (2024: 15.4%), reflecting geographic concentration and export-control exposure.

## Results That Matter

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income rose 25.3% to EUR 11.3B, with operating margin expanding 270 basis points to 34.6%. The effective tax rate decreased to 17.7% from 18.6%, primarily due to a correction for a historic tax position recognized in 2024 that pertained to multiple years, for which the underlying tax position has a lower impact in 2025. Profit from equity method investments was EUR 216.7M (2024: EUR 209.8M), including a EUR 76.4M cost due to intercompany profit elimination (2024: EUR 20.8M gain).

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of EUR 11.1B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid EUR 2.6B (prior EUR 2.5B), share repurchases EUR 6.0B (prior EUR 500.0M); capital expenditures EUR 1.6B (prior EUR 2.1B).

Capital allocation is framed around a stated financing policy of maintaining a capital and liquidity structure that supports continued investment in the business while returning cash to shareholders through growing dividends and share buybacks; the period's shareholder returns were funded from operating cash generation, with the financing outflow increase driven by a EUR 5.45B increase in share repurchases, the repayment of a EUR 1.0B bond due December 6, 2025, and a EUR 97.4M increase in total dividends paid.

Return on equity was 49.0% (prior 41.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 19.0% (prior 15.6%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- On January 28, 2026 ASML announced a new share buyback program to be executed by December 31, 2028, intending to repurchase shares of an amount up to EUR 12 billion, of which up to 2.0 million shares are expected to be used to cover employee share plans.
- ASML intends to declare a total dividend for 2025 of EUR 7.50 per ordinary share, a 17.2% increase compared to the 2024 total dividend of EUR 6.40 per ordinary share.
- During 2025 ASML took an approximately 11% share on a fully diluted basis in Mistral AI, with a EUR 1,302.2 million investment.

## Forward Signals

For 2026, ASML anticipates total net sales of between EUR 34 billion and EUR 39 billion, a gross margin between 51% and 53%, and an annualized effective tax rate of around 17%. For Q1 2026, total net sales between EUR 8.2 billion and EUR 8.9 billion, gross margin between 51% and 53%, R&D costs of around EUR 1.2 billion, and SG&A costs of around EUR 0.3 billion. For 2030, the company reiterates a revenue opportunity between EUR 44 billion and EUR 60 billion with gross margin between 56% and 60%.

**Known trends**
- ASML expects EUV revenue to increase significantly in 2026 as a result of the dynamics in advanced Logic and DRAM, while non-EUV revenues for 2026 are anticipated to be similar to 2025.
- Service and field option sales are expected to grow again, driven by the growing EUV installed base and customers' plans for performance upgrades.
- The 2026 outlook strengthened significantly in the final months of 2025, mainly due to the anticipated increase and acceleration of capacity expansion plans by advanced Logic and DRAM customers to meet end-market demand driven by AI.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 28, 2026 ASML announced a new share buyback program to be executed by December 31, 2028, intending to repurchase shares of an amount up to EUR 12 billion.
- On October 9, 2025, ASML announced that the Supervisory Board intends to add the role of Chief Technology Officer to the Board of Management effective per the 2026 Annual General Meeting.

> "In line with our 2024 Investor Day announcements, we expect a 2030 revenue opportunity between €44 billion and €60 billion with a gross margin expected between 56% and 60%." — Roger Dassen, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (long-term debt plus short-term borrowings) declined as the EUR 1,000M 3.500% senior notes due December 6, 2025 were repaid; long-term debt fell to EUR 2,709.0M from EUR 3,677.3M, while cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments rose to EUR 13,321.9M from EUR 12,741.3M. Shareholders' equity increased to EUR 19,612.2M from EUR 18,476.8M.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments of EUR 13,321.9M at year end, plus an available committed credit facility of EUR 1.5 billion (no amounts outstanding) and non-committed lines of credit up to EUR 3.0 billion (no amounts drawn). ASML states it has sufficient capital for the company's present obligations.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating EUR 12.7B, investing EUR -3.8B, financing EUR -8.7B.

- Total debt maturities of EUR 4,459.3M as of December 31, 2025, of which EUR 1,694.8M is due in 2026.
