payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

TSMC's FY2025 net revenue rose 31.6% to TWD 3,809,054 million and net income rose 46.4% to TWD 1,695,125 million, with advanced-node (7nm and below) wafer revenue reaching 74% of total wafer revenue.

Revenue growth accelerated to 31.6% in 2025 from 33.9% in 2024 on a larger base, with gross, operating and net margins all expanding year over year and advanced-node mix rising to 74% of wafer revenue.

- Net revenue of TWD 3,809,054 million (US$121,423 million) increased 31.6% from TWD 2,894,308 million in 2024, attributed by management to higher ASP from a greater proportion of advanced technology revenue and higher wafer shipments, partly offset by NT dollar appreciation.
- Net income of TWD 1,695,125 million (US$54,036 million) rose 46.4% from TWD 1,157,524 million; net income attributable to shareholders of the parent was TWD 1,697,604 million (US$54,116 million).
- Gross margin expanded to 59.9% from 56.1% and operating margin to 50.8% from 45.7%, which management attributed mainly to higher capacity utilization and cost improvement, partially offset by an unfavorable foreign exchange rate.
- Advanced technologies (7-nanometer and below) accounted for 74% of total wafer revenue, up from 69% in 2024, with 3-nanometer at 24%, 5-nanometer at 36% and 7-nanometer at 14%.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net revenue | TWD 3,809,054M (US$121,423M) | TWD 2,894,308M | — | Management attributed the increase mainly to higher ASP from a greater proportion of advanced technology (7-nanometer and below) revenue and higher wafer shipments, partially offset by NT dollar appreciation against the U.S. dollar. |
| Gross profit | TWD 2,281,294M (US$72,722M) | TWD 1,624,354M | — | Gross margin rose to 59.9% from 56.1%, which management attributed mainly to higher capacity utilization and cost improvement, partially offset by an unfavorable foreign exchange rate. |
| Income from operations | TWD 1,936,092M (US$61,718M) | TWD 1,322,053M | — | Operating margin expanded to 50.8% from 45.7%; total operating expenses rose 14.8% to TWD 345,649 million, with R&D up 20.7% on higher research activity for 10-angstrom, 14-angstrom and 16-angstrom process technologies. |
| Net income | TWD 1,695,125M (US$54,036M) | TWD 1,157,524M | — | Income tax expense rose 39.6% to TWD 346,530 million, which management attributed mainly to higher taxable income in 2025. |
| Net income attributable to shareholders of the parent | TWD 1,697,604M (US$54,116M) | TWD 1,158,380M | — | Net margin attributable to shareholders of the parent rose to 44.6% from 40.0%. |
| EPS (Basic) | TWD 65.47 | TWD 44.68 | +46.5% | Basic EPS rose with the increase in net income attributable to shareholders of the parent. |
| EPS (Diluted) | TWD 65.47 | TWD 44.67 | +46.6% | Diluted EPS rose with the increase in net income attributable to shareholders of the parent. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating results drove the year: income from operations rose 46.4% to TWD 1,936,092 million. Non-operating income increased 26.0% to TWD 105,563 million, which management attributed mainly to higher interest income of TWD 18,526 million compared with 2024; net other operating income and expenses swung to a net gain of TWD 447 million, which management attributed mainly to a lower loss on disposal of property, plant and equipment and reversal of impairment losses in 2025.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion).

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid TWD 466.8B (prior TWD 363.1B).

Capital expenditure was directed at installing and expanding capacity mainly for 2-nanometer, 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer nodes, including building/facility expansion for Fab 20, Fab 21 and Fab 22, and at expanding capacity for specialty technologies and advanced packaging, including Fab 23 and Fab 24. Management stated that cash generated from operations, cash and cash equivalents, current marketable securities, and ability to access capital markets will be sufficient to fund working capital needs, capital expenditures, debt repayments, dividend payments and other business requirements associated with existing operations over the next 12 months.

Return on equity was 31.4% (prior 27.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 21.4% (prior 17.3%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- The Board of Directors is authorized to approve quarterly cash dividends after the close of each quarter; the fourth quarter of 2025 cash dividend of NT$6.0 per share was approved on February 10, 2026 with a payment date of July 9, 2026.
- In 2025 the company issued NT dollar-denominated corporate bonds totaling NT$86,900 million (US$2,770 million).

## Forward Signals

Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be between US$52 billion and US$56 billion, which, depending on market conditions, may be adjusted later. Management also stated it plans to continue investment in technology research and development in 2026.

**Known trends**
- The NT dollar appreciation in 2025 had an unfavorable effect on revenue, with weighted average exchange rates of the NT dollar per U.S. dollar appreciating from NT$32.13 in 2024 to NT$31.11 in 2025.
- As TSMC's emissions from each fab in Taiwan exceed the current regulatory threshold, the company will start to pay carbon fees from 2026 (for the 2025 fees), which will result in increased manufacturing costs.

**Subsequent events**
- In February 2025, Longitude Licensing Ltd. and Marlin Semiconductor Limited filed complaints with the U.S. International Trade Commission and the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas alleging that TSMC and its customers infringe five U.S. patents; the ITC instituted an investigation on March 21, 2025 and the Texas lawsuit was statutorily stayed on April 23, 2025 pending the ITC investigation.
- The fourth quarter of 2025 cash dividend of NT$6.0 per share was approved on February 10, 2026, with a payment date of July 9, 2026.

> "We believe that our cash generated from operations, cash and cash equivalents, current marketable securities, and ability to access capital market will be sufficient to fund our working capital needs, capital expenditures, debt repayments, dividend payments and other business requirements associated with existing operations over the next 12 months." — TSMC (Item 5, Liquidity and Capital Resources)

> "Our capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be between US$52 billion and US$56 billion, which, depending on market conditions, may be adjusted later." — TSMC (Item 5, Capital Expenditures)

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Customer concentration: the ten largest customers accounted for approximately 78% of net revenue in 2025, up from 76% in 2024 and 70% in 2023, and the largest customer accounted for 19% of net revenue in 2025. | our ten largest customers in 2023, 2024 and 2025 accounted for approximately, 70%, 76% and 78% of our net revenue in the respective year |
| 2 | Trade and export-control measures: U.S. export controls may require an export license prior to shipping products using 16-nanometer or below process to specified destinations, and tariffs on semiconductor imports could raise costs and reduce demand. | we may need to obtain an export license prior to shipping products using 16-nanometer or below process to specified destinations unless specific conditions are met |
| 3 | Natural-disaster exposure: earthquakes in April 2024 and January 2025 caused damage to inventories, plant facilities, machinery and equipment, with recognized losses net of insurance claims. | We recognized approximately NT$3 billion and NT$5.3 billion in losses from earthquakes, net of insurance claim, respectively, in the second quarter of 2024 and the first quarter of 2025. |
| 4 | Intellectual property litigation: the ITC investigation and related Texas lawsuit filed by Marlin alleging infringement of five U.S. patents, with the outcome and any contingent liability not reliably estimable. | The outcome cannot be determined, and we cannot make a reliable estimate of the contingent liability at this time. |
| 5 | Government incentive dependence: TSMC Arizona entered agreements with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to US$6.6 billion in total direct funding and up to US$5 billion of proposed loans under the U.S. CHIPS Act, and ESMC entered an agreement with Germany for up to EUR5 billion of state aid under the European Chips Act. | which includes up to US$6.6 billion in total direct funding and up to US$5 billion of proposed loans |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: As of December 31, 2025, short-term loans were nil and aggregate long-term debts were TWD 1,032,988 million (US$32,929 million), of which TWD 136,926 million (US$4,365 million) was classified as current; the long-term debt mainly included NT dollar- and U.S. dollar-denominated corporate bonds with fixed interest rates ranging from 0.41% to 4.63% and remaining maturity ranging from less than one year to 35 years. Shareholders' equity was TWD 5,396,219 million.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents and current marketable securities increased to TWD 3,068,595 million (US$97,820 million) as of December 31, 2025, compared with TWD 2,422,019 million as of December 31, 2024; the current marketable securities primarily consisted of fixed income securities.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating TWD 2275.0B, investing TWD -1144.4B, financing TWD -440.3B.

Working capital: Current assets TWD 3817.1B vs. current liabilities TWD 1522.4B (current ratio 2.51x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: TWD 3088.4B vs. TWD 1308.7B (2.36x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Total contractual cash obligations as of December 31, 2025 were TWD 2,993,762 million, of which TWD 1,528,155 million is due in less than one year, including capital purchase or other purchase obligations of TWD 1,534,575 million in total.
- Long-Term Debt contractual payments total TWD 1,229,859 million, comprising TWD 156,822 million due in less than one year, TWD 321,847 million in one to three years, TWD 238,883 million in three to five years and TWD 512,307 million in more than five years.

| Taxation and investment tax credits | The corporate income tax rate in the R.O.C. is 20%; the alternative minimum tax rate for business entities is 12%; eligible companies may claim investment tax credit of 25% on qualified R&D expenditure and 5% on procurement of machinery/equipment for advanced processes under the amended R.O.C. Statute for Industrial Innovation. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

TSMC's FY2025 net revenue rose 31.6% to NT$3,809,054 million and net income rose 46.4% to NT$1,695,125 million, with gross margin expanding to 59.9%.

Revenue growth accelerated on advanced-node mix and higher wafer shipments, lifting gross, operating and net margins versus 2024.

- Net revenue of NT$3,809,054 million (US$121,423 million) increased 31.6% from NT$2,894,308 million in 2024, attributed by management to higher ASP from a greater proportion of advanced technology (7-nanometer and below) revenue and increased wafer shipments, partially offset by NT dollar appreciation.
- Net income of NT$1,695,125 million (US$54,036 million) rose 46.4% from NT$1,157,524 million, and diluted EPS was NT$65.47 versus NT$44.67.
- Gross margin expanded to 59.9% from 56.1%, which management attributed to higher capacity utilization and cost improvement, partially offset by an unfavorable foreign exchange rate.
- Advanced technologies (7-nanometer and below) accounted for 74% of total wafer revenue, up from 69% in 2024, with 3-nanometer at 24% and 5-nanometer at 36%.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net revenue | NT$3,809,054M | NT$2,894,308M | +31.6% | Management attributed the increase mainly to higher ASP from a greater proportion of advanced technology revenue and increased wafer shipments, partially offset by NT dollar appreciation. |
| Gross profit | NT$2,281,294M | NT$1,624,354M | +40.4% | Gross margin rose to 59.9% from 56.1%, mainly attributable to higher capacity utilization and cost improvement, partially offset by unfavorable foreign exchange rate. |
| Income from operations | NT$1,936,092M | NT$1,322,053M | +46.5% | Operating margin expanded to 50.8% from 45.7%. |
| Net income | NT$1,695,125M | NT$1,157,524M | +46.4% | Income tax expense increased 39.6%, mainly attributed to higher taxable income in 2025. |
| Net income attributable to shareholders of the parent | NT$1,697,604M | NT$1,158,380M | +46.5% | Net margin attributable to shareholders of the parent was 44.6% in 2025 versus 40.0% in 2024. |
| EPS (Diluted) | NT$65.47 | NT$44.67 | +46.6% | Not disclosed |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income rose 46.4% to NT$1,936,092 million, with operating margin at 50.8%. Non-operating income increased 26.0% to NT$105,563 million, mainly due to higher interest income of NT$18,526 million compared to 2024. Net other operating income and expenses swung to a net gain of NT$447 million, mainly due to lower loss on disposal of property, plant and equipment and reversal of impairment losses in 2025.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion).

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid TWD 466.8B (prior TWD 363.1B).

Capital expenditures for 2025 were NT$1,272,411 million, primarily for installing and expanding capacity for 2-nanometer, 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer nodes, specialty technologies and advanced packaging, and R&D projects. The company issued NT dollar-denominated corporate bonds totaling NT$86,900 million in 2025. Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be between US$52 billion and US$56 billion.

Return on equity was 31.4% (prior 27.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 21.4% (prior 17.3%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Board of Directors authorized quarterly cash dividends; fourth quarter of 2025 dividend of NT$6.0 per share approved February 10, 2026, payable July 9, 2026.
- In 2025, TSMC issued NT dollar-denominated corporate bonds totaling NT$86,900 million (US$2,770 million).

## Forward Signals

Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be between US$52 billion and US$56 billion, which, depending on market conditions, may be adjusted later.

**Known trends**
- The NT dollar appreciation in 2025 had an unfavorable effect on revenue, with weighted average exchange rates of the NT dollar per U.S. dollar appreciating from NT$32.13 in 2024 to NT$31.11 in 2025.
- As emissions from each fab in Taiwan exceed the current regulatory threshold, TSMC will start to pay carbon fees from 2026 (for the 2025 fees), which will result in increased manufacturing costs.

**Subsequent events**
- In February 2025, Longitude Licensing Ltd. and Marlin Semiconductor Limited filed complaints with the U.S. International Trade Commission and the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas alleging that TSMC and its customers infringe five U.S. patents; the ITC instituted an investigation on March 21, 2025 and the lawsuit was statutorily stayed on April 23, 2025 pending the ITC investigation.

> "We plan to continue our investment in technology research and development in 2026." — TSMC

| 2 | Trade and export-control measures: U.S. export controls require a license prior to shipping products using 16-nanometer or below process to specified destinations unless specific conditions are met. | we may need to obtain an export license prior to shipping products using 16-nanometer or below process to specified destinations unless specific conditions are met |
| 3 | Earthquake losses: TSMC recognized approximately NT$3 billion and NT$5.3 billion in losses from earthquakes, net of insurance claims, in the second quarter of 2024 and the first quarter of 2025, respectively. | We recognized approximately NT$3 billion and NT$5.3 billion in losses from earthquakes, net of insurance claim, respectively, in the second quarter of 2024 and the first quarter of 2025. |
| 4 | Intellectual property litigation: the Marlin complaints before the ITC and the Eastern District of Texas allege infringement of five U.S. patents, with the outcome not determinable and no reliable estimate of contingent liability. | The outcome cannot be determined, and we cannot make a reliable estimate of the contingent liability at this time. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: As of December 31, 2025, short-term loans were nil and aggregate long-term debts were NT$1,032,988 million (US$32,929 million), of which NT$136,926 million (US$4,365 million) was classified as current. Cash, cash equivalents and current marketable securities were NT$3,068,595 million (US$97,820 million), compared to NT$2,422,019 million as of December 31, 2024.

Liquidity: TSMC believes that its cash generated from operations, cash and cash equivalents, current marketable securities, and ability to access capital markets will be sufficient to fund working capital needs, capital expenditures, debt repayments, dividend payments and other business requirements over the next 12 months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating TWD 2275.0B, investing TWD -1144.4B, financing TWD -440.3B.

Working capital: Current assets TWD 3817.1B vs. current liabilities TWD 1522.4B (current ratio 2.51x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: TWD 3088.4B vs. TWD 1308.7B (2.36x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt mainly included NT dollar- and U.S. dollar-denominated corporate bonds with fixed interest rates ranging from 0.41% to 4.63% and remaining maturity ranging from less than one year to 35 years.
- Total contractual cash obligations as of December 31, 2025 were NT$2,993,762 million, of which NT$1,528,155 million is due in less than one year.

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of NT$1,936,092 million was supported by net non-operating income of NT$105,563 million, which management attributed mainly to higher interest income of NT$18,526 million compared to 2024; net other operating income and expenses swung to a net gain of NT$447 million from a net loss of NT$1,230 million, mainly due to lower loss on disposal of property, plant and equipment and reversal of impairment losses in 2025. Foreign exchange gain, net, was NT$13,831 million in 2025 versus NT$10,001 million in 2024.

Operating cash flow was 1.3x net income (cash conversion).

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid TWD 466.8B (prior TWD 363.1B).

Capital expenditure of NT$1,272,411 million in 2025 was directed at installing and expanding capacity mainly for 2-nanometer, 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer nodes, including building/facility expansion for Fab 20, Fab 21 and Fab 22, expanding capacity for specialty technologies and advanced packaging including Fab 23 and Fab 24, and investing in research and development projects for new process technologies. The company stated it believes cash generated from operations, cash and cash equivalents, current marketable securities, and ability to access capital markets will be sufficient to fund working capital needs, capital expenditures, debt repayments, dividend payments and other business requirements over the next 12 months. Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be between US$52 billion and US$56 billion.

Return on equity was 31.4% (prior 27.0%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 21.4% (prior 17.3%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Board of Directors authorized quarterly cash dividends, with 2025 quarterly dividends of NT$5.00001754, NT$5.00001118, NT$6.00003573 and NT$6.0 per share for the first through fourth quarters respectively.
- In 2025 the company issued NT dollar-denominated corporate bonds totaling NT$86,900 million (US$2,770 million).

## Forward Signals

Capital expenditures for 2026 are expected to be between US$52 billion and US$56 billion, which, depending on market conditions, may be adjusted later. The company also stated it plans to continue its investment in technology research and development in 2026.

**Known trends**
- The NT dollar appreciation in 2025 had an unfavorable effect on revenue, with weighted average exchange rates of the NT dollar per U.S. dollar appreciating from NT$32.13 in 2024 to NT$31.11 in 2025.
- As emissions from each fab in Taiwan exceed the current regulatory threshold, the company will start to pay carbon fees from 2026 (for the 2025 fees), which will result in increased manufacturing costs.
- The VEU authorization for the Nanjing fab expired in December 2025, and the U.S. Department of Commerce has granted TSMC Nanjing an annual export license; there is no assurance that this annual export license will not be terminated, or that it can be timely renewed.

**Subsequent events**
- In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court declared the IEEPA reciprocal tariffs unlawful; following the ruling, the U.S. imposed a replacement tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 and in March 2026 the U.S. Trade Representative initiated two Section 301 investigations targeting various economies, including Taiwan.
- In January 2026, the U.S. announced it had reached a trade and investment agreement with Taiwan which would reduce U.S. reciprocal tariff rates on Taiwanese goods to no more than 15%, and grants preferential Section 232 treatment for Taiwanese semiconductor producers investing in U.S. manufacturing capacity.

| 2 | Trade and export-control measures: in January 2025 the U.S. issued new rules under which the company may need an export license prior to shipping products using 16-nanometer or below process to specified destinations unless specific conditions are met, and the Nanjing fab's VEU authorization expired in December 2025. | we may need to obtain an export license prior to shipping products using 16-nanometer or below process to specified destinations unless specific conditions are met |
| 3 | Intellectual property litigation: in February 2025 Longitude Licensing Ltd. and Marlin Semiconductor Limited filed complaints with the U.S. ITC and the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas alleging that TSMC and its customers infringe five U.S. patents; the outcome cannot be determined and no reliable estimate of the contingent liability can be made. | The outcome cannot be determined, and we cannot make a reliable estimate of the contingent liability at this time. |
| 4 | Natural disaster exposure: in April 2024 and January 2025 several earthquakes struck Taiwan, causing damage to inventories, plant facilities, machinery and equipment, with recognized losses of approximately NT$3 billion and NT$5.3 billion net of insurance claims in the second quarter of 2024 and the first quarter of 2025 respectively. | We recognized approximately NT$3 billion and NT$5.3 billion in losses from earthquakes, net of insurance claim, respectively, in the second quarter of 2024 and the first quarter of 2025. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: As of December 31, 2025, short-term loans were nil and aggregate long-term debts were NT$1,032,988 million (US$32,929 million), of which NT$136,926 million (US$4,365 million) was classified as current; long-term debt mainly comprised NT dollar- and U.S. dollar-denominated corporate bonds with fixed interest rates ranging from 0.41% to 4.63% and remaining maturity ranging from less than one year to 35 years. Shareholders' equity was NT$5,396,219 million.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents and current marketable securities increased to NT$3,068,595 million (US$97,820 million) as of December 31, 2025, compared to NT$2,422,019 million as of December 31, 2024; the company stated it believes these sources plus cash generated from operations and ability to access capital markets will be sufficient to fund requirements over the next 12 months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating TWD 2275.0B, investing TWD -1144.4B, financing TWD -440.3B.

Working capital: Current assets TWD 3817.1B vs. current liabilities TWD 1522.4B (current ratio 2.51x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: TWD 3088.4B vs. TWD 1308.7B (2.36x).

- Total contractual cash obligations of NT$2,993,762 million as of December 31, 2025, of which NT$1,528,155 million is due in less than one year, including capital purchase or other purchase obligations of NT$1,534,575 million.

the_print.headline: TSMC's FY2025 net revenue rose 31.6% to NT$3,809,054 million (US$121,423 million) and net income rose 46.4% to NT$1,695,125 million, with gross margin expanding to 59.9%.
key_takeaways: Net revenue of NT$3,809,054 million (US$121,423 million) increased 31.6% from NT$2,894,308 million in 2024, attributed by management to higher ASP from a greater proportion of advanced technology (7-nanometer and below) revenue and increased wafer shipments, partially offset by NT dollar appreciation.

Net income of NT$1,695,125 million (US$54,036 million) rose 46.4% from NT$1,157,524 million; net income attributable to shareholders of the parent was NT$1,697,604 million (US$54,116 million), up 46.5%.

Gross margin expanded to 59.9% from 56.1% and operating margin to 50.8% from 45.7%, which management attributed mainly to higher capacity utilization and cost improvement, partially offset by an unfavorable foreign exchange rate.
Advanced technologies (7-nanometer and below) accounted for 74% of total wafer revenue, up from 69% in 2024, with 3-nanometer at 24%, 5-nanometer at 36% and 7-nanometer at 14%.
the_print.what_changed: Revenue growth accelerated to 31.6% in 2025 from 33.9% in 2024 on a larger base, with gross margin up 3.8 percentage points and net margin up 4.5 percentage points, while the NT dollar appreciated to a weighted average of NT$31.11 per US dollar from NT$32.13.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

JD.com's FY2025 total net revenues rose 13.0% to CNY 1,309.1B, but net income fell to CNY 23.1B from CNY 44.7B as operating income collapsed to CNY 2.8B on a CNY 46.6B operating loss in New Businesses.

Operating income and net income declined sharply year over year despite double-digit revenue growth, as strategic investment in new business initiatives (JD Food Delivery and Jingxi) drove a CNY 46.6B operating loss in the New Businesses segment.

- Total net revenues of CNY 1,309.1B (US$187.2B at the filing's stated rate) rose 13.0% from CNY 1,158.8B in 2024.
- Net income of CNY 23.1B (US$3.3B) fell from CNY 44.7B in 2024; basic net income per share was CNY 6.89 versus CNY 13.83.
- Income from operations fell to CNY 2.8B from CNY 38.7B, driven by a CNY 46.6B operating loss in New Businesses.
- Net cash provided by operating activities fell to CNY 19.0B from CNY 58.1B, while investing activities swung to a CNY 41.8B inflow from a CNY 0.9B outflow.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net revenues | CNY 1,309,085M | CNY 1,158,819M | +13.0% | Management attributes the increase to supply chain capabilities, user experience and mindshare investments, and improved price competitiveness and platform ecosystem at JD Retail, plus logistics growth and rapid scaling of JD Food Delivery and Jingxi. |
| Income from operations | CNY 2,774M | CNY 38,736M | −92.8% | Management attributes the decline primarily to increased strategic investment in new business initiatives. |
| Net income | CNY 23,142M | CNY 44,660M | −48.2% | Management states net income was CNY 23,142 million in 2025 as compared to CNY 44,660 million in 2024, as a result of the foregoing. |
| Net income per share — basic | CNY 6.89 | CNY 13.83 | −50.2% | Not disclosed |
| Net income per share — diluted | CNY 6.45 | CNY 13.43 | −52.0% | Not disclosed |
| Net income per ADS — basic | CNY 13.79 | CNY 27.67 | −50.2% | Each ADS represents two Class A ordinary shares. |
| Net income per ADS — diluted | CNY 12.90 | CNY 26.86 | −52.0% | Not disclosed |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income fell to CNY 2.8B from CNY 38.7B, while non-operating items partly offset the decline: share of results of equity investees was a gain of CNY 8.0B (up from CNY 2.3B) and 'Others, net' was a gain of CNY 17.3B (up from CNY 13.4B), which management attributes primarily to decreased impairment losses related to equity investments. Income tax expense fell to CNY 2.2B from CNY 6.9B. Net income attributable to non-controlling interests was CNY 3.5B, versus CNY 3.3B in 2024.

Operating cash flow was 0.8x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of CNY 11.2B.

**Red flag:** Net income fell 48.2% to CNY 23.1B while non-operating gains (share of equity investees of CNY 8.0B and 'Others, net' of CNY 17.3B) exceeded operating income of CNY 2.8B, indicating reported profitability was supported by items below the operating line.

**Red flag:** Impairment of goodwill of CNY 1,303M was recorded in 2025, following CNY 799M in 2024 and CNY 3,143M in 2023, indicating recurring goodwill impairment charges.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid CNY 10.4B (prior CNY 8.3B), share repurchases CNY 21.4B (prior CNY 25.9B); capital expenditures CNY 7.8B (prior CNY 5.4B).

Capital allocation in 2025 combined continued shareholder returns with a step-up in strategic investment: the company repurchased CNY 21.4B of ordinary shares (down from CNY 25.9B in 2024), paid CNY 10.4B in dividends (up from CNY 8.3B), and increased capital expenditures to CNY 7.8B from CNY 5.4B. The company also issued CNY 6.0B of corporate bonds in three tranches under a CNY 10.0B registered program and completed a post-period RMB7.5B and RMB2.5B notes offering in April 2026. The allocation is framed as funding new business initiatives while maintaining returns to shareholders.

Return on equity was 10.3% (prior 18.7%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 3.3% (prior 6.4%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In March 2026, the company declared an annual cash dividend for the year ended December 31, 2025 of US$0.5 per ordinary share, or US$1.0 per ADS, for an aggregate amount of approximately US$1.4 billion.
- In 2025, the company was granted CSRC approval to issue public offering corporate bonds to professional investors with an aggregate registered principal amount of up to RMB10.0 billion, of which RMB6.0 billion was issued in three tranches.
- In April 2026, the company completed the offering of RMB7.5 billion 2.05% notes due 2031 and RMB2.5 billion 2.75% notes due 2036, with proceeds partially used to repay certain existing borrowings and related interest.

## Forward Signals

No quantitative financial guidance is provided in the filing. Management states it believes it has sufficient working capital for present requirements and for at least the next 12 months from the date of the annual report, taking into account cash and cash equivalents on hand, operating cash flows, and available bank facilities.

**Known trends**
- Management states it has experienced and expects to continue to experience upward pressure on operating expenses.
- Management states it expects fulfillment expenses to increase in absolute amount on an annual basis in the near run, as it invests in new businesses, builds and leases new warehouses and establishes more delivery stations.
- Management states personnel costs are the largest component of fulfillment and research and development costs and are likely to remain the largest component for the foreseeable future as operations expand, and that labor costs are rising in China.

**Subsequent events**
- In March 2026, the company declared an annual cash dividend for the year ended December 31, 2025 of US$0.5 per ordinary share, or US$1.0 per ADS, for an aggregate amount of approximately US$1.4 billion.
- In April 2026, the company completed the offering of RMB7.5 billion 2.05% notes due 2031 and RMB2.5 billion 2.75% notes due 2036, with proceeds partially used to repay certain existing borrowings and related interest.
- In March 2026, all outstanding balance of the borrowings under the December 2021 US$2.0 billion green loan facility was early repaid in full.

> "Taking into account cash and cash equivalents on hand, our operating cash flows, and the available bank facilities, we believe that we have sufficient working capital for our present requirements and for at least the next 12 months from the date of this annual report." — JD.com, Inc. (Item 5.B. Liquidity and Capital Resources)

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | JD.com, Inc. is a Cayman Islands holding company with no equity ownership in the consolidated variable interest entities (VIEs); it relies on contractual arrangements to control and consolidate them, and the filing states these arrangements may not be as effective as direct ownership and have not been tested in PRC courts. | JD.com, Inc. is not an operating company but a Cayman Islands holding company with no equity ownership in the consolidated variable interest entities, but maintains contractual arrangements with the consolidated variable interest entities and is considered the primary beneficiary of these entities |
| 2 | The filing states that if the PRC government determines the VIE contractual arrangements do not comply with PRC laws and regulations, or if laws change or are interpreted differently, the company could be subject to severe penalties or be forced to relinquish its interests in those operations. | If the PRC government determines that the contractual arrangements constituting part of the consolidated variable interest entities structure do not comply with PRC laws and regulations, or if these laws and regulations change or are interpreted differently in the future, we could be subject to severe penalties or be forced to relinquish our interests in those operations. |
| 3 | The filing states that if the PCAOB determines in the future that it no longer has full access to inspect and investigate completely accounting firms in the Chinese mainland and Hong Kong, and the company continues to use such an auditor, it would be identified as a Commission-Identified Issuer, and if so identified for two consecutive years would become subject to the HFCAA trading prohibition. | If PCAOB determines in the future that it no longer has full access to inspect and investigate completely accounting firms in the Chinese mainland and Hong Kong and we continue to use an accounting firm headquartered in one of these jurisdictions to issue an audit report on our financial statements filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, we would be identified as a Commission-Identified Issuer following the filing of the annual report on Form 20-F for the relevant fiscal year. |
| 4 | The filing states that PRC laws and regulations restrict the company's ability to provide funding to its wholly foreign-owned subsidiaries in the Chinese mainland (only through loans or capital contributions, subject to government approval and limits) and to the consolidated VIEs (only through entrusted loans), and that amounts restricted, including paid-in capital and statutory reserve funds, were approximately RMB78.2 billion as of December 31, 2025. | As a Cayman Islands exempted company and offshore holding company, we are permitted under PRC laws and regulations to provide funding to our wholly foreign-owned subsidiaries in the Chinese mainland only through loans or capital contributions, subject to the approval of government authorities and limits on the amount of capital contributions and loans. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt increased: long-term debt rose to CNY 41.7B from CNY 31.7B, and short-term debts were CNY 8.0B as of December 31, 2025 (versus CNY 7.6B as of December 31, 2024), while cash and cash equivalents rose to CNY 137.5B from CNY 108.4B. Total shareholders' equity fell to CNY 293.8B from CNY 312.8B, with total JD.com, Inc. shareholders' equity of CNY 225.0B (down from CNY 239.3B) and non-controlling interests of CNY 68.7B (down from CNY 73.5B).

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of CNY 137.5B as of December 31, 2025, plus revolving lines of credit of CNY 304.0B from commercial banks, of which CNY 243.1B was unused. Management states it believes it has sufficient working capital for present requirements and for at least the next 12 months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating CNY 19.0B, investing CNY 41.8B, financing CNY -26.7B.

Working capital: Current assets CNY 374.4B vs. current liabilities CNY 306.1B (current ratio 1.22x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: CNY 386.7B vs. CNY 299.5B (1.29x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- The unsecured senior notes contain covenants including, among others, limitation on liens, and restriction on consolidation, merger and sale of all or substantially all of our assets; the company states it is in compliance with all the covenants.
- The 2029 Notes will mature on June 1, 2029, unless earlier redeemed, repurchased or converted; holders may require repurchase on June 1, 2027 or in the event of certain fundamental changes at 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest.
- In March 2026, all outstanding balance of the borrowings under the December 2021 US$2.0 billion green loan facility was early repaid in full.

## Notable Footnotes

| VIE consolidation and financial information | The consolidated VIEs' total net revenues were RMB88,489 million for 2025 (down from RMB101,218 million in 2024), and their total assets were RMB64,501 million as of December 31, 2025 (down from RMB85,451 million as of December 31, 2024). The external revenues contributed by the consolidated VIEs accounted for 6.8% of total revenues for 2025. |
| Convenience translation rate | US$ figures throughout the filing are convenience translations calculated at a stated rate of US$1.00 = RMB6.9931, the noon buying rate on December 31, 2025; the RMB amounts are authoritative. |
| Reclassifications | Certain reclassifications were made to prior years' consolidated financial statements to conform to the current year's presentation; the filing states these had no impact on net income, shareholders' equity, or cash flows as previously reported. |
| Segment reporting change | From the first quarter of 2024, the company reports three reportable segments (JD Retail, JD Logistics and New Businesses), replacing the prior four-segment structure that included Dada; prior periods' segment operating results were retrospectively recast. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

JD.com reported FY2025 total net revenues of CNY 1,309.1B (up 13.0% YoY) while net income fell to CNY 23.1B from CNY 44.7B, as operating income compressed to CNY 2.8B from CNY 38.7B on strategic investment in new business initiatives.

Revenue growth accelerated to 13.0% while profitability compressed sharply, with operating income down to CNY 2.8B from CNY 38.7B as the company funded new business initiatives including JD Food Delivery.

- Total net revenues rose 13.0% to CNY 1,309.1B (US$187.2B convenience translation at the filing's stated rate of US$1.00=RMB6.9931), with net service revenues up 23.6% to CNY 285.3B and net product revenues up 10.3% to CNY 1,023.8B.
- Operating income fell to CNY 2.8B (0.2% margin) from CNY 38.7B (3.3% margin), which management attributed to increased strategic investment in new business initiatives.
- Net income was CNY 23.1B (1.8% net margin) versus CNY 44.7B (3.9%) in 2024; basic net income per ADS was CNY 13.79 versus CNY 27.67.
- New Businesses revenue grew 157.3% to CNY 49.3B, driven by the scaling of JD Food Delivery and Jingxi, while the segment recorded an operating loss of CNY 46.6B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net revenues | CNY 1,309,085M | CNY 1,158,819M | +13.0% | Growth driven by JD Retail, JD Logistics and rapid scaling of New Businesses. |
| Income from operations | CNY 2,774M | CNY 38,736M | −92.8% | Decline primarily attributable to increased strategic investment in new business initiatives. |
| Net income | CNY 23,142M | CNY 44,660M | −48.2% | Result of the foregoing operating and other income items. |
| Net income per ADS, basic | CNY 13.79 | CNY 27.67 | −50.2% | Each ADS represents two Class A ordinary shares. |
| Net income per ADS, diluted | CNY 12.90 | CNY 26.86 | −52.0% | Each ADS represents two Class A ordinary shares. |
| Net income per share, basic | CNY 6.89 | CNY 13.83 | −50.2% | Weighted average basic shares declined to 2,847,199,686 from 2,989,701,855. |
| Net income per share, diluted | CNY 6.45 | CNY 13.43 | −52.0% | Weighted average diluted shares declined to 2,978,037,127 from 3,076,061,616. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of CNY 2.8B was substantially below net income of CNY 23.1B, with the gap filled by non-operating items: share of results of equity investees of CNY 8.0B (up from CNY 2.3B), others, net of CNY 17.3B (up from CNY 13.4B, which management attributed primarily to decreased impairment losses related to equity investments), and a CNY 2.2B income tax benefit versus CNY 6.9B expense in 2024. Non-cash charges included depreciation and amortization of CNY 9.7B, share-based compensation of CNY 4.7B, and impairment of goodwill, long-lived assets and equity investments totaling CNY 2.1B.

Operating cash flow was 0.8x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of CNY 11.2B.

**Red flag:** Operating income of CNY 2.8B was only 12.0% of net income of CNY 23.1B, with the majority of earnings derived from equity investee results, other non-operating gains and a tax benefit.

**Red flag:** Income tax flipped from CNY 6,878M expense in 2024 to a CNY 2,181M benefit in 2025, contributing to net income despite the operating income decline.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid CNY 10.4B (prior CNY 8.3B), share repurchases CNY 21.4B (prior CNY 25.9B); capital expenditures CNY 7.8B (prior CNY 5.4B).

Capital allocation in FY2025 combined continued shareholder returns with elevated investment in new business initiatives. Dividends paid rose to CNY 10.4B from CNY 8.3B, and share repurchases of CNY 21.4B were below the prior year's CNY 25.9B. Capital expenditures increased to CNY 7.8B from CNY 5.4B. The company also completed the Hong Kong listing of JD Industrials in December 2025, raising approximately RMB2.6 billion in net proceeds, and issued RMB6.0 billion of corporate bonds in three tranches under a RMB10.0 billion registered program.

Return on equity was 10.3% (prior 18.7%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 3.3% (prior 6.4%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In March 2026, the company declared an annual cash dividend for the year ended December 31, 2025 of US$0.5 per ordinary share, or US$1.0 per ADS, for an aggregate amount of approximately US$1.4 billion.
- In April 2026, the company completed the offering of RMB7.5 billion 2.05% notes due 2031 and RMB2.5 billion 2.75% notes due 2036, with proceeds partially used to repay certain existing borrowings and related interest.
- On December 11, 2025, shares of JD Industrials commenced trading on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under the stock code "7618," raising approximately RMB2.6 billion in net proceeds.

## Forward Signals

No quantitative financial guidance was provided in the filing. Management stated it believes it has sufficient working capital for present requirements and for at least the next 12 months from the date of the annual report, taking into account cash and cash equivalents on hand, operating cash flows, and available bank facilities.

**Known trends**
- The company expects fulfillment expenses to increase in absolute amount on an annual basis in the near run, as it invests in new businesses, builds and leases new warehouses and establishes more delivery stations to penetrate lower tier cities.
- The company has experienced and expects to continue to experience upward pressure on its operating expenses.
- Labor costs are rising in China and the company strives to continue improving efficiency and utilization of its fulfillment and other personnel to mitigate this effect.

**Subsequent events**
- In March 2026, the company declared an annual cash dividend for the year ended December 31, 2025 of US$0.5 per ordinary share, or US$1.0 per ADS, for an aggregate amount of approximately US$1.4 billion.
- In April 2026, the company completed the offering of RMB7.5 billion 2.05% notes due 2031 and RMB2.5 billion 2.75% notes due 2036.
- In March 2026, all outstanding balance of the borrowings under the December 2021 US$2.0 billion green loan facility was early repaid in full.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

JD.com's FY2025 total net revenues rose 13.0% to CNY 1,309.1B, but income from operations fell to CNY 2.8B from CNY 38.7B as New Businesses recorded an operating loss of CNY 46.6B.

The filing reports a shift from prior-year operating profitability to a near-breakeven operating result, driven by a CNY 46.6B operating loss in New Businesses, alongside a decline in operating cash flow and a swing to positive investing cash flow.

- Total net revenues increased 13.0% to CNY 1,309.1B (US$187.2B at the filing's convenience rate of US$1.00=RMB6.9931), with net service revenues up 23.6% to CNY 285.3B.
- Income from operations declined to CNY 2.8B from CNY 38.7B; the New Businesses segment posted an operating loss of CNY 46.6B, which management attributed to increased strategic investment in new business initiatives.
- Net income was CNY 23.1B (US$3.3B), down from CNY 44.7B, and net income attributable to the Company's ordinary shareholders was CNY 19.6B.
- Net cash provided by operating activities fell to CNY 19.0B from CNY 58.1B, while net cash provided by investing activities was CNY 41.8B versus net cash used of CNY 0.9B in 2024.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total net revenues | CNY 1,309,085M | CNY 1,158,819M | +13.0% | Management attributed the increase to growth across JD Retail, JD Logistics and New Businesses. |
| Income from operations | CNY 2,774M | CNY 38,736M | −92.8% | Management attributed the decline primarily to increased strategic investment in new business initiatives. |
| Net income | CNY 23,142M | CNY 44,660M | −48.2% | Management stated net income was a result of the foregoing factors, including the operating loss in New Businesses. |
| Net income attributable to the Company's ordinary shareholders | CNY 19,631M | CNY 41,359M | −52.5% | The decline reflects the lower consolidated net income and an increase in net income attributable to non-controlling interests shareholders. |
| Basic net income per share | CNY 6.89 | CNY 13.83 | −50.2% | Per-share results reflect the lower net income attributable to ordinary shareholders and a reduced weighted average share count. |
| Diluted net income per share | CNY 6.45 | CNY 13.43 | −52.0% | Diluted per-share results reflect the lower net income attributable to ordinary shareholders and a reduced weighted average share count. |
| Basic net income per ADS | CNY 13.79 | CNY 27.67 | −50.2% | Each ADS represents two Class A ordinary shares. |
| Diluted net income per ADS | CNY 12.90 | CNY 26.86 | −52.0% | Each ADS represents two Class A ordinary shares. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported income from operations fell to CNY 2.8B from CNY 38.7B, while non-operating items partly offset the decline: share of results of equity investees was a gain of CNY 8.0B (versus CNY 2.3B in 2024) and 'Others, net' was a gain of CNY 17.3B (versus CNY 13.4B), which management attributed primarily to decreased impairment losses related to equity investments. The company also recorded a CNY 1.3B goodwill impairment and a CNY 0.4B gain on sale of development properties.

Operating cash flow was 0.8x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of CNY 11.2B.

**Red flag:** Net cash provided by operating activities fell to CNY 19.0B from CNY 58.1B, a decline of 67.3%, while net income was CNY 23.1B, indicating operating cash flow was below net income for the year.

**Red flag:** Marketing expenses increased 75.1% to CNY 84.0B, outpacing the 13.0% increase in total net revenues, which management attributed primarily to increased spending in promotional efforts for new business initiatives.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid CNY 10.4B (prior CNY 8.3B), share repurchases CNY 21.4B (prior CNY 25.9B); capital expenditures CNY 7.8B (prior CNY 5.4B).

Capital allocation in FY2025 combined continued shareholder returns with increased investment in new business initiatives. Dividends paid rose to CNY 10.4B from CNY 8.3B, and share repurchases were CNY 21.4B, down from CNY 25.9B. Capital expenditures increased to CNY 7.8B from CNY 5.4B. The company also issued CNY 6.0B of corporate bonds in three tranches under a CNY 10.0B registered program and, in April 2026, completed an offering of RMB7.5 billion 2.05% notes due 2031 and RMB2.5 billion 2.75% notes due 2036, proceeds of which were partially used to repay certain existing borrowings and related interest.

Return on equity was 10.3% (prior 18.7%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 3.3% (prior 6.4%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- In March 2026, the company declared an annual cash dividend for the year ended December 31, 2025 of US$0.5 per ordinary share, or US$1.0 per ADS, for an aggregate amount of approximately US$1.4 billion.
- In 2025, the company was granted approval by the China Securities Regulatory Commission to issue public offering corporate bonds to professional investors with an aggregate registered principal amount of up to RMB10.0 billion, of which RMB6.0 billion was issued in three tranches during the year.
- In April 2026, the company completed the offering of RMB7.5 billion 2.05% notes due 2031 and RMB2.5 billion 2.75% notes due 2036 in reliance on Regulation S.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide quantitative financial guidance. Management states it believes it has sufficient working capital for present requirements and for at least the next 12 months from the date of the annual report, taking into account cash and cash equivalents on hand, operating cash flows, and available bank facilities.

**Known trends**
- Management states it has experienced and expects to continue to experience upward pressure on operating expenses.
- Management states it expects fulfillment expenses to increase in absolute amount on an annual basis in the near run, as it invests in new businesses, builds and leases new warehouses and establishes more delivery stations.
- Management states personnel costs are the largest component of fulfillment costs and research and development costs and are likely to remain the largest component for the foreseeable future as operations expand, and that labor costs are rising in China.

**Subsequent events**
- In March 2026, the company declared an annual cash dividend for the year ended December 31, 2025 of US$0.5 per ordinary share, or US$1.0 per ADS, for an aggregate amount of approximately US$1.4 billion.
- In April 2026, the company completed the offering of RMB7.5 billion 2.05% notes due 2031 and RMB2.5 billion 2.75% notes due 2036 in reliance on Regulation S under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended.
- In March 2026, all outstanding balance of the borrowings under the December 2021 five-year US$2.0 billion unsecured term and revolving loan facility was early repaid in full.

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The company operates parts of its business through consolidated variable interest entities (VIEs) in which it has no equity ownership; external revenues contributed by the consolidated VIEs accounted for 6.8% of total revenues in 2025, down from 8.7% in 2024. | The external revenues contributed by the consolidated variable interest entities accounted for 7.8%, 8.7% and 6.8% of our total revenues for the years of 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. |
| 2 | The company is subject to PRC regulatory oversight, including CSRC filing requirements for overseas offerings under the Trial Measures, and potential cybersecurity review by the CAC. | According to the Trial Measures, domestic companies in the Chinese mainland that directly or indirectly offer or list their securities in an overseas market are required to file with the CSRC. |
| 3 | The company's ADSs could be prohibited from trading in the United States under the HFCAA if the PCAOB is unable to inspect or investigate completely auditors located in China for two consecutive years. | There can be no assurance that we would not be identified as a Commission-Identified Issuer for any future fiscal year, and if we were so identified for two consecutive years, we would become subject to the prohibition on trading under the HFCAA. |
| 4 | The company's holding company structure and PRC regulations on currency conversion and dividend remittance may limit its ability to fund operations outside the Chinese mainland; restricted amounts totaled RMB78.2 billion as of December 31, 2025. | The amounts restricted include the paid-in capital and the statutory reserve funds of our PRC subsidiaries and the net assets of the consolidated variable interest entities in which we have no legal ownership, totaling RMB67.6 billion, RMB71.5 billion and RMB78.2 billion (US$11.2 billion) as of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt includes short-term debts of CNY 8.0B, unsecured senior notes of CNY 24.3B and long-term debts of CNY 41.7B, against cash and cash equivalents of CNY 137.5B and total shareholders' equity of CNY 293.8B.

Liquidity: As of December 31, 2025, the company had revolving lines of credit for an aggregate amount of RMB304.0 billion (US$43.5 billion) from several commercial banks, of which RMB243.1 billion (US$34.8 billion) was unused. Management believes it has sufficient working capital for present requirements and for at least the next 12 months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating CNY 19.0B, investing CNY 41.8B, financing CNY -26.7B.

Working capital: Current assets CNY 374.4B vs. current liabilities CNY 306.1B (current ratio 1.22x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: CNY 386.7B vs. CNY 299.5B (1.29x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- The unsecured senior notes contain covenants including, among others, limitation on liens, and restriction on consolidation, merger and sale of all or substantially all of our assets; the company states it is in compliance with all the covenants.
- The 2029 Notes will mature on June 1, 2029, unless earlier redeemed, repurchased or converted; holders may require repurchase on June 1, 2027 or in the event of certain fundamental changes.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| VIE consolidation and contractual arrangements | The company consolidates the VIEs under U.S. GAAP as primary beneficiary; as of December 31, 2025, total VIE assets were CNY 64.5B and total VIE liabilities were CNY 58.1B, and VIE net income was CNY 8.0B. |
| Convenience translation | US$ figures throughout the filing are convenience translations calculated at a single rate, not actual conversions. |
| Reclassifications | Certain prior-year amounts were reclassified to conform to current-year presentation, with no impact on net income, shareholders' equity, or cash flows. |
| Segment reporting change | The company reports three reportable segments (JD Retail, JD Logistics and New Businesses) from the first quarter of 2024, with prior periods retrospectively recast. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Sea Limited reported FY2025 revenue of US$22.9B, up 36.4% YoY, with net income of US$1.6B and diluted EPS of $2.52.

Revenue growth accelerated to 36.4% and net income more than tripled, while the digital financial services segment grew to 16.6% of total revenue and the company settled two class action lawsuits.

- Total revenue rose 36.4% to US$22.9B, driven by e-commerce service revenue up 33.9% to US$14.5B and digital financial services revenue up 60.1% to US$3.8B.
- Net income increased to US$1.6B from US$447.8M in 2024, with operating margin expanding to 8.6% from 3.9%.
- Operating cash flow was US$5.0B, up from US$3.3B, and free cash flow (OCF less capex) was US$4.5B, up from US$3.0B.
- The company settled two securities class actions for a combined US$86M and has no present plan to pay cash dividends.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenue | US$22,938,469 thousand | US$16,819,866 thousand | +36.4% | Growth driven by e-commerce service revenue up 33.9% and digital financial services revenue up 60.1%. |
| Gross profit | US$10,243,737 thousand | US$7,205,088 thousand | +42.2% | Gross margin improved to 44.7% from 42.8%, primarily due to a shift in gross profit mix toward higher-margin digital financial services. |
| Operating income | US$1,985,306 thousand | US$662,152 thousand | +199.8% | Operating margin expanded to 8.6% from 3.9%, driven by revenue growth and operating leverage. |
| Net income | US$1,610,894 thousand | US$447,827 thousand | +259.7% | Net income increased primarily due to higher operating income and lower net investment loss. |
| EPS (Basic) | $2.65 | $0.77 | +244.2% | Basic EPS increased in line with net income growth. |
| EPS (Diluted) | $2.52 | $0.74 | +240.5% | Diluted EPS increased in line with net income growth. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of US$1,985.3M included a US$121.3M other operating income (down 32.8% YoY) and a US$1,372.6M provision for credit losses (up 76.7% YoY). Non-operating items included a US$43.4M net investment loss (down from US$250.2M in 2024) and a US$21.0M net gain on debt extinguishment. The 2024 period included one-time expenses related to the settlement of two securities class actions.

Operating cash flow was 3.2x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $4.5B.

**Red flag:** Provision for credit losses increased 76.7% to US$1.4B, outpacing revenue growth of 36.4%, as loans receivable grew 91.4% to US$8.0B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — share repurchases $14.0M; capital expenditures $513.8M (prior $318.2M).

Capital allocation prioritized growth investments in e-commerce and digital financial services, with sales and marketing expenses up 29.4% and research and development expenses stable. The company repurchased US$14.0M of shares, its first such repurchase, and has no present plan to pay cash dividends.

Return on equity was 12.6% (prior 5.3%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 5.4% (prior 2.0%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- Share repurchases of US$14.0M in 2025, compared to none in 2024.

## Forward Signals

No specific financial guidance was provided in the filing. Management discusses historical results and factors affecting future results without giving quantitative outlook.

**Known trends**
- Revenue growth may be affected by seasonality, promotional activities, and macro-economic conditions.
- Provision for credit losses could increase with the growth of lending activity or if the credit environment worsens.

**Subsequent events**
- On August 7, 2025, the court issued an order and final judgment approving the US$40 million class action settlement.
- On July 11, 2025, the court issued an order and final judgment approving the US$46 million class action settlement.

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Credit risk from digital financial services lending, with provision for credit losses up 76.7% to US$1.4B as loans receivable grew 91.4% to US$8.0B. | Our provision for credit losses increased by 76.7% from US$776.9 million in 2024 to US$1.4 billion in 2025, primarily driven by an increase in lending activity during the year, in line with the growth in our loan book over the year. |
| 2 | Regulatory and licensing risks across multiple jurisdictions, including digital financial services, e-commerce, and gaming. | We are subject to a variety of regulations, including those relating to game operations, game ratings, e-commerce, social networking, internet applications or content services, digital platforms, marketing, advertising, AI technology and services, privacy, personal information, data use, data transfer, data processing, data localization, data storage, data retention and data protection, cybersecurity, livestreaming and video services, antitrust or competition laws, employment and labor laws, national language requirements, intellectual property, virtual items, user-generated content, loot boxes, national security, nationalization, content restrictions, platform regulations, sale of regulated or prohibited items, protection of minors, data of minors, consumer protection, pricing, product safety and product liability, logistics or postal operations, warehouse or fulfillment operations, prevention of money laundering and financing criminal activity and terrorism, anti-bribery and anti-corruption regulation, economic or other trade prohibitions or sanctions, electronic contracts and other communications, digital financial services regulation, payment services regulation, lending regulation, foreign investment and currency control regulation and regulations related to logistics, insurance, and banking. |
| 3 | Geopolitical tensions, including those surrounding the Taiwan Strait, could disrupt operations in Taiwan. | In addition, there have been and remain tensions surrounding the Taiwan Strait. If such tension intensifies, our business in Taiwan may not be able to operate normally or at all. |
| 4 | Reliance on structural arrangements (VIEs) to establish control over certain entities, which may be challenged by government authorities. | We rely on structural arrangements to establish control over certain entities and government authorities may determine that these arrangements do not comply with existing laws and regulations. We are also subject to other risks relating to such structural arrangements. |
| 5 | Intellectual property risks, including prior identification of Shopee as a 'notorious market' by the U.S. Trade Representative. | The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative had previously identified the Shopee platform in several of our markets as “notorious markets”in its annual Review of Notorious Markets for Counterfeiting and Piracy. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-Commerce (Shopee) | $16.6B |  | +33.4% | Revenue growth driven by GMV growth of 26.8% to US$127.4B and improved monetization rate to 11.4% of GMV. |
| Monee | $3.8B |  | +60.1% | Revenue growth driven by credit business expansion, with loans receivable growing 91.4% to US$8.0B. |
| Digital Entertainment (Garena) | $2.4B |  | +26.1% | Revenue increase primarily due to higher active user base and paying user penetration, with average Game QAUs up 5.7% and QPUs up 23.9%. |
| Other Services | $173.5M |  | +37.3% | Other services are a combination of multiple business activities that do not meet the quantitative threshold to qualify as reportable segments. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt not disclosed. Shareholders' equity increased to US$12.5B from US$8.4B. Cash and equivalents of US$4.2B against total assets of US$29.4B.

Liquidity: Cash and equivalents of US$4.2B, up from US$2.4B. Operating cash flow of US$5.0B provides liquidity.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $5.0B, investing $-4.4B, financing $1.6B.

Working capital: Current assets $23.2B vs. current liabilities $14.7B (current ratio 1.58x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: $16.9B vs. $11.3B (1.49x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Not disclosed

| Dividend policy | No present plan to pay cash dividends; intends to retain earnings for business expansion. |

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Sea Limited's FY2025 revenue rose 36.4% to US$22.9B and net income reached US$1.6B, with operating income of US$2.0B.

Revenue growth accelerated to 36.4% and net income more than tripled, driven by e-commerce GMV growth, digital financial services lending expansion, and a rebound in digital entertainment revenue.

- Total revenue increased 36.4% to US$22.9B in 2025 from US$16.8B in 2024, with gross profit up 42.2% to US$10.2B.
- Net income was US$1.6B in 2025, compared to US$447.8M in 2024, and operating income was US$2.0B versus US$662.2M.
- Diluted EPS was US$2.52 in 2025, up from US$0.74 in 2024.
- The company operates three reportable segments—E-commerce (Shopee), Digital Financial Services (Monee), and Digital Entertainment (Garena)—and reports in U.S. dollars.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Total revenue | US$22,938,469 thousand | US$16,819,866 thousand | +36.4% | Growth driven by e-commerce GMV growth, digital financial services lending expansion, and digital entertainment user base increase. |
| Gross profit | US$10,243,737 thousand | US$7,205,088 thousand | +42.2% | Gross margin improved to 44.7% from 42.8%, primarily due to a shift in gross profit mix toward higher-margin digital financial services. |
| Operating income | US$1,985,306 thousand | US$662,152 thousand | +199.8% | Operating margin expanded to 8.7% from 3.9%, driven by revenue growth and operating leverage. |
| Net income | US$1,610,894 thousand | US$447,827 thousand | +259.7% | Net income increased primarily due to higher operating income and lower net investment loss. |
| Diluted EPS | US$2.52 | US$0.74 | +240.5% | EPS growth reflects higher net income and share count changes. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income of US$2.0B was driven by core operations, with non-operating income of US$295.6M including interest income, net investment loss, and foreign exchange gains. The company recorded no goodwill impairment in 2025, compared to US$117.9M in 2023. Provision for credit losses increased 76.7% to US$1.4B, reflecting lending growth.

Operating cash flow was 3.2x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $4.5B.

**Red flag:** Provision for credit losses increased 76.7% to US$1.4B, outpacing revenue growth, tied to a 91.4% increase in loans receivable to US$8.0B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — share repurchases $14.0M; capital expenditures $513.8M (prior $318.2M).

Capital allocation prioritized growth investments, with significant funding directed toward e-commerce logistics, digital financial services lending, and marketing. The company does not plan to pay cash dividends in the foreseeable future, retaining funds to operate and expand the business.

Return on equity was 12.6% (prior 5.3%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 5.4% (prior 2.0%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

- The company repurchased US$14.0M of shares in 2025, compared to none in 2024.

## Forward Signals

No specific financial guidance was provided in the filing. Management discusses historical results and factors affecting future results but does not give quantitative outlook.

**Known trends**
- Revenue growth may be affected by seasonality, promotional activities, and macroeconomic conditions.
- Digital entertainment revenue recognition under U.S. GAAP defers bookings, causing timing differences between cash flow and reported revenue.

**Subsequent events**
- On August 7, 2025, the court issued an order and final judgment approving the US$40 million class action settlement.
- On July 11, 2025, the court issued an order and final judgment approving the US$46 million class action settlement.

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Credit risk from digital financial services lending, with provision for credit losses increasing 76.7% to US$1.4B and loans receivable growing 91.4% to US$8.0B. | Our provision for credit losses increased by 76.7% from US$776.9 million in 2024 to US$1.4 billion in 2025, primarily driven by an increase in lending activity during the year, in line with the growth in our loan book over the year. |
| 2 | Dependence on a limited number of online games for digital entertainment revenue and gross profit. | We derive a significant portion of digital entertainment revenue and gross profit from a limited number of online games. |
| 3 | Foreign exchange rate fluctuations may adversely affect reported results, as revenue is earned in local currencies while reporting in U.S. dollars. | Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates may adversely affect our operational and financial results, which we report in U.S. dollars. |

## Segments

| Monee | $3.8B |  | +60.1% | Revenue growth driven by credit business expansion, with loans receivable growing 91.4% to US$8.0B. |
| Digital Entertainment (Garena) | $2.4B |  | +26.1% | Revenue increase primarily due to higher active user base and paying user penetration, with average Game QAUs up 5.7% and QPUs up 23.9%. |
| Other Services | $173.5M |  | +37.3% | Other services are a combination of multiple business activities that do not meet the quantitative threshold to qualify as reportable segments. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total assets increased to US$29.4B from US$22.6B, and shareholders' equity rose to US$12.5B from US$8.4B. Cash and equivalents were US$4.2B, up from US$2.4B.

## The Print

Sea Limited's FY2025 revenue reached US$22.9B (up 36.4% YoY) with net income of US$1.6B, as operating income more than doubled to US$2.0B.

The filing shows a shift to higher profitability across all three segments, with e-commerce turning to positive operating segment income of US$581.1M from a loss of US$139.4M in 2024, and digital financial services operating income rising to US$972.7M.

- Total revenue grew 36.4% YoY to US$22.9B, driven by e-commerce service revenue up 33.9% to US$14.5B and digital financial services revenue up 60.1% to US$3.8B.
- Net income rose to US$1.6B from US$447.8M in 2024, with operating margin expanding to 8.6% from 3.9%.
- Diluted EPS increased to US$2.52 from US$0.74, while operating cash flow grew to US$5.0B from US$3.3B.
- Loans receivable grew 91.4% to US$8.0B, driving provision for credit losses up 76.7% to US$1.4B.

## Results That Matter

| Basic EPS | US$2.65 | US$0.77 | +244.2% | Basic EPS increased in line with net income growth. |

Operating income of US$1,985.3M included a net gain on debt extinguishment of US$21.0M and a foreign exchange gain of US$20.5M, while net investment loss was US$43.4M. The prior year included a net investment loss of US$250.2M and a net gain on debt extinguishment of US$42.6M. No goodwill impairment was recorded in 2025 or 2024, compared to US$117.9M in 2023.

Operating cash flow was 3.2x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $4.5B.

**Red flag:** Provision for credit losses increased 76.7% to US$1.4B, driven by a 91.4% increase in loans receivable to US$8.0B, indicating credit risk concentration in the growing loan book.

- The company expects competition to intensify in its digital financial services business as existing and new competitors introduce new services or enhance existing services.
- The company notes that changes in cash flow generated from games may not match revenue trends due to revenue recognition policies under U.S. GAAP, which require proceeds from sales of in-game virtual items to be recorded as deferred revenue and recognized over a period of time.

payload.executive_summary:
## The Print

Novo Nordisk reported FY2025 revenue of DKK 309.1B (up 6.4% YoY) and net income of DKK 102.4B, with operating margin compressing to 41.3% from 44.2%.

Operating margin contracted 290bps YoY despite revenue growth, driven by pricing pressure and higher rebates in the U.S. Obesity and Diabetes care segment.

- Revenue grew 6.4% to DKK 309.1B, but operating income declined 0.5% to DKK 127.7B as gross margin fell 370bps to 81.0%.
- Net income rose 1.4% to DKK 102.4B; diluted EPS increased to DKK 23.03 from DKK 22.63.
- Operating cash flow was DKK 119.1B, down from DKK 121.0B; investing outflow narrowed to DKK 79.2B from DKK 128.9B.
- The company will recognize USD 4.2B of previously constrained 340B revenue in Q1 2026 following a final HRSA decision.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | DKK 309,064,000,000 | DKK 290,403,000,000 | +6.4% | Growth driven by Obesity and Diabetes care segment, which comprises more than 90% of sales. |
| Gross Profit | DKK 250,276,000,000 | DKK 245,881,000,000 | +1.8% | Gross margin declined to 81.0% from 84.7%, reflecting pricing pressure and higher rebates. |
| Operating Income | DKK 127,658,000,000 | DKK 128,339,000,000 | −0.5% | Operating margin contracted to 41.3% from 44.2% as pricing pressure and increased rebates offset revenue growth. |
| Net Income | DKK 102,434,000,000 | DKK 100,988,000,000 | +1.4% | Net margin declined to 33.1% from 34.8%. |
| EPS (Basic) | DKK 23.06 | DKK 22.67 | +1.7% | Basic EPS increased despite margin compression. |
| EPS (Diluted) | DKK 23.03 | DKK 22.63 | +1.8% | Diluted EPS increased on higher net income and share count changes. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Operating income declined 0.5% YoY to DKK 127.7B, while net income rose 1.4% to DKK 102.4B, indicating non-operating items contributed positively. The filing discloses a USD 4.2B provision for 340B statutory discounts included in sales deductions and product returns as of December 31, 2025, which will be recognized as revenue in Q1 2026.

Operating cash flow was 1.2x net income (cash conversion).

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid DKK 51.8B (prior DKK 44.1B), share repurchases DKK 1.4B (prior DKK 20.2B).

Dividends paid increased to DKK 51.8B from DKK 44.1B, while share repurchases declined sharply to DKK 1.4B from DKK 20.2B. Investing cash outflow narrowed to DKK 79.2B from DKK 128.9B. The allocation shifted toward shareholder dividends and away from buybacks and investing activities.

Return on equity was 52.8% (prior 70.4%) (period net income / period-end equity, not annualized); return on assets 18.9% (prior 21.7%) (period net income / period-end assets, not annualized).

## Forward Signals

The filing states that for 2026, continued pricing pressure within Obesity and Diabetes Care is expected. No specific revenue or earnings guidance figures are provided in the excerpts.

**Known trends**
- Pricing pressure is expected to continue in the future, driven by increasing rebates in the commercial segment, payer consolidation, increasing exposure to high rebate channels such as Medicare and Medicaid, increasing sales in direct-to-patient cash channel as well as increasing competition.
- Research and development cost to sales ratio is expected to gradually increase, with current expenditure level of around 15-17% of sales.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 20, 2026, the HRSA decision became final and effective, and Novo Nordisk determined it is highly probable that inclusion of revenue relating to 340B Drug Pricing Program claims previously constrained will not result in a significant reversal; the Company will recognize USD 4.2B of revenue in Q1 2026.

> "For 2026, continued pricing pressure within Obesity and Diabetes Care is expected." — Novo Nordisk Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | US sales rebates, including provisions related to the 340B Drug Pricing Program, involve significant measurement uncertainty and judgment. | We identified the US sales rebates, including provisions related to the 340B Drug Pricing Program, as a critical audit matter due to the significant measurement uncertainty involved in developing these provisions |
| 2 | Cybersecurity breaches could disrupt IT systems and lead to loss of intellectual property, confidential information, or personal data. | disruption as a result of cybersecurity breaches could negatively impact the Company’s business and operations or financial results |
| 3 | Climate change and water scarcity risks could impact production facilities and supply chain. | our production facilities in North Carolina, United States are exposed to extreme weather conditions such as tornadoes and hurricanes |
| 4 | Pricing pressure from US payers demanding higher rebates, particularly in insulin and increasingly in GLP-1 category. | US payers continue to leverage their size and control to demand higher rebates, particularly in the insulin segment, but increasingly in the GLP-1 category, as well. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total assets increased to DKK 542.9B from DKK 465.6B; shareholders' equity rose to DKK 194.0B from DKK 143.5B. Cash and equivalents were DKK 26.5B. Debt details not disclosed in excerpts.

Liquidity: Cash and equivalents of DKK 26.5B; the company believes its financial resources are sufficient to meet requirements for at least the next 12 months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating DKK 119.1B, investing DKK -79.2B, financing DKK -28.4B.

Working capital: Current assets DKK 172.5B vs. current liabilities DKK 215.7B (current ratio 0.80x). Prior reported balance sheet as of 2024-12-31: DKK 161.8B vs. DKK 217.6B (0.74x).
